# 昇腾训练 NPU out of memory 的排查与显存优化

## 0. 证据来源（本次实际取得）

| 类型 | 来源 | URL |
|---|---|---|
| 官方（直接正文，完整参数表+约束+版本+示例） | Ascend/pytorch 仓库《PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF》 | https://github.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/master/docs/zh/api/environment_variable/memory_management/PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF.md |
| 官方（接口清单表） | 昇腾社区《Memory management API》TorchNPU 6.0.RC3 | https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/Pytorch/60RC3/apiref/apilist/ptaoplist_000873.html |
| 官方（论坛帖，仅有提问片段、无解决方案正文） | 昇腾论坛 baichuan2-7b OOM 帖 | https://www.hiascend.com/dev/forum/thread-0261157187867914417-1-1.html |
| 官方（PyTorch checkpoint 文档，梯度检查点的权威来源） | PyTorch 2.14 torch.utils.checkpoint | https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/checkpoint.html |
| 第三方（AI 风格排障文，无引用） | CSDN《昇腾NPU调试排障手册》2026-05-24 | https://hwcomputing.csdn.net/6a124934662f9a54cb76a74a.html |
| 第三方（运维排障文，无引用） | 顶有教育科技《昇腾NPU运维故障排查实战》2026-07-22 | https://www.zdyedu.cn/blog/ascend-npu-ops-troubleshooting-guide/ |

官方在检索中另出现（未抓取，内容与上表第 1 行同源）：https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/Pytorch/2610/apiref/ENV/docs/zh/environment_variable_reference/PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF.md

---

## 1. 先定性：是"真超"、碎片，还是别的进程占用

- 昇腾 OOM 典型报错：`RuntimeError: NPU out of memory. Tried to allocate XXX MiB (NPU n; ... bytes total capacity; ... already allocated)`。
- 官方论坛案例（baichuan2-7b）出现过 `Tried to allocate 66.00 MiB (NPU 1; 0 bytes total capacity; 6.02 GiB already allocated)`，且用户用 `npu-smi info` 看到显存并非 0。**提示：`total capacity` 字段异常时不要据它下结论，以 `npu-smi` 和 torch_npu 统计为准。**
- 查卡上真实占用与进程：
```bash
npu-smi info                 # 总览
npu-smi info -t memory       # HBM 已用/总量
npu-smi info -t proc         # 各进程占用
npu-smi info -i 0 -t common  # AICore 利用率等
```
（上述子命令取自第三方排障文，属常规 `npu-smi` 用法；本次未在官方正文逐条核实，标记**未核实**。）

## 2. 用 torch_npu 内存接口定位峰值与碎片

官方《Memory management API》确认存在（均为 beta，语义对齐 `torch.cuda`）：
`torch_npu.npu.memory_allocated / max_memory_allocated / memory_reserved / max_memory_reserved / memory_cached / max_memory_cached / memory_summary / memory_stats / memory_stats_as_nested_dict / memory_snapshot / empty_cache / reset_peak_memory_stats / reset_max_memory_allocated / reset_max_memory_cached / reset_accumulated_memory_stats / set_per_process_memory_fraction`。

```python
import torch, torch_npu
to_gb = lambda b: f"{b/1024**3:.2f} GB"
print("allocated", to_gb(torch.npu.memory_allocated()))
print("reserved ", to_gb(torch.npu.memory_reserved()))
print("peak     ", to_gb(torch.npu.max_memory_allocated()))
print(torch.npu.memory_summary())          # 分块/分池统计
torch.npu.empty_cache()                    # 只回收 reserved 中未复用块，不降 allocated
torch.npu.reset_peak_memory_stats()        # 重置峰值，便于分段定位
```
判读：若 `reserved` 远大于 `allocated`，说明缓存分配器持有大量未复用块（碎片/回收不及时），优先走第 3 节分配器参数；若 `allocated` 本身逼近卡容量，则需减激活（第 4 节）。

## 3. 显存碎片 / 分配器优化：PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF（官方正文）

语法 `键:值,键:值`（无空格）。**与碎片最相关的键**：

| 参数 | 作用 | 取值/默认 | 关键约束 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_split_size_mb` | 大于该值的块不再切分，**减少碎片**；官方注明用于"因 OOM 中断且出现大量非活动切分块"的场景 | 默认无限大，单位 MB，最小设置值需 >20MB | 非默认时必须令 `expandable_segments:False` |
| `garbage_collection_threshold` | 主动回收未使用 NPU 内存块（超阈值即回收，优先释放最早申请/久未复用块） | `(0.0,1.0)`，默认关闭 | 需与"内存因子"（`set_per_process_memory_fraction`）配合；非默认时 `expandable_segments` 必须 False |
| `expandable_segments` | 开启内存池扩展段（虚拟内存），更好应对尺寸频繁变化 | 默认 `False` | 需 Ascend HDK ≥ 23.0.0 |
| `roundup_power2_divisions` | 分配尺寸向上舍入到 2 的幂分段，提升块复用率 | 单值或 `[256:1,512:2,1024:4,>:8]` 形式 | — |
| `large_segment_size_mb` | 大块内存池段粒度 | >10，默认 20；单位 MB | TorchNPU ≥26.1.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.11.0；与 `max_split_size_mb` 同配需 ≥ 后者；官方建议在内存极限场景慎调大（会增碎片） |
| `segment_size_mb` | 虚拟内存下物理申请粒度 | 20~512，默认 20 | 仅 `expandable_segments=True` 生效；**已废弃**，改用 `large_segment_size_mb` |
| `page_size` | 1GB 大页，降低页表/TLB 压力 | 仅支持 1GB | 需 HDK ≥25.0.RC1 且 CANN 商用 ≥8.1.RC1，仅 Atlas A2/A3 |
| `base_addr_aligned_kb` | 基地址对齐 | 0~16，默认 16 | 仅 `expandable_segments=True` 生效 |
| `max_non_split_rounding_mb` | 结合 `max_split_size_mb` 控制块大小与复用 | 默认 20MB | — |
| `per_process_memory_fraction` | 限制单进程可用显存比例，**多进程共享一卡时防其他进程 OOM** | `[0.0,1.0]`，默认 1.0 | TorchNPU ≥26.1.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.10.0 |
| `throw_on_npumalloc_oom` | OOM 前**预防式拒绝**申请，跳过重试，报 `OutOfMemoryError` | `True/False`，默认 False | TorchNPU ≥26.2.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.13.0；当 `per_process_memory_fraction<1.0` 时不生效；被拒次数记入 `torch_npu.npu.memory_stats()['num_oom_rejections']` |
| `multi_stream_lazy_reclaim` | 多流下延迟 Events 查询，降 Host 开销 | 默认 False | TorchNPU >7.3.0 |
| `release_lock_on_npumalloc` | 分配时释放部分锁，缓解 Host 计算压力 | 默认 False | 自定义显存管理可能不兼容，谨慎 |

**官方配置示例（可直接抄）**：
```bash
# 碎片/OOM 场景，最常用
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6

# 虚拟内存扩展段
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True,base_addr_aligned_kb:16

# 2 的幂分段复用
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF="roundup_power2_divisions:[256:1,512:2,1024:4,>:8]"

# 多进程共享一卡，限制本进程显存比例
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=per_process_memory_fraction:0.5

# OOM 前预防式拒绝，便于尽早暴露并定位
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=throw_on_npumalloc_oom:True

# 大页
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=page_size:1g
```
**重要互斥**：`max_split_size_mb` 或 `garbage_collection_threshold` 任一非默认时，`expandable_segments` 必须为 `False`（两条路线二选一）。另：TorchNPU 26.2.0 + PyTorch 2.10.0 起支持 `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`（参数与 `PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF` 完全相同，二者同时配置会报错退出，官方建议优先 `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`）。

## 4. 梯度检查点（activation checkpointing，以计算换显存）

PyTorch 官方接口（框架标准，torch_npu 上沿用；**本次未找到昇腾官方对其单列的版本要求，标记未核实**）：
```python
from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint, checkpoint_sequential

# 方式一：直接调用（官方推荐显式传 use_reentrant=False，2.9 起必须显式传）
out = checkpoint(block_fn, x, use_reentrant=False)

# 方式二：顺序模型按段 checkpoint
model = nn.Sequential(...)
out = checkpoint_sequential(model, segments=4, input=x, use_reentrant=False)
```
- 机制（官方原文）：前向中间张量不再保留到反向，反向时重新调用 `function` 重算；`args` 中显式传入的张量仍会被保存。因此**只对需要在反向用到、且可重算的部分做 checkpoint**。
- 默认 `preserve_rng_state=True`，保证含 dropout 等随机算子的 checkpoint pass 与未 checkpoint 时一致；若不需此一致性可设 `False` 省内存（有梯度不正确风险）。
- 非重入版（`use_reentrant=False`）支持 `torch.autograd.grad`、kwargs 输入、嵌套结构张量、`debug`/`determinism_check` 等；重入版（`True`）不记录前向 autograd 图、仅支持不带 inputs 的 `backward()`、要求至少一个输入/输出 `requires_grad=True`。官方推荐 `use_reentrant=False`。
- 结合第 2 节：开启后 `max_memory_allocated()` 应明显下降；若未降，通常是 checkpoint 边界包错（把不该保存的张量留在了 `args` 里）。
- HuggingFace 模型常用 `model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()`（**本次未取到官方来源，标记未核实**）。

## 5. 其他配套手段（概念性，非强制代码）

- 混合精度：`torch.npu.amp.autocast` + GradScaler（**函数名未在本次官方检索中核实**）。
- 减小 `batch_size` / `seq_len`，用梯度累积模拟大 batch。
- 及时 `del` 中间张量、loss 计算前 `detach`、避免保留无用计算图。
- 周期调用 `torch.npu.empty_cache()`（第三方排障文建议；官方文档确认该接口存在）。
- 多进程共卡时用 `per_process_memory_fraction` 限流，避免相互 OOM。

## 6. 版本适用关系（供定版参考，均出自官方第 1 条来源）

- `PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF`：控制缓存分配器；`PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF` 需 TorchNPU ≥26.2.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.10.0。
- `expandable_segments`：需 Ascend HDK ≥23.0.0；且与 `max_split_size_mb`/`garbage_collection_threshold` 互斥。
- `page_size`：HDK ≥25.0.RC1、CANN 商用 ≥8.1.RC1，仅 Atlas A2/A3 训练产品。
- `large_segment_size_mb`：TorchNPU ≥26.1.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.11.0。
- `per_process_memory_fraction`：TorchNPU ≥26.1.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.10.0。
- `throw_on_npumalloc_oom`、`pinned_max_round_threshold_mb`、`pinned_max_cached_size_mb`：TorchNPU ≥26.2.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.13.0。
- `pin_memory_expandable_segments`：TorchNPU ≥7.3.0、HDK ≥25.5.0、CANN 商用 ≥8.5.0；`pinned_mem_register`：TorchNPU ≥26.0.0、HDK ≥26.0.RC1、CANN 商用 ≥8.5.0；二者不可同配。
- `multi_stream_lazy_reclaim`：TorchNPU >7.3.0；`pinned_use_background_threads`：TorchNPU ≥26.0.0 且 PyTorch ≥2.8.0。
- `<Ascend 950DT>` 仅支持 `expandable_segments`、`pinned_use_background_threads`、`pin_memory_expandable_segments`、`pinned_mem_register` 四个参数。

## 7. 无法核实 / 未确定处

1. 第三方排障文提出的 `export ASCEND_RT_MEMORY_REUSE=1` 缓解碎片 —— **官方第 1 条来源中无此键，未核实，可能过时**；官方碎片手段是 `max_split_size_mb` / `garbage_collection_threshold` / `roundup_power2_divisions`。
2. 第三方给出的 6 位错误码分类表（100000=内存、200000=HCCL 等）及 `EI9999 / ASCEND_OOM` 文本 —— **未核实**。
3. `torch.npu.memory._record_memory_history()` / `_dump_snapshot()` —— 第三方提及，**本次官方接口表中未见该私有接口，未核实**。
4. 第三方将 `max_split_size_mb:128` 描述为"关闭 ATB 算子显存预分配" —— 与官方定义（内存块切分上限）**不一致，判定为第三方说法有误**。
5. 梯度检查点在昇腾侧的专门版本要求 —— 未找到官方 Ascend 文档单列，本文按 PyTorch 标准接口给出，**Ascend 适配的额外要求未核实**。

## 一、先验知识：CUDA OOM 的排查路径

**1) 确认现象与占用主体**
- `nvidia-smi`（可配 `watch -n1 nvidia-smi`）查看每卡占用、是否有其他进程占显存。
- 区分 OOM 发生在 forward / backward / optimizer.step：activation（为 backward 保存）通常占大头，Adam 优化器状态约为参数量 2×。
- PyTorch 侧接口（凭记忆）：`torch.cuda.memory_summary()`、`torch.cuda.memory_allocated()`、`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()`、`torch.cuda.memory_reserved()`、`torch.cuda.memory_snapshot()`。

**2) `max_split_size_mb`（缓存分配器）**
- 通过环境变量 `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` 设置，例如 `max_split_size_mb:512`。
- 我理解的机制：CUDA caching allocator 会把大块切分（split）以满足小块请求，长期运行造成碎片；限制“可被切分的最大块大小”，超过该值的块不再切分，从而缓解碎片。设得过小会保留更多不可用大块、反而抬高 reserved。
- 同一环境变量族还包含 `garbage_collection_threshold:<0~1>`、`expandable_segments:True` 等。

**3) `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`**
- 释放 caching allocator 中**未被任何张量占用**的缓存块，归还给 CUDA 供其他进程使用；**不会**释放仍被引用的张量。频繁调用会因反复 `cudaMalloc` 降低性能，宜在阶段切换（如训练→评估）时调用，而非每步调用。

**4) 梯度检查点（gradient checkpointing）**
- `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(fn, *args)`：backward 时重算 activation，用额外前向计算换显存。
- HuggingFace transformers：`model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()`，并需 `use_cache=False`。

**5) 其他常用手段**：AMP（`torch.cuda.amp.autocast` + `GradScaler`）、减小 batch 并用梯度累积、`optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)`、`del` 中间张量、FlashAttention / `scaled_dot_product_attention`、`torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction`、FSDP/ZeRO。

## 二、先验中的不确定处（需检索核实）
1. `max_split_size_mb` 的**精确语义与单位（MB）、默认值（是否 unlimited）**，以及官方是否仍推荐它、还是更推荐 `expandable_segments`。
2. `expandable_segments` 的**引入版本**，以及它与 `max_split_size_mb` 是否可/需同时设置。
3. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` 的完整合法键名与拼写；是否存在 `torch.cuda.memory._set_allocator_settings` 运行时设置接口及其版本。
4. `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` 的确切行为边界与签名。
5. HF `gradient_checkpointing_enable()` 与 `use_cache` 的配套约束细节。
6. 各接口的**版本适用关系**（M4/M9 关注）。

# Analysis of PyTorch CUDA Semantics Documentation

## Page Metadata

- **Visible Page Title:** "CUDA semantics — PyTorch 2.14 documentation"
- **Created On:** Jan 16, 2017
- **Last Updated On:** Jul 17, 2026

## Truncation Assessment

**The content appears COMPLETE for the requested sections.** The "Memory management" section fully includes its subsection "Optimizing memory usage with `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`" and the full list of accepted keys. However, note two important limitations relative to the user's request:

1. There is **no dedicated "Environment variables" section** as a standalone heading. Environment variables are discussed within other sections (Memory management, Asynchronous execution, Best practices, etc.). I extract all environment-variable-related content I can locate.
2. The document ends abruptly at the Table of Contents entry for "Best practices" (a TOC fragment), but this appears to be a normal artifact of the page's navigation structure rather than mid-section truncation. The substantive Memory management content is intact.

---

## Section: Memory Management (Verbatim Extract)

> PyTorch uses a caching memory allocator to speed up memory allocations. This allows fast memory deallocation without device synchronizations. However, the unused memory managed by the allocator will still show as if used in `nvidia-smi`. You can use `memory_allocated()` and `max_memory_allocated()` to monitor memory occupied by tensors, and use `memory_reserved()` and `max_memory_reserved()` to monitor the total amount of memory managed by the caching allocator. Calling `empty_cache()` releases all **unused** cached memory from PyTorch so that those can be used by other GPU applications. However, the occupied GPU memory by tensors will not be freed so it can not increase the amount of GPU memory available for PyTorch.
>
> To better understand how CUDA memory is being used over time, [Understanding CUDA Memory Usage](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/torch_cuda_memory.html#torch-cuda-memory) describes tools for capturing and visualizing traces of memory use.
>
> For more advanced users, we offer more comprehensive memory benchmarking via `memory_stats()`. We also offer the capability to capture a complete snapshot of the memory allocator state via `memory_snapshot()`, which can help you understand the underlying allocation patterns produced by your code.

### Key points on `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`

- It **releases all UNUSED cached memory** from PyTorch so it can be used by other GPU applications.
- It **does NOT free GPU memory occupied by tensors**, so it **cannot increase the amount of GPU memory available** for PyTorch.

### Subsection: Optimizing memory usage with `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`

> Use of a caching allocator can interfere with memory checking tools such as `cuda-memcheck`. To debug memory errors using `cuda-memcheck`, set `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` in your environment to disable caching.
>
> The behavior of the caching allocator can be controlled via the environment variable `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` is its alias and is provided only for backward compatibility. The format is `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=<option>:<value>,<option2>:<value2>...` Available options:

#### Accepted keys (verbatim descriptions):

- **`backend`** — "allows selecting the underlying allocator implementation. Currently, valid options are `native`, which uses PyTorch's native implementation, and `cudaMallocAsync`, which uses [CUDA's built-in asynchronous allocator]. `cudaMallocAsync` requires CUDA 11.4 or newer. The default is `native`. `backend` applies to all devices used by the process, and can't be specified on a per-device basis."

- **`large_segment_size_mb`** — "the native allocator uses small and large blocks to manage allocated memory. This setting is used to configure the size of the large block. The default value is 20 MB."

- **`max_split_size_mb`** — "prevents the native allocator from splitting blocks larger than this size (in MB). This can reduce fragmentation and may allow some borderline workloads to complete without running out of memory. Performance cost can range from 'zero' to 'substantial' depending on allocation patterns. Default value is unlimited, i.e. all blocks can be split. The `memory_stats()` and `memory_summary()` methods are useful for tuning. This option should be used as a last resort for a workload that is aborting due to 'out of memory' and showing a large amount of inactive split blocks. `max_split_size_mb` is only meaningful with `backend:native`. With `backend:cudaMallocAsync`, `max_split_size_mb` is ignored."

- **`roundup_power2_divisions`** — "helps with rounding the requested allocation size to nearest power-2 division and making better use of the blocks. In the native CUDACachingAllocator, the sizes are rounded up in multiple of blocks size of 512, so this works fine for smaller sizes. However, this can be inefficient for large near-by allocations as each will go to different size of blocks and reuse of those blocks are minimized. This might create lots of unused blocks and will waste GPU memory capacity. This option enables the rounding of allocation size to nearest power-2 division. For example, if we need to round-up size of 1200 and if number of divisions is 4, the size 1200 lies between 1024 and 2048 and if we do 4 divisions between them, the values are 1024, 1280, 1536, and 1792. So, allocation size of 1200 will be rounded to 1280 as the nearest ceiling of power-2 division. Specify a single value to apply for all allocation sizes or specify an array of key value pairs to set power-2 division individually for each power of two interval. For example to set 1 division for all allocations under 256MB, 2 division for allocations between 256MB and 512MB, 4 divisions for allocations between 512MB and 1GB and 8 divisions for any larger allocations, set the knob value to: `[256:1,512:2,1024:4,>:8]`. `roundup_power2_divisions` is only meaningful with `backend:native`. With `backend:cudaMallocAsync`, `roundup_power2_divisions` is ignored."

- **`max_non_split_rounding_mb`** — "will allow non-split blocks for better reuse, eg, a 1024MB cached block can be reused for a 512MB allocation request. In the default case, we only allow up to 20MB of rounding of non-split blocks, so a 512MB block can only be served with between 512-532 MB size block. If we set the value of this option to 1024, it will allow 512-1536 MB size blocks to be used for a 512MB block which increases reuse of larger blocks. This will also help in reducing the stalls in avoiding expensive cudaMalloc calls."

- **`garbage_collection_threshold`** — "helps actively reclaiming unused GPU memory to avoid triggering expensive sync-and-reclaim-all operation (release_cached_blocks), which can be unfavorable to latency-critical GPU applications (e.g., servers). Upon setting this threshold (e.g., 0.8), the allocator will start reclaiming GPU memory blocks if the GPU memory capacity usage exceeds the threshold (i.e., 80% of the total memory allocated to the GPU application). The algorithm prefers to free old & unused blocks first to avoid freeing blocks that are actively being reused. The threshold value should be between greater than 0.0 and less than 1.0. The default value is set at 1.0.
  
  `garbage_collection_threshold` is only meaningful with `backend:native`. With `backend:cudaMallocAsync`, `garbage_collection_threshold` is ignored."

- **`expandable_segments`** (experimental, default: `False`) — "If set to `True`, this setting instructs the allocator to create CUDA allocations that can later be expanded to better handle cases where a job changing allocation sizes frequently, such as having a changing batch size. Normally for large (>2MB) allocations, the allocator calls cudaMalloc to get allocations that are the same size as what the user requests. In the future, parts of these allocations can be reused for other requests if they are free. This works well when the program makes many requests of exactly the same size or of sizes that even multiples of that size. Many deep learning models follow this behavior. However, one common exception is when the batch size changes slightly from one iteration to the next, e.g. in batched inference. When the program runs initially with batch size `N`, it will make allocations appropriate for that size. If in the future, it runs at size `N - 1`, the existing allocations will still be big enough. However, if it runs at size `N + 1`, then it will have to make new allocations that are slightly larger. Not all the tensors are the same size. Some might be `(N + 1)*A` and others `(N + 1)*A*B` where `A` and `B` are some non-batch dimensions in the model. Because the allocator reuses existing allocations when they are big enough, some number of `(N + 1)*A` allocations will actually fit in the already existing `N*B*A` segments, though not perfectly. As the model runs it will partially fill up all of these segments leaving unusable free slices of memory at the end of these segments. The allocator at some point will need to `cudaMalloc` a new `(N + 1)*A*B` segment. If there is not enough memory, there is now no way to recover the slices of memory that are free at the end of existing segments. With models 50+ layers deep, this pattern might repeat 50+ times creating many slivers.
  
  `expandable_segments` allows the allocator to create a segment initially and then expand its size later when more memory is needed. Instead of making one segment per allocation, it tries to make one segment (per stream) that grows as necessary. Now when the `N + 1` case runs, the allocations will tile nicely into the one large segment until it fills up. Then more memory is requested and appended to the end of the segment. This process does not create as many slivers of unusable memory, so it is more likely to succeed at finding this memory."

- **`pinned_use_cuda_host_register`** — "option is a boolean flag that determines whether to use the CUDA API's cudaHostRegister function for allocating pinned memory instead of the default cudaHostAlloc. When set to True, the memory is allocated using regular malloc and then pages are mapped to the memory before calling cudaHostRegister. This pre-mapping of pages helps reduce the lock time during the execution of cudaHostRegister."

- **`pinned_num_register_threads`** — "option is only valid when pinned_use_cuda_host_register is set to True. By default, one thread is used to map the pages. This option allows using more threads to parallelize the page mapping operations to reduce the overall allocation time of pinned memory. A good value for this option is 8 based on benchmarking results."

- **`pinned_use_background_threads`** — "option is a boolean flag to enable background thread for processing events. This avoids any slow path associated with querying/processing of events in the fast allocation path. This feature is disabled by default."

- **`pinned_reserve_segment_size_mb`** — "option is a size in MB to reserve for pinned memory segment. This allocates a large segment of pinned memory upfront and then uses to allocate small size requests. This helps reduce the number of expensive device library calls."

- **`pinned_max_round_threshold_mb`** — "option sets the maximum allocation size (in MB) that will be rounded up to the nearest power-of-2. Allocations larger than this threshold will use their exact requested size, which can reduce memory waste for large pinned memory allocations. For example, with a threshold of 128 MB, a 129 MB allocation will use 129 MB instead of being rounded to 256 MB. By default, this option is disabled. Allocations that exceed `pinned_max_cached_size_mb` are never rounded up, regardless of this setting, since rounding is only useful for cached blocks."

- **`pinned_max_cached_size_mb`** — "option sets the maximum block size (in MB) that will be cached in the free list for reuse. Blocks larger than this threshold will not be rounded up to power-of-2 and will be freed immediately when no longer in use, rather than being cached. This can help reduce peak memory usage for workloads with large pinned memory allocations that are used infrequently. By default, this option is disabled (all blocks are cached)."

- **`graph_capture_record_stream_reuse`** (experimental, default: `False`) — "If set to `True`, the CUDA caching allocator will attempt to reclaim device memory during CUDA Graph capture by using the graph topology (instead of CUDA events) to determine when a freed block is safe to reuse. This can reduce peak memory during long captures that free and reallocate buffers across multiple streams, especially when the capture DAG frequently reaches joined frontiers."

- **`per_process_memory_fraction`** — "option limits the amount of memory that can be allocated on all the CUDA devices to a specified fraction of the available memory. This is a value between 0 and 1. Attempting to allocate more memory will raise an out of memory error."

- **`throw_on_cudamalloc_oom`** (default: `False`) — "When set to `True`, the allocator will preemptively reject allocations that would exceed the `per_process_memory_fraction` limit by throwing an `OutOfMemoryError` instead of attempting the allocation through the driver, which could trigger a fatal GPU runtime abort (e.g., `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` on ROCm). The rejected allocation skips the retry chain and throws immediately, allowing the caller to catch the exception and handle it gracefully.
  
  Example configuration:
  
  ```
  PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=per_process_memory_fraction:0.95,throw_on_cudamalloc_oom:True
  ```
  
  This is particularly useful for inference serving, where a fatal GPU OOM would crash the server process. With this option, the serving framework can catch the `OutOfMemoryError` and reject the individual request while continuing to serve subsequent requests."

# Analysis: `torch.utils.checkpoint` — PyTorch 2.14 documentation

## Page Metadata

- **Page Title:** `torch.utils.checkpoint — PyTorch 2.14 documentation`
- **Documentation Version:** v2.14.0 (stable)
- **Created On:** Jun 16, 2025 | **Last Updated On:** Jul 27, 2026
- **Content Status:** The main documentation content appears **complete for the documented API surface**, but the page is heavily framed by navigation/sidebar boilerplate (version selector, full API tree). The core technical content — function signatures, descriptions, warnings, notes, and examples — is present and not truncated. No content after `set_device_states()` is missing (it ends with the footer).

---

## 1. Overview / Introductory Note on Checkpointing

> Checkpointing is implemented by rerunning a forward-pass segment for each checkpointed segment during backward propagation. This can cause persistent states like the RNG state to be more advanced than they would without checkpointing. By default, checkpointing includes logic to juggle the RNG state such that checkpointed passes making use of RNG (through dropout for example) have deterministic output as compared to non-checkpointed passes. The logic to stash and restore RNG states can incur a moderate performance hit depending on the runtime of checkpointed operations. If deterministic output compared to non-checkpointed passes is not required, supply `preserve_rng_state=False` to `checkpoint` or `checkpoint_sequential` to omit stashing and restoring the RNG state during each checkpoint.

**RNG / device state details:**
- The stashing logic saves and restores the RNG state for CPU and one other device type (inferred from Tensor arguments excluding CPU tensors via `_infer_device_type`) to the `run_fn`.
- If there are multiple devices, device state is saved only for devices of a single device type; the remaining devices are ignored → **may result in incorrect gradients if any checkpointed functions involve randomness.**
- If CUDA devices are detected, CUDA is prioritized; otherwise the first device encountered is selected.
- If there are no CPU tensors, the default device type state is saved/restored (default value is `cuda`, settable via `DefaultDeviceType`).
- **Caveat:** If you move tensors to a new device within `run_fn` (not in the set of [current device + devices of Tensor arguments]), deterministic output vs. non-checkpointed passes is **never guaranteed**.

**Decorator form note:** `checkpoint` may also be called without a function to produce a decorator:

```python
checkpointed_fn = checkpoint(use_reentrant=False, preserve_rng_state=False)(fn)
out = checkpointed_fn(*args, **kwargs)
```

---

## 2. `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint()`

### Signatures

**Direct-call form:**
```
torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
    *function: Callable[[...], _T],
    *args: Any,
    use_reentrant: bool | None = None,
    preserve_rng_state: bool = True,
    context_fn: Callable[[], Tuple[ContextManager, ContextManager]] = noop_context_fn,
    determinism_check: str = _DEFAULT_DETERMINISM_MODE,
    debug: bool = False,
    early_stop: bool = True,
    respect_saved_tensors_hooks: bool | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any
) → _T
```

**Decorator form:**
```
torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
    function: None = None,
    *,
    use_reentrant: bool | None = None,
    preserve_rng_state: bool = True,
    context_fn: Callable[[], Tuple[ContextManager, ContextManager]] = noop_context_fn,
    determinism_check: str = _DEFAULT_DETERMINISM_MODE,
    debug: bool = False,
    early_stop: bool = True,
    respect_saved_tensors_hooks: bool | None = None
) → Callable[[Callable[[_P], _T]], Callable[[_P], _T]]
```

### Description — "Compute for Memory" Trade

> Checkpoint a model or part of the model.
>
> **Activation checkpointing is a technique that trades compute for memory.** By default, tensors computed during the forward pass are kept alive until they are used in gradient computations in the backward pass. To reduce this memory usage, tensors produced in the passed `function` are not kept alive until the backward pass. Instead, any passed tensors in `args` are kept alive, and the unsaved tensors are recomputed by re-invoking `function` in the backward pass as needed for gradient computation. Activation checkpointing can be applied to any part of a model – this is sometimes described as "checkpointing" that part of the model.
>
> There are currently **two checkpointing implementations**, determined by the `use_reentrant` parameter. **It is recommended that you use `use_reentrant=False`.**

### Warnings

> **Warning:** If the `function` invocation during the backward pass differs from the forward pass, e.g., due to a global variable, the checkpointed version may not be equivalent, potentially causing an error being raised or leading to **silently incorrect gradients**.

> **Warning:** The `use_reentrant` parameter should be passed explicitly. **In version 2.9 we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed.** If you are using the `use_reentrant=True` variant, please refer to the note below for important considerations and potential limitations.

### Note — Differences Between `use_reentrant=True` and `use_reentrant=False`

1. **Recomputation stopping:** Non-reentrant checkpoint stops recomputation as soon as all needed intermediate activations have been recomputed (enabled by default; can be disabled with `set_checkpoint_early_stop()`). Reentrant checkpoint always recomputes `function` in its entirety during the backward pass.
2. **Autograd graph recording:** The reentrant variant does **not** record the autograd graph during the forward pass (runs forward under `torch.no_grad()`). The non-reentrant version **does** record the autograd graph, allowing backward on the graph within checkpointed regions.
3. **Backward API support:** The reentrant checkpoint only supports the `torch.autograd.backward()` API for the backward pass **without its `inputs` argument**. The non-reentrant version supports all ways of performing the backward pass.
4. **`requires_grad` requirement:** At least one input and output must have `requires_grad=True` for the reentrant variant; otherwise the checkpointed part of the model will not have gradients. The non-reentrant version does not have this requirement.
5. **Nested structures:** The reentrant version does **not** consider tensors in nested structures (custom objects, lists, dicts, etc.) as participating in autograd; the non-reentrant version does.
6. **Detached tensors:** The reentrant checkpoint does **not** support checkpointed regions with detached tensors from the computational graph, whereas the non-reentrant version does. For the reentrant variant, if the checkpointed segment contains tensors detached using `detach()` or with `torch.no_grad()`, **the backward pass will raise an error** — because `checkpoint` makes all outputs require gradients, causing issues when a tensor is defined to have no gradient. To avoid this, **detach the tensors outside of the `checkpoint` function.**

### Parameters

- **function** – describes what to run in the forward pass of the model or part of the model. It should also know how to handle the inputs passed as the tuple. For example, in LSTM, if user passes `(activation, hidden)`, `function` should correctly use the first input as `activation` and the second input as `hidden`. If omitted, `checkpoint` returns a decorator that can be used to wrap a function before passing user arguments.
- **args** – tuple containing inputs to the `function`

### Keyword Arguments

- **preserve_rng_state** (*bool, optional*) – Omit stashing and restoring the RNG state during each checkpoint. **Note:** under `torch.compile`, this flag doesn't take effect — RNG state is always preserved. Default: `True`
- **use_reentrant** (*bool*) – Specify whether to use the activation checkpoint variant that requires reentrant autograd. **Should be passed explicitly. In version 2.9 an exception will be raised if `use_reentrant` is not passed.** If `use_reentrant=False`, `checkpoint` uses an implementation that does not require reentrant autograd, supporting extra functionality such as working as expected with `torch.autograd.grad` and support for keyword arguments input into the checkpointed function.
- **context_fn** (*Callable, optional*) – A callable returning a tuple of two context managers. The function and its recomputation will be run under the first and second context managers respectively. **Only supported if `use_reentrant=False`.**
- **determinism_check** (*str, optional*) – A string specifying the determinism check to perform. Default is `"default"`, which compares shapes, dtypes, and devices of recomputed tensors against the saved tensors. To turn off, specify `"none"`. Only these two values are supported. **Only supported if `use_reentrant=False`**; if `use_reentrant=True`, the determinism check is always disabled.
- **debug** (*bool, optional*) – If `True`, error messages will also include a trace of the operators ran during the original forward computation as well as the recomputation. **Only supported if `use_reentrant=False`.**
- **early_stop** (*bool, optional*) – If `True`, non-reentrant checkpoint stops recomputation as soon as it has computed all needed Tensors. Ignored if `use_reentrant=True`. Can be overridden globally using `set_checkpoint_early_stop()` context manager. Default: `True`.
- **respect_saved_tensors_hooks** (*bool, optional*) – Whether tensors that selective activation checkpointing (SAC) saves are routed through the surrounding user `torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks()` (e.g. `torch.autograd.graph.save_on_cpu()`). Such tensors are held outside the autograd graph, so historically these hooks did not see them; **a future release will make checkpoint honor the hooks by default.** Until then, the default (`None`) keeps the legacy behavior and emits a `FutureWarning` when a user hook is in scope; pass `True` to opt in or `False` to keep the legacy behavior without the warning. Has no effect without SAC or when `use_reentrant=True`. **Only supported if `use_reentrant=False`.**

### Returns

Output of running `function` on `*args`, or a decorator when `function` is omitted.

### Example

```python
>>> # Direct call: checkpoint the function immediately.
>>> out = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
...     fn, *args, use_reentrant=False, **kwargs
... )
>>> # Decorator/curried form: configure once, then call.
>>> checkpointed_fn = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
...     use_reentrant=False,
...     preserve_rng_state=False,
... )(fn)
>>> out = checkpointed_fn(*args, **kwargs)
>>> # The same decorator can be applied directly to a function or method.
>>> @torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)
... def fn(*args, **kwargs):
...     ...
>>> out = fn(*args, **kwargs)
```

---

## 3. `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint_sequential()`

### Signature
```
torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint_sequential(
    functions, segments, input, use_reentrant=None, **kwargs
)
```

### Description
> Checkpoint a sequential model to save memory.
>
> Sequential models execute a list of modules/functions in order (sequentially). Therefore, we can divide such a model in various segments and checkpoint each segment. **All segments except the last will not store the intermediate activations.** The inputs of each checkpointed segment will be saved for re-running the segment in the backward pass.

### Warning
> The `use_reentrant` parameter should be passed explicitly. **In version 2.9 we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed.** It is recommended that you use `use_reentrant=False`.

*(Note: The doc text contains an internal inconsistency — it says "In version 2.5 we will raise an exception" in the Parameters section, while the Warning says "In version 2.9". Both are quoted below as written.)*

### Parameters
- **functions** – A `torch.nn.Sequential` or the list of modules or functions (comprising the model) to run sequentially.
- **segments** – Number of chunks to create in the model
- **input** – A Tensor that is input to `functions`
- **preserve_rng_state** (*bool, optional*) – Omit stashing and restoring the RNG state during each checkpoint. Default: `True`
- **use_reentrant** (*bool*) – Specify whether to use the activation checkpoint variant that requires reentrant autograd. Should be passed explicitly. *(Text states: "In version 2.5 we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed.")* If `use_reentrant=False`, `checkpoint` will use an implementation that does not require reentrant autograd, supporting additional functionality such as working as expected with `torch.autograd.grad` and support for keyword arguments input into the checkpointed function.

### Returns
Output of running `functions` sequentially on `*inputs`

### Example
```python
>>> model = nn.Sequential(...)
>>> input_var = checkpoint_sequential(model, chunks, input_var)
```

---

## 4. `torch.utils.checkpoint.set_checkpoint_debug_enabled(enabled)`

Context manager that sets whether checkpoint should print additional debug information when running. See the `debug` flag for `checkpoint()` for more information. When set, this context manager **overrides** the value of `debug` passed to checkpoint. To defer to the local setting, pass `None` to this context.

**Parameters:** **enabled** (*bool*) – Whether checkpoint should print debug information. Default is 'None'.

---

## 5. `class torch.utils.checkpoint.CheckpointPolicy(value)`

Enum for specifying the policy for checkpointing during backpropagation.

Supported policies:
- `{MUST,PREFER}_SAVE`: The operation's output will be saved during the forward pass and will not be recomputed during the backward pass
- `{MUST,PREFER}_RECOMPUTE`: The operation's output will not be saved during the forward pass and will be recomputed during the backward pass
- `{MUST,PREFER}_CPU_OFFLOAD`: The operation's output will be saved during the forward pass, offloaded to CPU, and reloaded to GPU during the backward pass

Use `MUST_*` over `PREFER_*` to indicate that the policy should not be overridden by other subsystems like torch.compile.

**Note:**
- A policy function that always returns `PREFER_RECOMPUTE` is equivalent to vanilla checkpointing.
- A policy function that returns `PREFER_SAVE` every op is **NOT** equivalent to not using checkpointing — it would save additional tensors not limited to ones actually needed for gradient computation.

---

## 6. `class torch.utils.checkpoint.SelectiveCheckpointContext(*, is_recompute, op_output=None)`

Context passed to policy function during selective checkpointing. Used to pass relevant metadata to the policy function.

The policy function is only called during the forward pass. During recomputation, cached values are retrieved by index, so `is_recompute` **is deprecated and always `False`**.

**Example:**
```python
>>>
>>> def policy_fn(ctx, op, *args, **kwargs):
>>>    print(ctx.op_output)
>>>
>>> context_fn = functools.partial(create_selective_checkpoint_contexts, policy_fn)
>>>
>>> out = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
>>>     fn, x, y,
>>>     use_reentrant=False,
>>>     context_fn=context_fn,
>>> )
```

---

## 7. `torch.utils.checkpoint.create_selective_checkpoint_contexts(policy_fn_or_list, allow_cache_entry_mutation=False)`

Helper to avoid recomputing certain ops during activation checkpointing. Use with `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint` to control which operations are recomputed during the backward pass.

**Parameters:**
- **policy_fn_or_list** (*Callable or List*) –
  - If a policy function is provided, it should accept a `SelectiveCheckpointContext`, the `OpOverload`, args and kwargs to the op, and return a `CheckpointPolicy` enum value indicating whether the execution of the op should be recomputed or not.
  - If a list of operations is provided, it is equivalent to a policy returning `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_SAVE` for the specified operations and `CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE` for all other operations.
- **allow_cache_entry_mutation** (*bool, optional*) – By default, an error is raised if any tensors cached by selective activation checkpoint are mutated, to ensure correctness. If set to `True`, this check is disabled.

**Returns:** A tuple of two context managers.

**Example:**
```python
>>> import functools
>>>
>>> x = torch.rand(10, 10, requires_grad=True)
>>> y = torch.rand(10, 10, requires_grad=True)
>>>
>>> ops_to_save = [
>>>    torch.ops.aten.mm.default,
>>> ]
>>>
>>> def policy_fn(ctx, op, *args, **kwargs):
>>>    if op in ops_to_save:
>>>        return CheckpointPolicy.MUST_SAVE
>>>    else:
>>>        return CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE
>>>
>>> context_fn = functools.partial(create_selective_checkpoint_contexts, policy_fn)
>>>
>>> # or equivalently
>>> context_fn = functools.partial(create_selective_checkpoint_contexts, ops_to_save)
>>>
>>> def fn(x, y):
>>>     return torch.sigmoid(torch.matmul(torch.matmul(x, y), y)) * y
>>>
>>> out = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
>>>     fn, x, y,
>>>     use_reentrant=False,
>>>     context_fn=context_fn,
>>> )
```

---

## 8. `class torch.utils.checkpoint.GraphExecGroup`

> Any checkpointed regions encountered by backward under the same instance of this context manager will trigger recompute **at most once**, even if there are multiple calls to backward.
>
> Backward calls under the same instance of this context manager must execute over **non-overlapping regions** of the backward graph even if `retain_graph=True`. In particular, any two backward calls cannot use the same saved activation for gradient computation.

**Note:** This context manager only affects checkpoint with `use_reentrant=False`, and is a no-op otherwise.

---

## 9. `torch.utils.checkpoint.set_checkpoint_early_stop(enable)`

Controls whether checkpoint should stop recomputation early.

By default, non-reentrant checkpoint stops recomputation as soon as it has computed all needed Tensors. This context manager can be used to disable that feature if it is problematic for your specific application.

**This context manager only needs to be active when forward is run. It does not need to be active during backward.**

**Example:**
```python
>>> message = "saved tensors default hooks are disabled"
>>> with set_checkpoint_early_stop(False):
...     # Any checkpoint under this context manager will respect this
...     # context manager, even if its backward is performed outside.
...     out = checkpoint(fn, inputs)
...
>>> out.backward()
```

---

## 10. `torch.utils.checkpoint.set_device_states(devices, states, *, device_type=None)`

Sets random number generator states for the specified devices.

**Parameters:**
- **devices** – Device ids to set states for.
- **states** – States to set.
- **device_type** – `device_type` of the devices to set states for. Default is the device returned by a call to `DefaultDeviceType.get_device_type()`, which is `cuda` if not changed by calling `DefaultDeviceType::set_device_type()`.

---

## Key Version Notes Summary

| Item | Note |
|---|---|
| `use_reentrant` explicit passing | **Version 2.9 will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed** (stated in `checkpoint` warning and `checkpoint_sequential` warning). |
| `checkpoint_sequential` params inconsistency | Parameters section states "In version 2.5 we will raise an exception" — likely a doc typo vs. the 2.9 stated in the warning. |
| `preserve_rng_state` under `torch.compile` | Flag has no effect; RNG state is always preserved. |
| `respect_saved_tensors_hooks` | Default (`None`) = legacy behavior + `FutureWarning`; a **future release** will make checkpoint honor saved-tensor hooks by default. |
| Documentation build | v2.14.0 (stable); Created Jun 16, 2025; Last Updated Jul 27, 2026. |

## Code Examples Preserved
All code examples (decorator usage, `checkpoint_sequential`, `SelectiveCheckpointContext`, `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts`, and `set_checkpoint_early_stop`) are included verbatim above in their respective sections.

## Truncation Assessment
**No core content appears truncated.** The page includes the complete API reference for `torch.utils.checkpoint` (all 9 documented members), all warnings, notes, parameters, and examples. The document ends naturally with `set_device_states()`, followed by standard footer navigation and copyright. The only non-content elements are the extensive sidebar navigation and version selector.

# Understanding CUDA Memory Usage — Analysis

## Page Metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Title** | Understanding CUDA Memory Usage |
| **Source** | PyTorch 2.14 documentation |
| **Version** | v2.14.0 (stable) |
| **Created On** | Aug 23, 2023 |
| **Last Updated On** | Jul 07, 2026 |
| **URL** | docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/torch_cuda_memory.html |

**Version notes:** The page is the v2.14.0 (stable) version. A version selector includes v2.15.0 (unstable) and all prior releases back to v0.1.12. Adjacent navigation links are `Event` (torch.cuda.streams) as previous page and `torch.mps` as next page.

**Content completeness:** The content appears **complete and not truncated**. It includes the full narrative sections, code examples, the complete Snapshot API Reference (with all TypedDict definitions for `Snapshot`, `Segment`, `Block`, `Frame`, `TraceEntry`), and the trailing site footer/navigation — with no cut-off markers.

---

## Purpose (from the page intro)

PyTorch provides a way to generate **memory snapshots** that record the state of allocated CUDA memory at any point in time, and optionally record the history of allocation events leading up to that snapshot. Snapshots can be dragged and dropped onto an interactive viewer at **pytorch.org/memory_viz**.

> **Important caveat:** By default, the profiler only sees CUDA device memory allocated/managed through the PyTorch allocator. Memory allocated directly via CUDA APIs in C++ (`cudaMalloc`, `cuMemCreate`) or third-party bindings (e.g., `cuda-python`) — notably **NCCL** — will **not** be visible.

---

## Tool 1: Generating a Snapshot

The canonical three-step pattern:

```python
# enable memory history, which will
# add tracebacks and event history to snapshots
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()

run_your_code()
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("my_snapshot.pickle")
```

### Including Pinned (Host) Memory

By default snapshots only include CUDA device memory. To also capture CPU pinned memory (e.g., tensors created with `pin_memory=True`):

```python
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(record_pinned_host_memory=True)

run_your_code()
snapshot = torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()
# Host allocator data is in snapshot["host_segments"] and snapshot["host_traces"]
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("my_snapshot.pickle")
```

To record **only** host pinned memory and skip the CUDA device allocator:

```python
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(record_pinned_host_memory=True, record_cuda=False)
```

> **Note:** The memory_viz visualizer does **not yet support** displaying host memory data; inspect `host_segments` and `host_traces` programmatically instead.

---

## Tool 2: Visualization at pytorch.org/memory_viz

Open **https://pytorch.org/memory_viz** and drag/drop the pickled snapshot file onto it. It is a **JavaScript app that runs locally** — it does **not** upload any snapshot data.

The visualizer provides two primary views:

**Active Memory Timeline**
- Shows all live tensors over time on a particular GPU.
- Pan/Zoom to inspect smaller allocations; mouse over blocks to see the allocation stack trace and address details.
- A "detail" slider reduces rendered allocations to improve performance with large datasets.

**Allocator State History**
- Shows individual allocator events on a timeline (left side); selecting an event shows a visual summary of the allocator state at that moment.
- Displays each `cudaMalloc` segment and how it splits into blocks (allocations or free space).
- Mouse-over reveals stack traces for allocation, freeing, and OOM events.
- Examining memory state during an OOM can explain why an allocation failed even when reserved memory exists.

**Address lookup format:** `b7f064c000000_0` decodes as the (b)**lock** at address `7f064c000000`, the **"_0"th** time that address was allocated. This unique string can be cross-referenced in the Active Memory Timeline and searched in the Active State History.

---

## Tool 3: Identifying Non-PyTorch Allocations

If you suspect CUDA memory is allocated outside PyTorch, collect raw CUDA allocation info via the **pynvml** package and compare with PyTorch's reported usage:

```python
import torch
device_idx = ...
print(torch.cuda.device_memory_used(device_idx))
```

---

## API Reference Summary

### `torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(...)`

Key parameters:

| Param | Type | Purpose / Default |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `None`/"state"/"all" | `None`=off; "state"=current allocations; "all"=+full alloc/free history. Default: **"all"** |
| `context` | `None`/"state"/"alloc"/"all" | Controls traceback recording depth. Default: **"all"** |
| `stacks` | "python"/"all" | "python"=Python/TorchScript/inductor frames; "all"=+C++ frames. Default: **"all"** |
| `max_entries` | int | Max alloc/free events kept (default `sys.maxsize`). Ring-buffer: new overwrites old. |
| `clear_history` | bool | Default `False` |
| `skip_actions` | list[str] | Events to skip: `alloc`, `free_requested`, `free_completed`, `segment_alloc`, `segment_free`, `oom`, `snapshot`. Default `None` |
| `record_pinned_host_memory` | bool | Default `False` |
| `record_cuda` | bool | Default `True` |

**Performance:** Python trace collection is fast (~2 µs per trace); C++ collection ~50 ns/frame. The page notes you may consider enabling this on **production jobs** if you anticipate debugging memory issues.

**Memory caution:** Each `TraceEntry` is several KB; long/indefinite jobs should set a reasonable `max_entries` limit.

### `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot(device=None, augment_with_fx_traces=False)`

Returns a `Snapshot` dict:
- `segments: List[Segment]` — memory returned from `cudaMalloc`, cached/reused, split into `Block`s.
- `device_traces: List[List[TraceEntry]]` — allocator action history.

`augment_with_fx_traces=True` adds FX debug fields (`fx_node_op`, `fx_node_name`, `fx_original_trace`) mapping generated FX code back to original model source.

### `torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot(filename='dump_snapshot.pickle', augment_with_fx_traces=False)`

Saves a pickled `_snapshot()` dict to a file readable by pytorch.org/memory_viz. File sizes scale with `max_entries` × stack depth — **can easily reach GB range** for long workflows.

**`TraceEntry.action` values:** `alloc`, `free_requested`, `free_completed`, `segment_alloc`, `segment_free`, `oom`, `snapshot`, `annotate`.

---

## Recommended Debugging Workflow

1. **Enable recording** before the suspect code: `torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()` (add `record_pinned_host_memory=True` / set `max_entries` / `skip_actions` as needed).
2. **Run** the code to be observed.
3. **Dump** a pickled snapshot: `torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("my_snapshot.pickle")`.
4. **Visualize** by dragging the `.pickle` into pytorch.org/memory_viz (runs locally, no upload).
5. **Investigate** via the Active Memory Timeline and Allocator State History — inspect stack traces, block addresses, and OOM state.
6. **If memory is missing from the snapshot**, suspect non-PyTorch (e.g., NCCL) allocations and compare using `torch.cuda.device_memory_used(device_idx)`.

*Source: PyTorch 2.14.0 (stable) documentation.*

**发布时间**: 2026/01/17

# CUDA Out of Memory 完全排查指南

理解这个错误错误长什么样什么原因导致 CUDA OOM？快速诊断第一步：检查当前 GPU 显存使用第二步：在 Python 中检查显存第三步：找出占用显存的操作快速修复（先试这些）修复 1：减小批次大小修复 2：清理 GPU 缓存修复 3：使用混合精度（FP16/BF16）修复 4：启用梯度检查点修复 5：使用更小的数据类型高级解决方案方案 1：8-bit 和 4-bit 量化方案 2：梯度累积方案 3：CPU 卸载方案 4：模型并行方案 5：高效注意力（Flash Attention）各框架专用方案PyTorchTensorFlowStable Diffusion / ComfyUIHugging Face Transformers显存需求参考LLM 训练显存公式图像生成显存排查内存泄漏识别泄漏常见泄漏模式预防策略1. 运行前估算显存2. 从小开始，逐步扩大3. 训练时监控快速参考：各场景 OOM 解决方案总结

"CUDA out of memory" 是深度学习中最令人头疼的错误。本文涵盖所有解决方案，从快速修复到高级技术。

## 理解这个错误

### 错误长什么样

**PyTorch:**

```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB
(GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total capacity; 21.58 GiB already allocated;
1.45 GiB free; 22.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
```

**TensorFlow:**

```
ResourceExhaustedError: OOM when allocating tensor with shape [32, 512, 512, 3]
```

**Stable Diffusion:**

```
torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory.
```

### 什么原因导致 CUDA OOM？

原因描述解决方案**模型太大**模型参数超过显存使用更小的模型或量化**批次大小太高**每个样本都占用显存减小 batch size**输入太大**高分辨率图像/长序列减小输入尺寸**内存泄漏**张量没有正确释放清理缓存，修复代码**梯度累积**反向传播存储梯度使用梯度检查点**多个模型**同时加载多个模型卸载不用的模型

## 快速诊断

### 第一步：检查当前 GPU 显存使用

```
# 实时监控
watch -n 1 nvidia-smi

# 单次检查
nvidia-smi
```

**输出说明：**

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.104.05   Driver Version: 535.104.05   CUDA Version: 12.2     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|         Memory-Usage | GPU-Util  Compute M. |
|===============================+======================+======================|
|   0  NVIDIA RTX 4090     On   | 00000000:01:00.0 Off |                  Off |
| 30%   45C    P2    75W / 450W |  18432MiB / 24564MiB |     85%      Default |
+-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+
```

**关键指标：** `18432MiB / 24564MiB` = 已使用 75% 显存

### 第二步：在 Python 中检查显存

```
import torch

# 检查 CUDA 是否可用
print(f"CUDA 可用: {torch.cuda.is_available()}")
print(f"设备数量: {torch.cuda.device_count()}")
print(f"当前设备: {torch.cuda.current_device()}")
print(f"设备名称: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")

# 显存信息
print(f"总显存: {torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1e9:.2f} GB")
print(f"已分配: {torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0) / 1e9:.2f} GB")
print(f"已缓存: {torch.cuda.memory_reserved(0) / 1e9:.2f} GB")
```

### 第三步：找出占用显存的操作

```
# 启用显存追踪
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()

# 运行你的代码
# ...

# 获取显存快照
snapshot = torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()

# 使用 PyTorch 显存可视化工具分析
```

## 快速修复（先试这些）

### 修复 1：减小批次大小

最简单也最有效的解决方案：

```
# 修改前
train_loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=32)  # OOM!

# 修改后
train_loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=8)   # 成功!
```

**经验法则：** 如果 OOM，把 batch size 减半，直到能运行。

### 修复 2：清理 GPU 缓存

```
import torch
import gc

# 清理 PyTorch 缓存
torch.cuda.empty_cache()

# 强制垃圾回收
gc.collect()
```

**使用时机：** 加载/卸载模型后，训练运行之间。

### 修复 3：使用混合精度（FP16/BF16）

减少约 50% 显存占用，精度损失很小：

```
# PyTorch 原生 AMP
from torch.cuda.amp import autocast, GradScaler

scaler = GradScaler()

for batch in dataloader:
    optimizer.zero_grad()

    with autocast():  # FP16 前向传播
        outputs = model(batch)
        loss = criterion(outputs, targets)

    scaler.scale(loss).backward()  # 缩放后的反向传播
    scaler.step(optimizer)
    scaler.update()
```

**Hugging Face Transformers:**

```
from transformers import TrainingArguments

training_args = TrainingArguments(
    fp16=True,  # 启用 FP16
    # 或 bf16=True 用于新显卡 (RTX 3090+, A100, H100)
)
```

### 修复 4：启用梯度检查点

用计算换显存，通过重新计算激活值：

```
# PyTorch
model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()

# Hugging Face
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b",
    gradient_checkpointing=True
)
```

**显存节省：** Transformer 模型可节省 50-70%

### 修复 5：使用更小的数据类型

```
# 以低精度加载模型
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,  # 半精度
    # 或 torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 用于 A100/H100
)
```

## 高级解决方案

### 方案 1：8-bit 和 4-bit 量化

**8-bit 量化 (bitsandbytes):**

```
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b",
    load_in_8bit=True,
    device_map="auto"
)
```

**4-bit 量化 (QLoRA):**

```
from transformers import BitsAndBytesConfig

bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
    load_in_4bit=True,
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
)

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "meta-llama/Llama-2-70b",
    quantization_config=bnb_config,
    device_map="auto"
)
```

**显存对比：**

模型FP32FP168-bit4-bitLlama 2 7B28 GB14 GB7 GB3.5 GBLlama 2 13B52 GB26 GB13 GB6.5 GBLlama 2 70B280 GB140 GB70 GB35 GB

### 方案 2：梯度累积

不增加显存模拟更大的批次：

```
accumulation_steps = 4
optimizer.zero_grad()

for i, batch in enumerate(dataloader):
    outputs = model(batch)
    loss = criterion(outputs, targets)
    loss = loss / accumulation_steps  # 归一化 loss
    loss.backward()

    if (i + 1) % accumulation_steps == 0:
        optimizer.step()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
```

**等效批次大小：** `实际批次大小 × 累积步数`

### 方案 3：CPU 卸载

把模型部分放到 CPU：

```
from accelerate import Accelerator

accelerator = Accelerator(cpu_offload=True)
model, optimizer = accelerator.prepare(model, optimizer)
```

**DeepSpeed ZeRO-Offload:**

```
{
    "zero_optimization": {
        "stage": 3,
        "offload_optimizer": {
            "device": "cpu"
        },
        "offload_param": {
            "device": "cpu"
        }
    }
}
```

### 方案 4：模型并行

把模型分布到多个 GPU：

```
from accelerate import Accelerator

### 识别泄漏

```
import torch

def check_memory():
    print(f"已分配: {torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0) / 1e9:.2f} GB")
    print(f"已保留: {torch.cuda.memory_reserved(0) / 1e9:.2f} GB")

```

### 常见泄漏模式

**1. 在列表中存储张量：**

```
# 错误 - 累积 GPU 显存
losses = []
for batch in dataloader:
    loss = model(batch)
    losses.append(loss)  # 张量留在 GPU 上！

# 正确 - 分离并移到 CPU
losses = []
for batch in dataloader:
    loss = model(batch)
    losses.append(loss.detach().cpu().item())
```

**2. 没有清理梯度：**

```
# 错误 - 梯度累积
for batch in dataloader:
    loss = model(batch)
    loss.backward()

# 正确 - 清零梯度
for batch in dataloader:
    optimizer.zero_grad()  # 清除之前的梯度
    loss = model(batch)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
```

**3. 保留计算图：**

```
# 错误 - 保留整个计算图
total_loss = 0
for batch in dataloader:
    loss = model(batch)
    total_loss += loss  # 保留了计算图！

# 正确 - 从计算图分离
total_loss = 0
for batch in dataloader:
    loss = model(batch)
    total_loss += loss.item()  # 只取数值
```

## 预防策略

### 1. 运行前估算显存

```
def estimate_model_memory(model, batch_size, precision='fp32'):
    """估算模型显存使用。"""
    param_size = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())

    bytes_per_param = {'fp32': 4, 'fp16': 2, 'int8': 1}[precision]

    # 参数 + 梯度 + 优化器状态 (Adam ≈ 3x)
    training_memory = param_size * bytes_per_param * 4

    total = training_memory
    return total / 1e9  # GB

# 使用
memory_needed = estimate_model_memory(model, batch_size=8)
print(f"估计显存: {memory_needed:.2f} GB")
```

### 2. 从小开始，逐步扩大

# 最终答案：PyTorch 训练 CUDA OOM 的排查与显存优化

以下结论区分三类：**[官方原文]** = 已抓取的官方文档正文；**[我的解释]** = 基于原文的推断；**[未核实]** = 未取得证据处。

## 0. 先诊断：区分「张量占用」与「分配器缓存占用」

**[官方原文，CUDA semantics]**
> "PyTorch uses a caching memory allocator... the unused memory managed by the allocator will still show as if used in `nvidia-smi`. You can use `memory_allocated()` and `max_memory_allocated()` to monitor memory occupied by tensors, and use `memory_reserved()` and `max_memory_reserved()` to monitor the total amount of memory managed by the caching allocator."

**排查命令/代码：**
```bash
nvidia-smi                    # 是否有别的进程占卡
watch -n1 nvidia-smi          # 实时观察
```
```python
import torch
print(torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0), torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(0))  # 张量占用
print(torch.cuda.memory_reserved(0),  torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved(0))   # 分配器管理总量
print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())
```
**[官方原文，Understanding CUDA Memory Usage]** 抓快照并可视化：
```python
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()          # 记录 alloc/free 历史
run_your_code()
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("my_snapshot.pickle")
```
打开 `https://pytorch.org/memory_viz` 拖入 pickle（官方说明该可视化在本地运行、不上传）。快照可看 **Active Memory Timeline** 与 **Allocator State History**（能看 OOM 时刻的 segment/block 切分与栈），可解释"reserved 有余量仍 OOM"的碎片场景。

**[官方原文，同页警告]** 默认快照只覆盖 PyTorch 分配器管理的内存，直接经 C++ CUDA API 分配的（**尤其是 NCCL**）不可见；可用 `torch.cuda.device_memory_used(device_idx)` 对比排查。

---

## 1. `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`

**[官方原文，CUDA semantics]**
> "Calling `empty_cache()` releases all **unused** cached memory from PyTorch so that those can be used by other GPU applications. However, the occupied GPU memory by tensors will not be freed so it can not increase the amount of GPU memory available for PyTorch."

即：只归还分配器里**空置**的缓存块；**不会**释放仍被张量引用的显存，也就**不能**直接为本次 PyTorch 运算腾出可用显存。**[我的解释]** 因此它主要用在阶段切换（如训练前、评估前后、模型加载/卸载之间）或配合 `del` 释放引用后回收，频繁每步调用会因反复 `cudaMalloc` 增加开销（官方未在此页给出"频繁调用变慢"的量化结论，属我的解释）。

```python
import gc, torch
del some_tensor          # 先解引用
gc.collect()
torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```
**[未核实]** `torch.cuda.empty_cache` 的独立生成页 `docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.cuda.empty_cache.html` 抓取返回 **404（Page not found · GitHub Pages）**，故未取到该函数的独立签名页；行为原文取自 CUDA semantics 页。

---

## 2. 分配器参数 `max_split_size_mb` 等（`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`）

**[官方原文，CUDA semantics]** 环境变量已改名为 `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`：
> "The behavior of the caching allocator can be controlled via the environment variable `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` is its alias and is provided only for backward compatibility. The format is `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=<option>:<value>,<option2>:<value2>...`"

**[官方原文，`max_split_size_mb`]**
> "prevents the native allocator from splitting blocks larger than this size (in MB). This can reduce fragmentation and may allow some borderline workloads to complete without running out of memory. Performance cost can range from 'zero' to 'substantial' depending on allocation patterns. Default value is unlimited, i.e. all blocks can be split. The `memory_stats()` and `memory_summary()` methods are useful for tuning. This option should be used as a last resort for a workload that is aborting due to 'out of memory' and showing a large amount of inactive split blocks. `max_split_size_mb` is only meaningful with `backend:native`. With `backend:cudaMallocAsync`, `max_split_size_mb` is ignored."

要点（均为官方原文）：单位 **MB**；默认 **unlimited**；作用是"禁止切分大于该值的块"以缓解碎片；性能代价可能为 0 到显著；**属于最后手段**，官方定位是"出现大量 inactive split blocks 且 OOM 时用 `memory_stats()/memory_summary()` 调参"；**仅在 `backend:native` 下有意义**。

用法（须在导入/初始化前设置，**[我的解释]** 分配器在进程早期读取）：
```bash
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:512
# 或（新名）
export PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:512
```
```python
import os
os.environ["PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF"] = "max_split_size_mb:512"
```

同页其他相关键（**[官方原文]** 摘要）：
- `garbage_collection_threshold`：取值 (0,1)，默认 1.0；超过阈值比例时主动回收空置块，优先回收旧块，避免昂贵的 release_cached_blocks；**仅 `backend:native` 有意义**。
- `expandable_segments`（实验性，默认 `False`）：让分配器创建可增长的 CUDA 段，缓解"batch size 变动/深层模型产生大量内存碎片"的情形；原文以 50+ 层模型产生 sliver 为例。
- `roundup_power2_divisions`：把分配尺寸向上取整到最近的 2 的幂分段（示例 `[256:1,512:2,1024:4,>:8]`）；**仅 `backend:native` 有意义**。
- `max_non_split_rounding_mb`：允许非切分块更大范围复用（如 1024MB 缓存块服务 512MB 请求），减少 cudaMalloc 停顿。
- `backend`：`native`（默认）或 `cudaMallocAsync`（**需 CUDA 11.4+**）。
- `per_process_memory_fraction`（0~1，超过即 OOM）、`throw_on_cudamalloc_oom`（默认 `False`，设 `True` 时超限直接抛 `OutOfMemoryError` 而非触发致命 abort，示例 `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=per_process_memory_fraction:0.95,throw_on_cudamalloc_oom:True`）。
- 调试用：`PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` 可关闭缓存（供 `cuda-memcheck`）。

**[官方原文明确否证的一点]** 官方 `max_split_size_mb` 段落**没有**"设置过小会警告"的文字，只有"performance cost zero~substantial"和"last resort"。[我的解释] 网上常见的"设太小反而更差"属经验说法，本页未给出。

## 3. 梯度检查点（Gradient Checkpointing）

**[官方原文，torch.utils.checkpoint]**
> "Activation checkpointing is a technique that trades compute for memory. By default, tensors computed during the forward pass are kept alive until they are used in gradient computations in the backward pass. To reduce this memory usage, tensors produced in the passed `function` are not kept alive until the backward pass. Instead, any passed tensors in `args` are kept alive, and the unsaved tensors are recomputed by re-invoking `function` in the backward pass... There are currently two checkpointing implementations, determined by the `use_reentrant` parameter. **It is recommended that you use `use_reentrant=False`.**"

签名（官方）：
```python
torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
    *function, *args, use_reentrant=None, preserve_rng_state=True,
    context_fn=noop_context_fn, determinism_check=_DEFAULT_DETERMINISM_MODE,
    debug=False, early_stop=True, respect_saved_tensors_hooks=None, **kwargs)
```
用法：
```python
import torch.utils.checkpoint as cp
out = cp.checkpoint(fn, x, use_reentrant=False)          # 直接调用
@cp.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)                       # 装饰器
def fn(x): ...
```
```python
model = nn.Sequential(...)
out = cp.checkpoint_sequential(model, chunks, input_var)  # 分段 checkpoint
```

**[官方原文，关键约束/注意事项]**
- **必须显式传 `use_reentrant`**：*"The `use_reentrant` parameter should be passed explicitly. **In version 2.9 we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed.**"*（`checkpoint_sequential` 的 Warning 同样写 2.9；但同页 Parameters 段却写 2.5，**官方文档内部不一致**，见"未核实处"。）
- **RNG/确定性**：默认 `preserve_rng_state=True` 会存取 RNG 状态以对齐非 checkpoint 结果，有中等性能开销；仅在多设备类型时只保存一种设备类型的状态，**可能产生错误梯度**；`torch.compile` 下该 flag 不生效（始终保留 RNG）。
- **`use_reentrant=True` 的限制**：前向在 `torch.no_grad()` 下运行、不记录 autograd 图；只支持不带 `inputs` 的 `torch.autograd.backward()`；要求至少一个输入/输出 `requires_grad=True`；不支持嵌套结构中的张量与已 `detach()`/`no_grad` 的段（会报错，需在 checkpoint 外 `detach`）。
- `use_reentrant=False` 支持 `context_fn`、`determinism_check`、`debug`、`early_stop` 等；另有选择性检查点 API `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts` 与 `CheckpointPolicy`（`MUST/PREFER_SAVE/RECOMPUTE/CPU_OFFLOAD`）。
- **警告**：若 backward 时 `function` 调用与 forward 不一致（如依赖全局变量），可能报错或**静默产生错误梯度**。

**[我的解释]** 训练 OOM 时开启 checkpoint 通常显著降低 activation 显存（换取约一次额外前向计算）；HuggingFace 侧常见 `model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()` 并配 `use_cache=False`——**[未核实]** 本次未检索 HF 官方文档，此接口细节未取得官方原文印证，仅作提示。

## 4. 其他常用优化（**综合二手源与通用实践，非本页官方原文逐条印证**）

高置信、与官方精神一致的顺序建议：
1. 减小 batch size；用**梯度累积**保持等效 batch（损失需除以累积步数）。
2. 混合精度 AMP（`torch.cuda.amp.autocast` + `GradScaler`）。
3. 梯度检查点（见上）。
4. `optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)`；避免把 loss 张量累积进列表（`loss.item()`/`detach().cpu()`）；释放无需的中间张量后 `empty_cache()`。
5. 高效注意力（FlashAttention / `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`）、量化（8/4-bit）、CPU offload、模型并行/FSDP/DeepSpeed ZeRO。
6. 碎片顽固时再动分配器：优先试 `expandable_segments:True`，**最后**才调 `max_split_size_mb`（官方定位为 last resort）。

2. **梯度爆炸**：
   - 梯度裁剪 `torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)`。

6. **权重初始化 / BN**：
   - BN 在 batch size=1 或 fp16 下易出 NaN；初始化不当（如全零或过大）导致爆炸。

# torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_[#](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_.html#torch-nn-utils-clip-grad-norm "Link to this heading")

torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(*parameters*, *max_norm*, *norm_type=2.0*, *error_if_nonfinite=False*, *foreach=None*)[[source]](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.14.0/torch/nn/utils/clip_grad.py#L184)[#](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_.html#torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ "Link to this definition")

Clip the gradient norm of an iterable of parameters.

The norm is computed over the norms of the individual gradients of all parameters, as if the norms of the individual gradients were concatenated into a single vector. Gradients are modified in-place.

This function is equivalent to [`torch.nn.utils.get_total_norm()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.utils.get_total_norm.html#torch.nn.utils.get_total_norm "torch.nn.utils.get_total_norm") followed by [`torch.nn.utils.clip_grads_with_norm_()`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.utils.clip_grads_with_norm_.html#torch.nn.utils.clip_grads_with_norm_ "torch.nn.utils.clip_grads_with_norm_") with the `total_norm` returned by `get_total_norm`.

Parameters:

- **parameters** (*Iterable[*[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/tensors.html#torch.Tensor "torch.Tensor")*] or* [*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/tensors.html#torch.Tensor "torch.Tensor")) – an iterable of Tensors or a single Tensor that will have gradients normalized
- **max_norm** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float "(in Python v3.14)")) – max norm of the gradients
- **norm_type** ([*float*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float "(in Python v3.14)")*, optional*) – type of the used p-norm. Can be `'inf'` for infinity norm. Default: 2.0
- **error_if_nonfinite** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool "(in Python v3.14)")*, optional*) – if True, an error is thrown if the total norm of the gradients from `parameters` is `nan`, `inf`, or `-inf`. Default: False
- **foreach** ([*bool*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool "(in Python v3.14)")*, optional*) – use the faster foreach-based implementation. If `None`, use the foreach implementation for CUDA and CPU native tensors and silently fall back to the slow implementation for other device types. Default: `None`

Returns:

Total norm of the parameter gradients (viewed as a single vector).

Return type:

[*Tensor*](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/tensors.html#torch.Tensor "torch.Tensor")

## Version Shown
The page is **PyTorch 2.14 documentation** (specifically labeled "**v2.14.0 (stable)**" in the version selector). The page title reads "Automatic differentiation package - torch.autograd — PyTorch 2.14 documentation."

## Full Text of the "Debugging and anomaly detection" Section

*(Note: The section actually appears under the heading **"Debugging and anomaly detection"**, of which anomaly detection is the subject.)*

### *class* `torch.autograd.detect_anomaly(check_nan=True)`

Context-manager that enables anomaly detection for the autograd engine.

This does two things:

- Running the forward pass with detection enabled will allow the backward pass to print the traceback of the forward operation that created the failing backward function.
- If `check_nan` is `True`, any backward computation that generates "nan" value will raise an error. Default `True`.

**Warning**

This mode should be enabled only for debugging as the different tests will slow down your program execution.

**Example**

```
>>> import torch
>>> from torch import autograd
>>> class MyFunc(autograd.Function):
...     @staticmethod
...     def forward(ctx, inp):
...         return inp.clone()
...
...     @staticmethod
...     def backward(ctx, gO):
...         # Error during the backward pass
...         raise RuntimeError("Some error in backward")
...         return gO.clone()
>>> def run_fn(a):
...     out = MyFunc.apply(a)
...     return out.sum()
>>> inp = torch.rand(10, 10, requires_grad=True)
>>> out = run_fn(inp)
>>> out.backward()
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
      File "/your/pytorch/install/torch/_tensor.py", line 93, in backward
        torch.autograd.backward(self, gradient, retain_graph, create_graph)
      File "/your/pytorch/install/torch/autograd/__init__.py", line 90, in backward
        allow_unreachable=True)  # allow_unreachable flag
      File "/your/pytorch/install/torch/autograd/function.py", line 76, in apply
        return self._forward_cls.backward(self, *args)
      File "<stdin>", line 8, in backward
    RuntimeError: Some error in backward
>>> with autograd.detect_anomaly():
...     inp = torch.rand(10, 10, requires_grad=True)
...     out = run_fn(inp)
...     out.backward()
    Traceback of forward call that caused the error:
      File "tmp.py", line 53, in <module>
        out = run_fn(inp)
      File "tmp.py", line 44, in run_fn
        out = MyFunc.apply(a)
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "<stdin>", line 4, in <module>
      File "/your/pytorch/install/torch/_tensor.py", line 93, in backward
        torch.autograd.backward(self, gradient, retain_graph, create_graph)
      File "/your/pytorch/install/torch/autograd/__init__.py", line 90, in backward
        allow_unreachable=True)  # allow_unreachable flag
      File "/your/pytorch/install/torch/autograd/function.py", line 76, in apply
        return self._forward_cls.backward(self, *args)
      File "<stdin>", line 8, in backward
    RuntimeError: Some error in backward
```

### *class* `torch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(mode, check_nan=True)`

Context-manager that sets the anomaly detection for the autograd engine on or off.

`set_detect_anomaly` will enable or disable the autograd anomaly detection based on its argument `mode`. It can be used as a context-manager or as a function.

See `detect_anomaly` above for details of the anomaly detection behaviour.

**Parameters:**

- **mode** (*bool*) – Flag whether to enable anomaly detection (`True`), or disable (`False`).
- **check_nan** (*bool*) – Flag whether to raise an error when the backward generate "nan"

---

## Key Summaries

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| **`detect_anomaly(check_nan=True)`** | Context-manager enabling anomaly detection. (1) Prints traceback of the forward operation that created a failing backward function; (2) if `check_nan=True`, raises an error when backward generates NaN. Warning: use only for debugging—it slows execution. |
| **`set_detect_anomaly(mode, check_nan=True)`** | Enables/disables anomaly detection via the `mode` argument; usable as either a context-manager or a function. Takes `mode` (bool) and `check_nan` (bool). |

Both classes reference each other, and the example demonstrates how `autograd.detect_anomaly()` adds a "Traceback of forward call that caused the error" to the output that is otherwise absent.

# Automatic Mixed Precision package - torch.amp#

# Automatic Mixed Precision package - torch.amp#
Created On: Jun 12, 2025 | Last Updated On: Jul 11, 2026

`torch.amp` provides convenience methods for mixed precision, where some operations use the `torch.float32` (`float`) datatype and other operations use lower precision floating point datatype (`lower_precision_fp`): `torch.float16` (`half`) or `torch.bfloat16`. Some ops, like linear layers and convolutions, are much faster in `lower_precision_fp`. Other ops, like reductions, often require the dynamic range of `float32`. Mixed precision tries to match each op to its appropriate datatype.

Ordinarily, “automatic mixed precision training” with datatype of `torch.float16` uses `torch.autocast` and `torch.amp.GradScaler` together, as shown in the Automatic Mixed Precision examples and Automatic Mixed Precision recipe. However, `torch.autocast` and `torch.GradScaler` are modular, and may be used separately if desired. As shown in the CPU example section of `torch.autocast`, “automatic mixed precision training/inference” on CPU with datatype of `torch.bfloat16` only uses `torch.autocast`.

Warning

[...]

## Gradient Scaling#

# Automatic Mixed Precision package - torch.amp#
## Gradient Scaling#
If the forward pass for a particular op has `float16` inputs, the backward pass for that op will produce `float16` gradients. Gradient values with small magnitudes may not be representable in `float16`. These values will flush to zero (“underflow”), so the update for the corresponding parameters will be lost.

To prevent underflow, “gradient scaling” multiplies the network’s loss(es) by a scale factor and invokes a backward pass on the scaled loss(es). Gradients flowing backward through the network are then scaled by the same factor. In other words, gradient values have a larger magnitude, so they don’t flush to zero.

Each parameter’s gradient (`.grad` attribute) should be unscaled before the optimizer updates the parameters, so the scale factor does not interfere with the learning rate.

Note

AMP/fp16 may not work for every model! For example, most bf16-pretrained models cannot operate in the fp16 numerical range of max 65504 and will cause gradients to overflow instead of underflow. In this case, the scale factor may decrease under 1 as an attempt to bring gradients to a number representable in the fp16 dynamic range. While one may expect the scale to always be above 1, our GradScaler does NOT make this guarantee to maintain performance. If you encounter NaNs in your loss or gradients when running with AMP/fp16, verify your model is compatible.

*class*torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler(*init_scale=65536.0*, *growth_factor=2.0*, *backoff_factor=0.5*, *growth_interval=2000*, *enabled=True*)[[source]](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.14.0/torch/cuda/amp/grad_scaler.py#L12)#

See `torch.amp.GradScaler`. `torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler(args...)` is deprecated. Please use `torch.amp.GradScaler("cuda", args...)` instead.

See `torch.amp.GradScaler`. `torch.cpu.amp.GradScaler(args...)` is deprecated. Please use `torch.amp.GradScaler("cpu", args...)` instead.

# CUDA Environment Variables#

# CUDA Environment Variables#
Created On: May 08, 2026 | Last Updated On: May 08, 2026

For more information on CUDA runtime environment variables, see CUDA Environment Variables.

**PyTorch Environment Variables**

Variable

Description

`PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING`

If set to `1`, disables caching of memory allocations in CUDA. This can be useful for debugging.

`PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`

For a more in depth explanation of this environment variable, see Memory management. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` is its alias and is provided only for backward compatibility.

`PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK`

If set to `1`, before importing PyTorch modules that check if CUDA is available, PyTorch will use NVML to check if the CUDA driver is functional instead of using the CUDA runtime. This can be helpful if forked processes fail with a CUDA initialization error.

`TORCH_CUDNN_V8_API_LRU_CACHE_LIMIT`

The cache limit for the cuDNN v8 API. This is used to limit the memory used by the cuDNN v8 API. The default value is 10000, which roughly corresponds to 2GiB assuming 200KiB per ExecutionPlan. Set to `0` for no limit or a negative value for no caching.

`TORCH_CUDNN_V8_API_DISABLED`

If set to `1`, disables the cuDNN v8 API. And will fall back to the cuDNN v7 API.

`TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE`

If set to `1`, forces TF32 enablement, overrides `set_float32_matmul_precision` setting.

`TORCH_NCCL_USE_COMM_NONBLOCKING`

If set to `1`, enables non-blocking error handling in NCCL.

`TORCH_NCCL_AVOID_RECORD_STREAMS`

If set to `0`, enables fallback to record streams-based synchronization behavior in NCCL.

`TORCH_CUDNN_V8_API_DEBUG`

If set to `1`, sanity check whether cuDNN V8 is being used.

**CUDA Runtime and Libraries Environment Variables**

Variable

Description

# CUDA Environment Variables#
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`

Comma-separated list of GPU device IDs that should be made available to CUDA runtime. If set to `-1`, no GPUs are made available.

`CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING`

If set to `1`, makes CUDA calls synchronous. This can be useful for debugging.

`CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`

This environment variable is used to set the workspace configuration for cuBLAS per allocation. The format is `:[SIZE]:[COUNT]`. As an example, the default workspace size per allocation is `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:2:16:8` which specifies a total size of `2 * 4096 + 8 * 16 KiB`. To force cuBLAS to avoid using workspaces, set `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:0:0`.

`CUDNN_CONV_WSCAP_DBG`

Similar to `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, this environment variable is used to set the workspace configuration for cuDNN per allocation.

`CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE`

Similar to `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`, this environment variable is used to set the workspace size for cuBLASLT.

`CUDNN_ERRATA_JSON_FILE`

Can be set to a file path for an errata filter that can be passed to cuDNN to avoid specific engine configs, used primarily for debugging or to hardcode autotuning.

`NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE`

If set to `0`, disables TF32 globally across all kernels, overriding all PyTorch settings.
