## 在昇腾上用 MindIE 部署模型为推理服务（含配置与起服务）

> 说明：以下内容来自本轮实际检索到的官方/官方文档副本，命令与字段均标注来源 URL；我自行拼装的 JSON 已明确标注为“按文档字段拼装”，非原文整体拷贝。请求别名 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 在本轮检索到的官方文档中没有出现（详见末节“未核实处”）。

### 1. 组件与总体路线

- **CANN**：底层异构计算架构（Toolkit / ops / NNAL）。MindIE 必须与 CANN 配套使用（来源：`https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/preparing_software_and_dependencies/`）。
- **MindIE**：全称 Mind Inference Engine，基于昇腾硬件的高性能推理框架；安装包会依次安装 **MindIE RT、MindIE Torch、MindIE Service、MindIE LLM、MindIE SD** 各组件（来源：`https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindie/10RC3/envdeployment/instg/mindie_instg_0019.html`）。
- **MindIE Server（MindIE-Service）**：对外提供 HTTP(S) 服务，兼容 Triton/OpenAI/TGI/vLLM 第三方框架接口（来源：`https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindie/10RC3/mindieservice/servicedev/mindie_service0004.html`）。

流程：装驱动/固件 → 装 CANN → 装 MindIE → 准备权重 → 改 `config.json` → 启动 `mindieservice_daemon` → curl 验证。

### 2. 版本配套（原题需要定版的组件）

官方文档副本给出的配套表（MindIE / CANN / Ascend Extension for PyTorch 三者必须配套）：

| MindIE | CANN | Ascend Extension for PyTorch |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0.0 | 8.5.1 | 7.3.0（torch、torch_npu：2.9.0）（推荐）；7.2.0（torch、torch_npu：2.1.0） |

- 附注：**DeepSeek-V3.2 不支持 torch、torch_npu 2.1.0**。
- glibc 依赖：`abi0` 包需 glibc ≥ 2.34；`abi1` 包需 glibc ≥ 2.38。
- 来源：`https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/install/source/preparing_software_and_dependencies/`

另有按 Release 分线的官方文档：MindIE **1.0.RC2 / 1.0.RC3 / 1.0.0 / 3.0.0**（hiascend 文档路径中的 `10RC2`、`10RC3`、`100`、`300`），选择时按“文档版本 = 你的安装包版本”对齐。

### 3. 安装（run 包方式）

来源：`https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindie/10RC3/envdeployment/instg/mindie_instg_0019.html`

```bash
# 1) 以 CANN 安装用户登录，上传 MindIE 包到任意路径
cd /home/package

# 2) 加可执行权限（软件包名.run 替换为实际 Ascend-mindie-<version>_linux-<arch>.run）
chmod +x 软件包名.run

# 3) 先配置 ascend-toolkit 环境变量（root 默认路径示例）
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh

# 4) 校验一致性与完整性
./软件包名.run --check

# 5) 安装（支持 --install-path=<path> 等参数）
./软件包名.run --install --quiet
# 成功回显：xxx install success

# 6) 配置 MindIE 环境变量（root 默认路径）
source /usr/local/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh
# 非 root 默认路径：source /home/{当前用户名}/Ascend/mindie/set_env.sh
```

要点（原文）：
- 默认安装路径：root 为 `/usr/local/Ascend`；非 root 为 `/home/{用户名}/Ascend`。
- root 用户**勿安装在非 root 用户目录下**。
- 安装日志：root 为 `/var/log/mindie_log/mindie_install.log`；非 root 为 `/home/{用户名}/var/log/mindie_log/mindie_install.log`。
- 默认安装 `abi0` 版本；默认装 torch 2.1.0 的 CPP/Python API。

### 4. 配置 config.json

**配置文件路径**（来源：`https://mindie-llm-doc.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/user_guide/user_manual/service_parameter_configuration/`）：
- whl 包方式：`{MindIE安装目录}/mindie_llm/conf/config.json`
- run 包方式：`{MindIE安装目录}/latest/mindie-service/conf/config.json`
- 系统会先校验文件大小，必须在 **(0MB, 10MB]** 之间，否则读取失败。

**结构**：根级 `Version`（固定 `"1.0.0"`，不支持修改）、`ServerConfig`、`BackendConfig`、`LogConfig`、`EnableDynamicAdjustTimeoutConfig`。

**ServerConfig 关键项**（同源）：

| 字段 | 默认 | 必填 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ipAddress` | `"127.0.0.1"` | 必填 | 业务面 RESTful 绑定 IP；有环境变量 `MIES_CONTAINER_IP` 时优先 |
| `port` | `1025` | 必填 | 业务面端口，范围 [1024,65535] |
| `managementIpAddress` | `"127.0.0.2"` | 选填 | 内部接口 IP；优先级 `MIES_CONTAINER_MANAGEMENT_IP` > 本字段 > `ipAddress` |
| `managementPort` | `1026` | 选填 | 内部接口端口 |
| `metricsPort` | `1027` | 选填 | 普罗指标端口 |
| `maxLinkNum` | `1000` | 必填 | 并发处理数，**推荐 300** |
| `httpsEnabled` | `true` | 必填 | 是否启用 HTTPS 认证 |
| `allowAllZeroIpListening` | `false` | 必填 | 是否允许绑 0.0.0.0（默认禁止） |
| `inferMode` | `"standard"` | 必填 | `standard`=PD 混部；`dmi`=PD 分离 |
| `openAiSupport` | `"vllm"` | 选填 | `"vllm"` 时 `/v1/chat/completions` 用 vLLM 兼容版本 |
| `tokenTimeout` / `e2eTimeout` | `600` | — | 单 token / 端到端超时（秒），PD 分离场景无效 |
| `maxRequestLength` | `40` | 选填 | 请求体上限（MB） |
| `distDPServerEnabled` | `false` | 必填 | 分布式部署开关（大规模专家并行） |
| `HealthCheckConfig.npuUsageThreshold` | `10` | 选填 | 0=关闭健康检查；健康/繁忙/异常通过 `v2/health/live`、`v2/health/ready` 返回 200/503/500 区分 |

`httpsEnabled=true` 时还需 `tlsCaPath`(`security/ca/`)、`tlsCaFile`(`["ca.pem"]`)、`tlsCert`(`security/certs/server.pem`)、`tlsPk`(`security/keys/server.key.pem`，私钥长度 ≥3072) 等，以及内部接口/指标接口/KMC 密钥库（`kmcKsfMaster`、`kmcKsfStandby`）相关项。

**BackendConfig 关键项**：

| 字段 | 默认 | 必填 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backendName` | — | 必填 | 目前只支持 `"mindieservice_llm_engine"`（仅小写字母/下划线，不以下划线首尾） |
| `modelInstanceNumber` | `1` | 必填 | 模型实例数 [1,10]；单模型多机推理须为 1 |
| `npuDeviceIds` | `[[0,1,2,3]]` | 必填 | 用**芯片逻辑 ID**；未设 `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` 时用 `npu-smi info -m` 查询；多机场景该值无效 |
| `tokenizerProcessNumber` | `8` | 必填 | tokenizer 进程数 [1,32] |
| `multiNodesInferEnabled` | `false` | 选填 | 是否多机推理 |
| `multiNodesInferPort` | `1120` | 选填 | 跨机通信端口 |

**ModelDeployConfig / ModelConfig 关键项**：

| 字段 | 默认 | 必填 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxSeqLen` | `2560` | 必填 | 最大序列长度 |
| `maxInputTokenLen` | `2048` | 必填 | 输入 token 上限 [1,4194304]，实际取 `min(maxInputTokenLen, maxSeqLen-1)` |
| `truncation` | `0` | 选填 | `-1/true`=右截断；`0/false`=禁截断（超长报错）；`1`=左截断（**仅 qwen、deepseek 支持左截断**） |
| `modelName` | `"llama_65b"` | 必填 | **模型名，即请求里 `model` 字段要填的值**；长度 ≤256 |
| `modelWeightPath` | `/data/atb_testdata/weights/llama1-65b-safetensors` | 必填 | 权重路径；程序读该路径下 `config.json` 的 `torch_dtype`、`vocab_size` |
| `worldSize` | `4` | 必填 | 启用卡数，须与实际 NPU 数相等（多机/PD 分离场景规则不同） |
| `cpuMemSize` | `5`（GB） | 必填 | 单个 CPU 可用于 KV Cache 申请上限；仅 `maxPreemptCount=0` 时可为 0 |
| `npuMemSize` | `-1`（GB） | 必填 | `-1`=按可用显存自动分配；多模态模型不支持 `-1` |
| `backendType` | `"atb"` | 必填 | `atb`=加速库；`torch`=兼容 torch 框架 |
| `trustRemoteCode` | `false` | 选填 | 设为 true 有代码注入风险 |

**ScheduleConfig**（必填项含 `templateType`(`Standard`/`Mix`)、`templateName`(只能 `Standard_LLM`)、`cacheBlockSize`(128，须为 16 的倍数)、`maxPrefillBatchSize`(50)、`maxPrefillTokens`(8192，须 ≥ `maxInputTokenLen`)、`prefillTimeMsPerReq`(150)、`decodeTimeMsPerReq`(50)、`prefillPolicyType`/`decodePolicyType`(均只能 0)、`maxBatchSize`(200；Atlas 300I Duo 上限 2000)、`maxIterTimes`(512)、`maxPreemptCount`(0)、`maxQueueDelayMicroseconds`(5000)），选填 `maxFirstTokenWaitTime`(2500)、`maxN`(128)。

**按上述文档字段拼装的最小可用片段（非官方原文整体示例，仅用于说明需改哪些字段）**：

```jsonc
{
  "Version": "1.0.0",
  "ServerConfig": {
    "ipAddress": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 1025,
    "managementPort": 1026,
    "maxLinkNum": 300,
    "httpsEnabled": false,          // 仅内网调试；官方提示关闭 HTTPS 有安全风险
    "allowAllZeroIpListening": false,
    "inferMode": "standard",
    "openAiSupport": "vllm"
  },
  "BackendConfig": {
    "backendName": "mindieservice_llm_engine",
    "modelInstanceNumber": 1,
    "npuDeviceIds": [[0, 1, 2, 3]],
    "tokenizerProcessNumber": 8,
    "multiNodesInferEnabled": false,
    "ModelDeployConfig": {
      "maxSeqLen": 2560,
      "maxInputTokenLen": 2048,
      "truncation": 0,
      "ModelConfig": [
        {
          "modelInstanceType": "Standard",
          "modelName": "<对外暴露的模型名，请求 model 字段填它>",
          "modelWeightPath": "/path/to/weights",
          "worldSize": 4,
          "cpuMemSize": 5,
          "npuMemSize": -1,
          "backendType": "atb",
          "trustRemoteCode": false
        }
      ]
    },
    "ScheduleConfig": { /* 见上表，Standard_LLM 模板 */ }
  },
  "LogConfig": { "dynamicLogLevelValidHours": 2 }
}
```

### 5. 启动服务

来源：`https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/mindie/10RC3/mindieservice/servicedev/mindie_service0004.html`

默认监听 `https://127.0.0.1:1025`，可用 `config.json` 的 `ipAddress`、`port` 修改。

```bash
# （推荐）后台进程方式；关闭窗口进程仍保留
nohup ./bin/mindieservice_daemon > output.log 2>&1 &

# 或直接启动
./bin/mindieservice_daemon
```

成功回显：`Daemon start success!`（两种方式相同）

原文注意事项：
- `bin` 目录权限为 550（无写权限），但推理时算子会在当前目录生成 `kernel_meta`，需写权限，**因此不能直接在 bin 目录内启动 `mindieservice_daemon`**；应在有写权限的目录（如 `Ascend-mindie-server_<version>_linux_<arch>` 目录或其下自建临时目录）启动。
- `Ascend-cann-toolkit` 会在执行服务启动的目录生成 `kernel_meta_temp_xxxx` 目录（算子 cce 文件）。
- 切换用户后需先执行 `rm -f /dev/shm/*`，删除上一用户创建的共享文件，避免权限问题导致推理失败。

### 6. 验证服务

同源（RC3 启动服务页，HTTPS 示例）：

```bash
# 列出当前模型列表
curl -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-type: application/json" \
  --cacert ca.pem --cert client.pem --key client.key.pem \
  -X GET https://127.0.0.1:1025/v1/models
```

- `--cacert`：服务端证书的验签证书/根证书（`ca.pem`）
- `--cert`：客户端证书（`client.pem`）
- `--key`：客户端私钥（`client.key.pem`，未加密，建议加密）

若 `httpsEnabled=false`，去掉 TLS 参数用 http 调用（注意官方明确提示关闭 HTTPS 存在较高网络安全风险）。健康检查接口为 `v2/health/live`、`v2/health/ready`。

### 关于请求别名 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`

- 本轮检索到的官方文档中**未出现** `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 这一模型名；文档里明确提到的 DeepSeek 相关条目只有 **DeepSeek-V3.2**（“DeepSeek-V3.2 不支持 torch、torch_npu 2.1.0”）以及 `truncation` 支持左截断的 “deepseek” 模型类。因此无法给出该别名的官方 `modelType`/权重转换方式，`modelName` 只能按“你实际部署的权重名”填写（字符限制见上）。

仅凭已有知识（未检索），我可以给出下面这样的回答，并对不确定处标注：

**Triton Model Repository 布局（我记得的结构）**
```
model_repository/
└── <model_name>/
    ├── config.pbtxt
    ├── 1/
    │   └── model.plan        # TensorRT engine（或 model.onnx / model.py / model.pt）
    └── 2/
        └── model.plan
```
- 每个模型一个目录，目录名即模型名；其下是数字版本号目录（`1`、`2`…），版本号必须是数字。
- `config.pbtxt` 描述 backend/platform、`max_batch_size`、`input`/`output` 的 `name`/`dims`/`data_type`。
- TensorRT 的配置我印象中是 `platform: "tensorrt_plan"`，较新版本改成了 `backend: "tensorrt"`；`platform` 与 `backend` 二选一。**哪一版改用 `backend:` 我不确定。**

**TensorRT 部分**
- TensorRT backend 需要 `.plan` 引擎文件。引擎与构建时的 TensorRT 版本、CUDA/驱动、GPU 架构（compute capability）绑定，跨环境一般不通用，通常需在目标 GPU 上用 `trtexec` 或 Triton 自动生成。
- ONNX 可以让 Triton 自动转换：启动时不加 `--strict-model-config`（即 `--strict-model-config=false`），Triton 会尝试自动补全 config（`--model-config` 或 auto-complete）。**自动补全对 `dims`/动态 shape 的处理细节我不确定。**
- 动态 shape 需要 `optimization { }` 里的 profile（TensorRT `profile`/`dynamic_batching`）。Triton 侧我记得有 `dynamic_batching { }` 和 `instance_group`。

**起服务**
- 最小启动命令我印象是：
  ```
  tritonserver --model-repository=/models
  ```
- Docker 方式：
  ```
  docker run --gpus all --rm \
    -p8000:8000 -p8001:8001 -p8002:8002 \
    -v /host/models:/models \
    nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:<tag>-py3 \
    tritonserver --model-repository=/models
  ```
- 端口我记得是 8000=HTTP、8001=gRPC、8002=metrics（Prometheus）。
- 常用参数：`--model-control-mode=poll`（目录变更自动加载）、`--strict-model-config`、`--log-verbose`。

**我不确定 / 需外部核对的关键点**
1. `platform: "tensorrt_plan"` 与 `backend: "tensorrt"` 的适用范围与弃用时间线。
2. Triton 容器镜像当前最新 tag 与对应 TensorRT/CUDA 版本（生态 cuda）。
3. TensorRT backend 的 `optimization` / profile 字段在 `config.pbtxt` 中的确切写法。
4. 自动补全 config 的确切开关名与默认值。
5. 是否需要 `--allow-gpu-metrics`、`--grpc-port` 等确切默认值。
6. 官方文档当前 URL 结构（`user-guide/docs/...`）。

因此检索前的答案属于「有正确概念与方法骨架、但关键参数/版本需外部资料补充」。下面开始真实检索。

**标题**: Model Repository — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server

# Model Repository#

**Is this your first time setting up a model repository?** Check out these tutorials to begin your Triton journey!

The Triton Inference Server serves models from one or more model repositories that are specified when the server is started. While Triton is running, the models being served can be modified as described in Model Management.

## Repository Layout#

# Model Repository#
## Repository Layout#
These repository paths are specified when Triton is started using the `--model-repository` option. The `--model-repository` option can be specified multiple times to included models from multiple repositories. The directories and files that compose a model repository must follow a required layout. Assuming a repository path is specified as follows.

```
$ tritonserver --model-repository=<model-repository-path>
```

The corresponding repository layout must be:

```
  <model-repository-path>/
    <model-name>/
      [config.pbtxt]
      [<output-labels-file> ...]
      [configs]/
        [<custom-config-file> ...]
      <version>/
        <model-definition-file>
      <version>/
        <model-definition-file>
      ...
    <model-name>/
      [config.pbtxt]
      [<output-labels-file> ...]
      [configs]/
        [<custom-config-file> ...]
      <version>/
        <model-definition-file>
      <version>/
        <model-definition-file>
      ...
    ...
```

Within the top-level model repository directory there must be zero or more sub-directories. Each of the sub-directories contains the repository information for the corresponding model. The config.pbtxt file describes the model configuration for the model. For some models, config.pbtxt is required while for others it is optional. See Auto-Generated Model Configuration for more information.

# Model Repository#
## Repository Layout#
Each directory may include an optional sub-directory configs. Within the configs directory there must be zero or more with .pbtxt file extension. For more information about how the custom model configuration is handled by Triton see Custom Model Configuration.

Each directory must have at least one numeric sub-directory representing a version of the model. For more information about how the model versions are handled by Triton see Model Versions. Each model is executed by a specific backend. Within each version sub-directory there must be the files required by that backend. For example, models that use framework backends such as TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX and OpenVINO must provide the framework-specific model files.

## Model Repository Locations#

Triton can access models from one or more locally accessible file paths, from Google Cloud Storage, from Amazon S3, and from Azure Storage.

### Local File System#

For a locally accessible file-system the absolute path must be specified.

```
$ tritonserver --model-repository=/path/to/model/repository ...
```

[...]

### Cloud Storage with Credential file (Beta)#

# Model Repository#
## Model Repository Locations#
### Cloud Storage with Credential file (Beta)#
If the `TRITON_CLOUD_CREDENTIAL_PATH` environment variable is not set, the Cloud Storage with Environment variables will be used.

[...]

## Model Versions#

Each model can have one or more versions available in the model repository. Each version is stored in its own, numerically named, subdirectory where the name of the subdirectory corresponds to the version number of the model. The subdirectories that are not numerically named, or have names that start with the character “0” will be ignored. Each model configuration specifies a version policy that controls which of the versions in the model repository are made available by Triton at any given time.

## Model Files#

The contents of each model version sub-directory is determined by the type of the model and the requirements of the backend that supports the model.

### TensorRT Models#

A TensorRT model definition is called a *Plan*. A TensorRT Plan is a single file that by default must be named model.plan. This default name can be overridden using the *default_model_filename* property in the model configuration.

A TensorRT Plan is specific to a GPU’s CUDA Compute Capability. As a result, TensorRT models will need to set the *cc_model_filenames* property in the model configuration to associate each Plan file with the corresponding Compute Capability.

A minimal model repository for a TensorRT model is:

```
  <model-repository-path>/
    <model-name>/
      config.pbtxt
      1/
        model.plan
```

### ONNX Models#

An ONNX model is a single file or a directory containing multiple files. By default the file or directory must be named model.onnx. This default name can be overridden using the *default_model_filename* property in the model configuration.

Triton supports all ONNX models that are supported by the version of ONNX Runtime being used by Triton. Models will not be supported if they use a stale ONNX opset version or contain operators with unsupported types.

A minimal model repository for a ONNX model contained in a single file is:

```
  <model-repository-path>/
    <model-name>/
      config.pbtxt
      1/
        model.onnx
```

An ONNX model composed from multiple files must be contained in a directory. By default this directory must be named model.onnx but can be overridden using the *default_model_filename* property in the model configuration. The main model file within this directory must be named model.onnx. A minimal model repository for a ONNX model contained in a directory is:

```
  <model-repository-path>/
    <model-name>/
      config.pbtxt
      1/
        model.onnx/
           model.onnx
           <other model files>
```

### TorchScript Models#

An TorchScript model is a single file that by default must be named model.pt. This default name can be overridden using the *default_model_filename* property in the model configuration. It is possible that some models traced with different versions of PyTorch may not be supported by Triton due to changes in the underlying opset.

A minimal model repository for a TorchScript model is:

```
  <model-repository-path>/
    <model-name>/
      config.pbtxt
      1/
        model.pt
```

[...]

### Python Models#

The Python backend allows you to run Python code as a model within Triton. By default the Python script must be named model.py but this default name can be overridden using the *default_model_filename* property in the model configuration.

A minimal model repository for a Python model is:

```
  <model-repository-path>/
    <model-name>/
      config.pbtxt
      1/
        model.py
```

# NVIDIA Triton Inference Server — Model Configuration: Extracted Structure & Content

## Summary of Findings

The provided document is the **"Model Configuration"** chapter of the NVIDIA Triton Inference Server user guide. It covers how to write `config.pbtxt` files using the **ModelConfig protobuf**.

**Important notes on scope and truncation:**
- The document is **truncated/partial** relative to the user's full request. Several requested topics are **NOT present** in this content:
  - ❌ `default_model_filename` — mentioned only in passing ("Similar to the `default_model_filename` field...") but not defined here.
  - ❌ `dynamic_batching` — referenced via links and default-behavior discussion, but no dedicated config section shown.
  - ❌ **TensorRT optimization** (`optimization` / `ModelOptimizationPolicy`) — only a brief pointer to external docs; **no optimization profiles section is present**.
- Most requested fields (platform/backend, max_batch_size, inputs/outputs, version_policy, cc_model_filenames, instance_group) **are covered**.

---

## 1. Backend vs Platform Field

**Source section:** *Minimal Model Configuration → Name, Platform and Backend*

- A minimal configuration **must specify the `platform` and/or `backend` properties**, the `max_batch_size`, and the input/output tensors.
- The `name` property is **optional**. If omitted, it defaults to the name of the model repository directory. If specified, it **must match** the repository directory name.
- Required values for `platform` and `backend` are defined in the external *backend documentation*.

**Example (uses `platform`):**
```protobuf
platform: "tensorrt_plan"
```
> For custom backends: your `config.pbtxt` must include a `backend` field **or** your model name must be in the form `<model_name>.<backend_name>`.

---

## 2. max_batch_size (Maximum Batch Size)

**Source section:** *Maximum Batch Size*

- Indicates the **maximum batch size** the model supports for Triton-exploitable batching.
- If the model's batch dimension is the **first dimension** and all inputs/outputs carry it, Triton's **dynamic batcher** or **sequence batcher** can auto-batch. Set `max_batch_size` ≥ 1.
- **Models that don't support batching → `max_batch_size` must be 0.**

**Shape derivation:**
- If `max_batch_size` > 0: full shape = `[ -1 ] + dims`
- If `max_batch_size` == 0: full shape = `dims`

**Default max batch size (auto-complete only):**
- Set via `--backend-config=default-max-batch-size=<int>`; **default value is 4**.
- Applies to backends using auto-complete config: **Onnxruntime** and **TensorRT**.
  - *Onnxruntime:* uses the default value and enables dynamic batching.
  - *TensorRT:* stores max batch size explicitly and does **not** use the default-max-batch-size param; however if `max_batch_size > 1` and no scheduler is provided, the dynamic batch scheduler is enabled.
- If `max_batch_size > 1` and no scheduler is specified, `dynamic_batching` config will be set automatically.

---

## 3. Input/Output Tensors: dims & data_type

**Source section:** *Inputs and Outputs*

- Each input/output must specify a **name, datatype, and shape**.
- **Shape rank must be ≥ 1** — empty shape `[ ]` is **not allowed**.
- Variable-size dimensions can be listed as `-1` (treated as any size ≥ 0).
- The `reshape` property is required when request/response shapes differ from the model's expected/produced shapes.
- `allow_ragged_batch` flags a **ragged input** (used with dynamic batcher).

### Minimal config example
```protobuf
platform: "tensorrt_plan"
max_batch_size: 8
input [
  {
    name: "input0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  },
  {
    name: "input1"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  }
]
output [
  {
    name: "output0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  }
]
```

### Dims example with max_batch_size
```protobuf
platform: "tensorrt_plan"
max_batch_size: 8
input [
  {
    name: "input0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  }
]
output [
  {
    name: "output0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 4 ]
  }
]
```
- `input0` shape → `[-1, 16]`; `output0` shape → `[-1, 4]`

### Dims example with max_batch_size = 0
```protobuf
platform: "tensorrt_plan"
max_batch_size: 0
input [
  {
    name: "input0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  }
]
output [
  {
    name: "output0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 4 ]
  }
]
```
- `input0` shape → `[16]`; `output0` shape → `[4]`

### datatype mapping table (Model Config ↔ TensorRT / ONNX Runtime / PyTorch / API / NumPy)

| Model Config | TensorRT | ONNX Runtime | PyTorch | API | NumPy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TYPE_BOOL | kBOOL | BOOL | kBool | BOOL | bool |
| TYPE_UINT8 | kUINT8 | UINT8 | kByte | UINT8 | uint8 |
| TYPE_UINT16 | — | UINT16 | — | UINT16 | uint16 |
| TYPE_UINT32 | — | UINT32 | — | UINT32 | uint32 |
| TYPE_UINT64 | — | UINT64 | — | UINT64 | uint64 |
| TYPE_INT8 | kINT8 | INT8 | kChar | INT8 | int8 |
| TYPE_INT16 | — | INT16 | kShort | INT16 | int16 |
| TYPE_INT32 | kINT32 | INT32 | kInt | INT32 | int32 |
| TYPE_INT64 | kINT64 | INT64 | kLong | INT64 | int64 |
| TYPE_FP16 | kHALF | FLOAT16 | — | FP16 | float16 |
| TYPE_FP32 | kFLOAT | FLOAT | kFloat | FP32 | float32 |
| TYPE_FP64 | — | DOUBLE | kDouble | FP64 | float64 |
| TYPE_STRING | — | STRING | — | BYTES | dtype(object) |
| TYPE_BF16 | kBF16 | — | — | BF16 | — |

Prefixes/namespaces:
- TensorRT: `nvinfer1::DataType` (e.g., `nvinfer1::DataType::kFLOAT`)
- ONNX Runtime: prefixed `ONNX_TENSOR_ELEMENT_DATA_TYPE_` (e.g., `..._FLOAT`)
- PyTorch: `torch::` namespace (e.g., `torch::kFloat`)
- NumPy: `numpy.` module (e.g., `numpy.float32`)

### PyTorch backend naming conventions
- If input is **not** a Dictionary of Tensors, names must mirror `forward()` argument names (e.g., `forward(self, input0, input1)`).
- Alternative: `<name>__<index>` (e.g., `INPUT__0`, `OUTPUT__1`).
- If inputs/outputs don't share one convention, strict ordering from the config is enforced.
- **Dictionary of Tensors input** (single dict input only): input names map to dict keys (e.g., `"A"`, `"B"`), **not** `<name>__<index>`.

---

## 4. version_policy

**Source section:** *Version Policy*

- `ModelVersionPolicy` options:
  - **All:** `version_policy: { all: {}}`
  - **Latest:** `version_policy: { latest: { num_versions: 2}}` (numerically greatest version numbers)
  - **Specific:** `version_policy: { specific: { versions: [1,3]}}`
- **Default (if unspecified):** Latest with n=1 → only the most recent version available.

```protobuf
platform: "tensorrt_plan"
max_batch_size: 8
input [
  {
    name: "input0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  },
  {
    name: "input1"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  }
]
output [
  {
    name: "output0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 16 ]
  }
]
version_policy: { all { }}
```

---

## 5. default_model_filename

- **Not documented in this content.** Only referenced indirectly: *"Similar to the `default_model_filename` field, you can optionally specify the `cc_model_filenames` field..."* — no definition or example provided here. (Truncation — external protobuf docs required.)

---

## 6. cc_model_filenames (CUDA Compute Capability mapping)

**Source section:** *CUDA Compute Capability*

- Maps GPU CUDA Compute Capability → model filename at load time (useful for TensorRT, generally tied to a specific CC).

```protobuf
cc_model_filenames [
  {
    key: "7.5"
    value: "resnet50_T4.plan"
  },
  {
    key: "8.0"
    value: "resnet50_A100.plan"
  }
]
```

---

## 7. instance_group

**Source section:** *Instance Groups* (+ sub-sections)

- `ModelInstanceGroup` controls number of execution instances and compute resource.
- **Default:** a single execution instance per available GPU.

**Multiple instances per GPU:**
```protobuf
instance_group [
  {
    count: 2
    kind: KIND_GPU
  }
]
```

**Per-GPU placement:**
```protobuf
instance_group [
  {
    count: 1
    kind: KIND_GPU
    gpus: [ 0 ]
  },
  {
    count: 2
    kind: KIND_GPU
    gpus: [ 1, 2 ]
  }
]
```

**CPU instances:**
```protobuf
instance_group [
  {
    count: 2
    kind: KIND_CPU
  }
]
```
- If no `count` for KIND_CPU: default = **2** for Onnxruntime; **1** for all other backends.

**Host policy:**
```protobuf
instance_group [
  {
    count: 2
    kind: KIND_CPU
    host_policy: "policy_0"
  }
]
```
- Default host policy derives from device kind: `KIND_CPU`→`cpu`, `KIND_MODEL`→`model`, `KIND_GPU`→`gpu_<gpu_id>`.

**Rate limiter config (within instance_group):**
```protobuf
instance_group [
  {
    count: 1
    kind: KIND_GPU
    gpus: [ 0, 1, 2 ]
    rate_limiter {
      resources [
        {
          name: "R1"
          count: 4
        },
        {
          name: "R2"
          global: True
          count: 2
        }
      ]
      priority: 2
    }
  }
]
```
- `resources`: `name`, `count` (copies required), `global` (per-device vs system-shared). Cannot use same name both global and non-global.
- `priority`: weighting — priority 2 → ½ the scheduling chances of priority 1.
- Rate limiter config is ignored if rate limiting is off.

**Ensemble models:** `instance_group` **cannot** be set on an ensemble itself (no physical instance). Each composing model can set its own in its config.

---

## 8. dynamic_batching

**Not a dedicated section in this content (truncated).** Referenced only via:
- *Maximum Batch Size* and *Default Max Batch Size* sections: dynamic batcher linkage to batching models.
- Auto-enable rule: if `max_batch_size > 1` and no scheduler provided → `dynamic_batching` config set.
- External link to the *batcher* documentation.

---

## 9. TensorRT Backend-Specific Config (optimization, profiles)

**Only a brief pointer is present — the detailed content is truncated/absent.**

**Source section:** *Optimization Policy*
> The `ModelOptimizationPolicy` property is used to specify optimization and prioritization settings for a model. These settings control if/how a model is optimized by the backend and how it is scheduled and executed by Triton.

- **Full details deferred to:** *ModelConfig protobuf* and *optimization* documentation (external links).
- **No optimization profiles (`optimization { ... }`) examples appear in this document.**

**Other TensorRT-relevant items present in this content:**
- **Shape Tensors:** `is_shape_tensor: true` (**only TensorRT supports shape tensors**).
  ```protobuf
  name: "myshapetensormodel"
  platform: "tensorrt_plan"
  max_batch_size: 8
  input [
    {
      name: "input0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 1 , 3]
    },
    {
      name: "input1"
      data_type: TYPE_INT32
      dims: [ 2 ]
      is_shape_tensor: true
    }
  ]
  output [
    {
      name: "output0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 1 , 3]
    }
  ]
  ```
  - For shape tensors, batching occurs at the **first shape value** (not the implicit batch dim).
  - `input1` delivered as shape `[3]` (not `[2]` as in config); Triton accumulates shape values for the batch dimension.
  - Only TensorRT supports shape tensors.

- **Non-Linear I/O Formats:** `is_non_linear_format_io: true` (**only TensorRT supports this**).
  ```protobuf
  name: "mytensorrtmodel"
  platform: "tensorrt_plan"
  max_batch_size: 8
  input [
    {
      name: "INPUT0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP16
      dims: [ 3,224,224 ]
      is_non_linear_format_io: true
    },
    {
      name: "INPUT1"
      data_type: TYPE_FP16
      dims: [ 3,224,224 ]
      is_non_linear_format_io: true
    }
  ]
  output [
    {
      name: "OUTPUT0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP16
      dims: [ 1,3 ]
     }
  ]
  ```

- **`cc_model_filenames`** (see §6) is "particularly useful for TensorRT models."

---

## Additional Covered Sections (bonus)

- **Model Transaction Policy (`model_transaction_policy`)** → `decoupled` (bool, default false). Decoupled = response count may differ from request count and may be out-of-order.
- **Auto-Generated Model Configuration:**
  - Auto-complete can be disabled via `--disable-auto-complete-config` (but `instance_group` defaults are still filled in).
  - Auto-derived for most **TensorRT**, **ONNX**, **OpenVINO** models.
  - **Python models:** implement `auto_complete_config` using `set_max_batch_size`, `add_input`, `add_output`.
  - **All other model types MUST provide a config file.**
  - Custom backends populate via `TRITONBACKEND_ModelSetConfig`. Only inputs/outputs, max_batch_size, and dynamic batching settable by backend.
  - Inspect generated config: `curl localhost:8000/v2/models/<model name>/config`
- **Custom Model Configuration:** `--model-config-name=h100` → searches `<model>/configs/h100.pbtxt`, falls back to `config.pbtxt` or auto-generated. Works with `Explicit`/`Poll` control modes. No spaces allowed in name. (Three tree examples given.)
- **Reshape:**
  ```protobuf
  input [
    {
      name: "in"
      dims: [ 1 ]
      reshape: { shape: [ ] }
    }
  ]
  ```
  ```protobuf
  output [
    {
      name: "in"
      dims: [ 1 ]
      reshape: { shape: [ ] }
    }
  ]
  ```
- **Model Warmup (`ModelWarmup`):** defines inference requests to warm each instance; model not "ready" until warmup completes; varies by backend; reduces responsiveness to model updates.
- **Response Cache:**
  ```protobuf
  response_cache {
    enable: true
  }
  ```
  Requires `--cache-config` at server start.

---

## Truncation Notice

The following requested items are **missing or only stubbed** in this document:
- `default_model_filename` — referenced, not defined.
- `dynamic_batching` — no dedicated section.
- TensorRT **optimization** and **optimization profiles** — only a one-paragraph pointer to external protobuf/optimization docs.

To fully answer on those topics, the **ModelConfig protobuf** (`model_config.proto`) and the **Optimization** user-guide page would be required.

**标题**: Quickstart — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server

Back to top

# Quickstart[#](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/getting_started/quickstart.html#quickstart "Link to this heading")

**New to Triton Inference Server and want do just deploy your model quickly?** Make use of [these tutorials](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/tutorials/README.html#quick-deploy) to begin your Triton journey!

The Triton Inference Server is available as [buildable source code](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/customization_guide/build.html), but the easiest way to install and run Triton is to use the pre-built Docker image available from the [NVIDIA GPU Cloud (NGC)](https://ngc.nvidia.com).

Launching and maintaining Triton Inference Server revolves around the use of building model repositories. This tutorial will cover:

- Creating a Model Repository
- Launching Triton
- Send an Inference Request

## Create A Model Repository[#](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/getting_started/quickstart.html#create-a-model-repository "Link to this heading")

The [model repository](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/user_guide/model_repository.html) is the directory where you place the models that you want Triton to serve. An example model repository is included in the [docs/examples/model_repository](https://github.com/triton-inference-server/server/blob/main/docs/examples/model_repository). Before using the repository, you must fetch any missing model definition files from their public model zoos via the provided script.

```
$ cd docs/examples
$ ./fetch_models.sh
```

## Launch Triton[#](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/getting_started/quickstart.html#launch-triton "Link to this heading")

Triton is optimized to provide the best inferencing performance by using GPUs, but it can also work on CPU-only systems. In both cases you can use the same Triton Docker image.

### Run on System with GPUs[#](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/getting_started/quickstart.html#run-on-system-with-gpus "Link to this heading")

Use the following command to run Triton with the example model repository you just created. The [NVIDIA Container Toolkit](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker) must be installed for Docker to recognize the GPU(s). The –gpus=1 flag indicates that 1 system GPU should be made available to Triton for inferencing.

```
$ docker run --gpus=1 --rm -p8000:8000 -p8001:8001 -p8002:8002 -v/full/path/to/docs/examples/model_repository:/models nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:<xx.yy>-py3 tritonserver --model-repository=/models
```

Where <xx.yy> is the version of Triton that you want to use (and pulled above). After you start Triton you will see output on the console showing the server starting up and loading the model. When you see output like the following, Triton is ready to accept inference requests.

```
+----------------------+---------+--------+
| Model                | Version | Status |
+----------------------+---------+--------+
| <model_name>         | <v>     | READY  |
| ..                   | .       | ..     |
| ..                   | .       | ..     |
+----------------------+---------+--------+
...
...
...
I1002 21:58:57.891440 62 grpc_server.cc:3914] Started GRPCInferenceService at 0.0.0.0:8001
I1002 21:58:57.893177 62 http_server.cc:2717] Started HTTPService at 0.0.0.0:8000
I1002 21:58:57.935518 62 http_server.cc:2736] Started Metrics Service at 0.0.0.0:8002
```

All the models should show “READY” status to indicate that they loaded correctly. If a model fails to load the status will report the failure and a reason for the failure. If your model is not displayed in the table check the path to the model repository and your CUDA drivers.

### Run on CPU-Only System[#](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/getting_started/quickstart.html#run-on-cpu-only-system "Link to this heading")

On a system without GPUs, Triton should be run without using the –gpus flag to Docker, but is otherwise identical to what is described above.

```
$ docker run --rm -p8000:8000 -p8001:8001 -p8002:8002 -v/full/path/to/docs/examples/model_repository:/models nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:<xx.yy>-py3 tritonserver --model-repository=/models
```

Because the –gpus flag is not used, a GPU is not available and Triton will therefore be unable to load any model configuration that requires a GPU.

### Verify Triton Is Running Correctly[#](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/getting_started/quickstart.html#verify-triton-is-running-correctly "Link to this heading")

Use Triton’s *ready* endpoint to verify that the server and the models are ready for inference. From the host system use curl to access the HTTP endpoint that indicates server status.

```
$ curl -v localhost:8000/v2/health/ready
...
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Length: 0
< Content-Type: text/plain
```

The HTTP request returns status 200 if Triton is ready and non-200 if it is not ready.

## Send an Inference Request[#](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/triton-inference-server/user-guide/docs/getting_started/quickstart.html#send-an-inference-request "Link to this heading")

Use docker pull to get the client libraries and examples image from NGC.

```
$ docker pull nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:<xx.yy>-py3-sdk
```

Where <xx.yy> is the version that you want to pull. Run the client image.

```
$ docker run -it --rm --net=host nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:<xx.yy>-py3-sdk
```

From within the nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:<xx.yy>-py3-sdk image, run the example image-client application to perform image classification using the example densenet_onnx model.

To send a request for the densenet_onnx model use an image from the /workspace/images directory. In this case we ask for the top 3 classifications.

```
$ /workspace/install/bin/image_client -m densenet_onnx -c 3 -s INCEPTION /workspace/images/mug.jpg
Request 0, batch size 1
Image '/workspace/images/mug.jpg':
    15.346230 (504) = COFFEE MUG
    13.224326 (968) = CUP
    10.422965 (505) = COFFEEPOT
```

**标题**: Optimization — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server

# Optimization#

# Optimization#
The Triton Inference Server has many features that you can use to decrease latency and increase throughput for your model. This section discusses these features and demonstrates how you can use them to improve the performance of your model. As a prerequisite you should follow the QuickStart to get Triton and client examples running with the example model repository.

This section focuses on understanding latency and throughput tradeoffs for a single model. The Model Analyzer section describes a tool that helps you understand the GPU memory utilization of your models so you can decide how to best run multiple models on a single GPU.

Unless you already have a client application suitable for measuring the performance of your model on Triton, you should familiarize yourself with Performance Analyzer. The Performance Analyzer is an essential tool for optimizing your model’s performance.

As a running example demonstrating the optimization features and options, we will use a ONNX Inception model that you can obtain by following the QuickStart. As a baseline we use perf_analyzer to determine the performance of the model using a basic model configuration that does not enable any performance features.

[...]

## Optimization Settings#

For most models, the Triton feature that provides the largest performance improvement is dynamic batching. This example sheds more light on conceptual details. If your model does not support batching then you can skip ahead to Model Instances.

[...]

### Dynamic Batcher#

# Optimization#
## Optimization Settings#
### Dynamic Batcher#
Instead of having perf_analyzer collect data for a range of request concurrency values we can instead use a couple of simple rules that typically applies when perf_analyzer is running on the same system as Triton. The first rule is that for minimum latency set the request concurrency to 1 and disable the dynamic batcher and use only 1 model instance. The second rule is that for maximum throughput set the request concurrency to be `2 * <maximum batch size> * <model instance count>`. We will discuss model instances below, for now we are working with one model instance. So for maximum-batch-size 4 we want to run perf_analyzer with request concurrency of `2 * 4 * 1 = 8`.

```
$ perf_analyzer -m inception_onnx --percentile=95 --concurrency-range 8
...
Inferences/Second vs. Client p95 Batch Latency
Concurrency: 8, throughput: 267.8 infer/sec, latency 35590 usec
```

[...]

### Model Instances#

# Optimization#
## Optimization Settings#
### Model Instances#
In this case having two instances of the model increases throughput from about 73 inference per second to about 110 inferences per second compared with one instance.

It is possible to enable both the dynamic batcher and multiple model instances, for example, change the model configuration file to include the following.

```
dynamic_batching { }
instance_group [ { count: 2 }]
```

When we run perf_analyzer with the same options used for just the dynamic batcher above.

```
$ perf_analyzer -m inception_onnx --percentile=95 --concurrency-range 16
...
Inferences/Second vs. Client p95 Batch Latency
Concurrency: 16, throughput: 289.6 infer/sec, latency 59817 usec
```

We see that two instances does not improve throughput much while increasing latency, compared with just using the dynamic batcher and one instance. This occurs because for this model the dynamic batcher alone is capable of fully utilizing the GPU and so adding additional model instances does not provide any performance advantage. In general the benefit of the dynamic batcher and multiple instances is model specific, so you should experiment with perf_analyzer to determine the settings that best satisfy your throughput and latency requirements.

## Framework-Specific Optimization#

Triton has several optimization settings that apply to only a subset of the supported model frameworks. These optimization settings are controlled by the model configuration optimization policy. Visit this guide for an end to end discussion.

### ONNX with TensorRT Optimization (ORT-TRT)#

# Optimization#
## Framework-Specific Optimization#
### ONNX with TensorRT Optimization (ORT-TRT)#
One especially powerful optimization is to use TensorRT in conjunction with an ONNX model. As an example of TensorRT optimization applied to an ONNX model, we will use an ONNX DenseNet model that you can obtain by following QuickStart. As a baseline we use perf_analyzer to determine the performance of the model using a basic model configuration that does not enable any performance features.

```
$ perf_analyzer -m densenet_onnx --percentile=95 --concurrency-range 1:4
...
Inferences/Second vs. Client p95 Batch Latency
Concurrency: 1, 113.2 infer/sec, latency 8939 usec
Concurrency: 2, 138.2 infer/sec, latency 14548 usec
Concurrency: 3, 137.2 infer/sec, latency 21947 usec
Concurrency: 4, 136.8 infer/sec, latency 29661 usec
```

To enable TensorRT optimization for the model: stop Triton, add the following lines to the end of the model configuration file, and then restart Triton.

```
optimization { execution_accelerators {
  gpu_execution_accelerator : [ {
    name : "tensorrt"
    parameters { key: "precision_mode" value: "FP16" }
    parameters { key: "max_workspace_size_bytes" value: "1073741824" }
    }]
}}
```

As Triton starts you should check the console output and wait until Triton prints the “Staring endpoints” message. ONNX model loading can be significantly slower when TensorRT optimization is enabled. In production you can use model warmup to avoid this model startup/optimization slowdown. Now run perf_analyzer using the same options as for the baseline.

# Optimization#
## Framework-Specific Optimization#
### ONNX with TensorRT Optimization (ORT-TRT)#
```
$ perf_analyzer -m densenet_onnx --percentile=95 --concurrency-range 1:4
...
Inferences/Second vs. Client p95 Batch Latency
Concurrency: 1, 190.6 infer/sec, latency 5384 usec
Concurrency: 2, 273.8 infer/sec, latency 7347 usec
Concurrency: 3, 272.2 infer/sec, latency 11046 usec
Concurrency: 4, 266.8 infer/sec, latency 15089 usec
```

The TensorRT optimization provided 2x throughput improvement while cutting latency in half. The benefit provided by TensorRT will vary based on the model, but in general it can provide significant performance improvement.

# TensorRT Backend

The Triton backend for [TensorRT](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT).
You can learn more about Triton backends in the [backend
repo](https://github.com/triton-inference-server/backend). Ask
questions or report problems on the [issues
page](https://github.com/triton-inference-server/server/issues).
This backend is designed to run a serialized [TensorRT engine](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt/developer-guide/index.html#build_engine_c)
models using the TensorRT C++ API.

Where can I ask general questions about Triton and Triton backends?
Be sure to read all the information below as well as the [general
Triton documentation](https://github.com/triton-inference-server/server#triton-inference-server)
available in the main [server](https://github.com/triton-inference-server/server)
repo. If you don't find your answer there you can ask questions on the
main Triton [issues page](https://github.com/triton-inference-server/server/issues).

## Command-line Options

The command-line options configure properties of the TensorRT
backend that are then applied to all models that use the backend.

Below is an example of how to specify the backend config and the full list of
options.

##### --backend-config=tensorrt,coalesce-request-input=\<boolean\>,plugins="/path/plugin1.so;/path2/plugin2.so,version-compatible=true"

* The `coalesce-request-input` flag instructs TensorRT to consider the requests' inputs with the same name as
one contiguous buffer if their memory addresses align with each other.
This option should only be enabled if all requests' input tensors are allocated
from the same memory region. The default value is false.

* The `execution-policy` flag instructs TensorRT backend to execute the model with
different Triton execution policies (see `TRITONBACKEND_ExecutionPolicy`
for detail). Currently the following values are accepted:
  * `DEVICE_BLOCKING`: corresponds to `TRITONBACKEND_EXECUTION_DEVICE_BLOCKING`,
  this option can be set to avoid possible CUDA contention from launching
  many kernels from multiple threads.
  * `BLOCKING`: corresponds to `TRITONBACKEND_EXECUTION_BLOCKING`, this option
  can be set to overlap the host thread workload between model instances.

* The `plugins` flag provides a way to load any custom TensorRT plugins that your models rely on. If you have
multiple plugins to load, use a semicolon as the delimiter.

* The `version-compatible` flag enables the loading of version-compatible TensorRT models where the version of
TensorRT used for building does not matching the engine version used by Triton. You must trust the models
loaded in this mode, as version-compatible models include a lean runtime which gets deserialized and executed
by Triton. You can find more information in the TensorRT documentation
[here](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/tensorrt/developer-guide/index.html#version-compat).
The default value is false.


## Build the TensorRT Backend

Appropriate version of TensorRT must be installed on the system. Check the support matrix to find the correct version of TensorRT to be installed.

```
$ mkdir build
$ cd build
$ cmake -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX:PATH=`pwd`/install ..
$ make install
```

The following required Triton repositories will be pulled and used in
the build. By default the "main" branch/tag will be used for each repo
but the listed CMake argument can be used to override.

* triton-inference-server/backend: -DTRITON_BACKEND_REPO_TAG=[tag]
* triton-inference-server/core: -DTRITON_CORE_REPO_TAG=[tag]
* triton-inference-server/common: -DTRITON_COMMON_REPO_TAG=[tag]

## Parameters

Triton exposes some flags to control the execution mode of the TensorRT models through
the Parameters section of the model's `config.pbtxt` file.

### execution_context_allocation_strategy

Different memory allocation behaviors for IExecutionContext. IExecutionContext requires a block of device memory for internal activation tensors during inference. The user can let the execution context manage the memory in various ways. Current options are "STATIC" (default) and "ON_PROFILE_CHANGE".

* "STATIC": Default static allocation with the maximum size across all profiles.
* "ON_PROFILE_CHANGE": Reallocate for a profile when it's selected.

```
parameters: {
  key: "execution_context_allocation_strategy"
  value: {
    string_value: "STATIC"
  }
}
```
````

## 把模型部署为 Triton 推理服务（Triton Inference Server + TensorRT, CUDA）——检索后完整答案

以下内容均来自本轮实际抓取的官方页面；未取到的部分单独标注。

### 1. Model Repository 目录布局（官方：model_repository.html）

`--model-repository` 在启动时指定，可指定多次。要求的布局：

```
<model-repository-path>/
  <model-name>/
    [config.pbtxt]
    [<output-labels-file> ...]
    [configs]/
      [<custom-config-file> ...]
    <version>/                      # 版本目录必须是数字，且不能以 "0" 开头
      <model-definition-file>
    <version>/
      <model-definition-file>
    ...
```

- 每个模型目录下**至少要有一个数字版本子目录**；非数字或以 `0` 开头命名的目录会被忽略。
- 每个模型由特定 backend 执行，版本子目录里必须放该 backend 需要的模型文件。
- 版本策略由 config 里的 `version_policy` 控制。

**TensorRT 模型的最小仓库**（官方原文）：

```
<model-repository-path>/
  <model-name>/
    config.pbtxt
    1/
      model.plan
```

- TensorRT 的模型定义叫 **Plan**，默认文件名必须是 `model.plan`，可用 `default_model_filename` 覆盖。
- Plan **与 GPU 的 CUDA Compute Capability 绑定**，因此 TensorRT 模型需用 `cc_model_filenames` 把每个 plan 关联到对应算力版本。

### 2. config.pbtxt（TensorRT backend）

最小配置必须含 `platform` 和/或 `backend`、`max_batch_size`、输入/输出张量。官方当前 `model_configuration.html` 仍使用：

```protobuf
platform: "tensorrt_plan"
max_batch_size: 8
input [
  { name: "input0" data_type: TYPE_FP32 dims: [ 16 ] },
  { name: "input1" data_type: TYPE_FP32 dims: [ 16 ] }
]
output [
  { name: "output0" data_type: TYPE_FP32 dims: [ 16 ] }
]
```

要点（均有官方正文支持）：
- `name` 可省略，省略时默认取模型仓库目录名；若显式写出则必须与目录名一致。
- `max_batch_size`：≥1 表示支持 Triton 批处理；不支持批处理必须写 `0`。完整 shape：`max_batch_size>0` 时 `[-1]+dims`，否则就是 `dims`。
- 每个 input/output 必须给 `name`/`data_type`/`dims`；`dims` 秩必须 ≥1（不允许空 `[]`）；变长维用 `-1`。
- `version_policy`：`{ all {} }` / `{ latest { num_versions: 2 } }` / `{ specific { versions: [1,3] } }`；不写默认 Latest n=1。
- 数据类型映射（Model Config ↔ TensorRT）：`TYPE_FP32→kFLOAT`、`TYPE_FP16→kHALF`、`TYPE_INT8→kINT8`、`TYPE_INT32→kINT32`、`TYPE_BOOL→kBOOL`、`TYPE_BF16→kBF16`（TensorRT 无 UINT8/UINT16/UINT32/UINT64/FLOAT64/STRING）。
- TensorRT 专属：`is_shape_tensor: true`、`is_non_linear_format_io: true`（官方注明仅 TensorRT 支持）；`cc_model_filenames` 示例：

```protobuf
cc_model_filenames [
  { key: "7.5" value: "resnet50_T4.plan" },
  { key: "8.0" value: "resnet50_A100.plan" }
]
```

**实例与批处理**（官方 optimization.html）：

```protobuf
dynamic_batching { }
instance_group [ { count: 2 }]
```

另有官方示例把 `instance_group` 写成 `{ count: 1 kind: KIND_GPU gpus: [ 0 ] }`；KIND_CPU 未写 count 时默认 2（Onnxruntime）/1（其他 backend）。

**自动补全 config**：TensorRT、ONNX、OpenVINO 多数模型可自动生成 config，可用 `--disable-auto-complete-config` 关闭；生成的 config 可用 `curl localhost:8000/v2/models/<model>/config` 查看。其他模型类型必须自带 config。

**TensorRT backend 参数**（官方 tensorrt_backend README，本次仅取回前半部分）：

```
--backend-config=tensorrt,coalesce-request-input=<bool>,plugins="/path/plugin1.so;...",version-compatible=true
```
- `execution-policy`：`DEVICE_BLOCKING` / `BLOCKING`
- `version-compatible=true`：允许加载与 Triton 所用 TensorRT 版本不一致的 version-compatible 引擎（需信任模型）
- `parameters` 节可设 `execution_context_allocation_strategy`：`STATIC`(默认) / `ON_PROFILE_CHANGE`

### 3. 起服务（官方 quickstart.html）

```bash
docker run --gpus=1 --rm -p8000:8000 -p8001:8001 -p8002:8002 \
  -v/full/path/to/model_repository:/models \
  nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:<xx.yy>-py3 \
  tritonserver --model-repository=/models
```

- `<xx.yy>` 为要使用的 Triton 版本；须安装 NVIDIA Container Toolkit 才能让 Docker 识别 GPU。
- 端口（官方日志原文）：gRPC `0.0.0.0:8001`、HTTP `0.0.0.0:8000`、Metrics `0.0.0.0:8002`。
- 就绪检查：`curl -v localhost:8000/v2/health/ready`，返回 `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` 即就绪。
- 启动后控制台会打印模型状态表（`READY` 表示加载成功；失败会给出原因）。
- CPU-only：去掉 `--gpus` 即可，其余相同。

### 4. ONNX → TensorRT 加速（ORT-TRT，官方 optimization.html）

若走 ONNX Runtime + TensorRT 而非原生 plan，在 config 末尾加：

```protobuf
optimization { execution_accelerators {
  gpu_execution_accelerator : [ {
    name : "tensorrt"
    parameters { key: "precision_mode" value: "FP16" }
    parameters { key: "max_workspace_size_bytes" value: "1073741824" }
    }]
}}
```

官方说明：开启后 ONNX 模型加载会明显变慢，生产可用 model warmup 缓解；示例中吞吐约 2×、延迟约减半。

### 5. 版本 / 定版相关（部分有据）
- TensorRT Plan 与 CUDA Compute Capability 绑定 → 需 `cc_model_filenames`（官方明确）。
- `version-compatible` 用于缓解构建/运行 TensorRT 版本不一致（官方 README）。
- 容器版本 `<xx.yy>-py3`、SDK 侧 `<xx.yy>-py3-sdk`（官方 quickstart 占位符，未给具体号）。

prior.text:
仅凭已有知识，我可以这样回答该任务：

## 1. TensorRT 侧的动态 shape（Optimization Profile）

- TensorRT 用 **`IOptimizationProfile`** 描述每个输入张量允许的动态范围。核心是三个 shape 向量：
  - `min`：最小 shape（下界）
  - `opt`：编译器用于挑选最优 kernel/tactic 的「典型」shape（通常期望是运行时最常出现的 shape）
  - `max`：最大 shape（上界）
- C++ API：
  ```cpp
  auto profile = builder->createOptimizationProfile();
  profile->setDimensions("input", OptProfileSelector::kMIN, Dims4(1,3,224,224));
  profile->setDimensions("input", OptProfileSelector::kOPT, Dims4(8,3,224,224));
  profile->setDimensions("input", OptProfileSelector::kMAX, Dims4(32,3,224,224));
  config->addOptimizationProfile(profile);
  ```
  `Dims` 中用 `-1` 表示该维是动态的（build 时 unknown，运行时由 profile 区间决定），或用 `setShape` 并把某维标为 `-1`。
- Python API：
  ```python
  profile = builder.create_optimization_profile()
  profile.set_shape("input", min=(1,3,224,224), opt=(8,3,224,224), max=(32,3,224,224))
  config.add_optimization_profile(profile)
  ```
- 运行时用 `context->setInputShape("input", runtime_dims)` 绑定实际维度；若输入维度超出 min/max 或维数不符，会报错（比如 shape 不匹配 / binding 失败）。
- 动态 shape 需要 **explicit batch**（`NetworkDefinitionCreationFlag::kEXPLICIT_BATCH`），TRT 8/10 中 explicit batch 是默认。
- 一个 engine 可有多个 profile；多 profile 时 context 需 `setOptimizationProfileAsync(index)` 选择。profile 数量多会增加 build 时间和显存。
- 「动态 batch」通常把 batch 维设为动态：min=1, opt=N, max=M。注意 `opt` 不自动居中，需自己填。
- TRT 10 里 `build_serialized_network` 的 builder config 还涉及 `builder_optimization_level`，与 shape 无关但影响 build；`IInt8Calibrator` 等。

## 2. Triton Inference Server 侧的 dynamic batching

- 模型配置文件 `config.pbtxt`：
  ```
  max_batch_size: 32
  dynamic_batching {
    preferred_batch_size: [ 4, 8 ]
    max_queue_delay_microseconds: 100
  }
  ```
  - `max_batch_size > 0` 时启用 batching，请求张量的第 0 维是 batch 维；Triton 会把多个请求合并成更大 batch。
  - `preferred_batch_size` 是期望的 batch 大小集合；`max_queue_delay_microseconds` 控制调度器最多等待多久来凑 batch。
- **TensorRT 模型在 Triton 中的动态 shape**：用 `config.pbtxt` 里的
  ```
  input [
    {
      name: "input"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 3, 224, 224 ]
    }
  ]
  ```
  这里 dims 不含 batch 维。要支持可变空间维，用 `-1`：
  ```
  dims: [ 3, -1, -1 ]
  ```
  并在 `instance_group` / `optimization` 里用 `dynamic_batching` 之外，Triton 会为 TensorRT 生成 optimization profile。
- Triton 有两种「动态」：
  1. **dynamic batching**：合并请求的 batch 维（由 `max_batch_size` + `dynamic_batching` 控制）。
  2. **dynamic shape**：非 batch 维可变（由 `dims` 中 `-1` + TensorRT optimization profile 控制）。
- Triton 允许通过 `optimization { }` 块（`input_pinned_memory` 等）以及 `tensorrt` backend 的 `parameters` 影响 profile。对于 TRT backend，Triton 根据 `max_batch_size` 和输入 dims 自动构造 profile：min、opt、max。若需要自定义，有 `tensorrt` backend 的 `profile` 相关参数（如 TRT 8.5+ 的 `optimization profiles` 参数）；我记得较老版本的可控性有限，需要传 `--min-shape/--opt-shape/--max-shape` 之类的参数（不确定具体键名）。
- 还有一个要点：Triton 的 **sequence batching** 和 **ensemble** 与动态 batching 的关系；以及 `max_batch_size: 0` 表示禁用 batching（但 TensorRT TRT 8+ 的 explicit batch 通过 dims 表达）。
- 模型仓库结构：`model_repository/<model_name>/config.pbtxt` + `1/model.plan`（TensorRT plan）。

## 我不确定 / 需要外部资料核实的地方

1. **Triton TensorRT backend 自定义 optimization profile 的确切参数键名和语法**（例如 `tensorrt` backend parameters 里如何显式给 min/opt/max，以及是否要配合 `dims` 的 `-1`）。这是我最不确定、最需要检索的点。
2. TRT 版本差异：较新的 TRT 10.x 与 8.x 在 `IOptimizationProfile`、`set_shape` 上的 API 细节，以及 TRT 10 中 `build_serialized_network` 的变化。
3. `dynamic_batching` 与 TensorRT 动态 batch 在 Triton 中同时使用时的组合语义（是否 `preferred_batch_size` 会与 TRT profile 的 opt batch 冲突）。
4. 具体版本号建议（Triton 版本 ↔ TRT 版本 ↔ CUDA 版本对应关系），我无法凭记忆给出可靠的确切版本。
5. 具体的 `tritonclient` 请求中如何传 shape（`InferInput` 的 dims 设定）。
6. 是否存在 `min/opt/max` 必须满足的额外约束（例如 opt 必须落在 min..max 内、动态维在 min/max 中必须一致地标 -1 等 — 我记得有这类约束但需核实原文）。

我打算先检索官方文档（NVIDIA TensorRT developer guide 的 optimization profile 章节，以及 Triton 的 dynamic batching / TensorRT backend 文档）。

**标题**: Model Configuration — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server

# Model Configuration#

**Is this your first time writing a config file?** Check out this guide or this example!

Each model in a model repository must include a model configuration that provides required and optional information about the model. Typically, this configuration is provided in a config.pbtxt file specified as ModelConfig protobuf. In some cases, discussed in Auto-Generated Model Configuration, the model configuration can be generated automatically by Triton and so does not need to be provided explicitly.

This section describes the most important model configuration properties but the documentation in the ModelConfig protobuf should also be consulted.

## Minimal Model Configuration#

A minimal model configuration must specify the *platform* and/or *backend* properties, the *max_batch_size* property, and the input and output tensors of the model.

As an example consider a TensorRT model that has two inputs, *input0* and *input1*, and one output, *output0*, all of which are 16 entry float32 tensors. The minimal configuration is:

```
  platform: "tensorrt_plan"
  max_batch_size: 8
  input [
    {
      name: "input0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 16 ]
    },
    {
      name: "input1"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 16 ]
    }
  ]
  output [
    {
      name: "output0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 16 ]
    }
  ]
```

### Name, Platform and Backend#

The model configuration *name* property is optional. If the name of the model is not specified in the configuration it is assumed to be the same as the model repository directory containing the model. If *name* is specified it must match the name of the model repository directory containing the model. The required values for *platform* and *backend* are described in the backend documentation.

[...]

### Maximum Batch Size#

The *max_batch_size* property indicates the maximum batch size that the model supports for the types of batching that can be exploited by Triton. If the model’s batch dimension is the first dimension, and all inputs and outputs to the model have this batch dimension, then Triton can use its dynamic batcher or sequence batcher to automatically use batching with the model. In this case *max_batch_size* should be set to a value greater-or-equal-to 1 that indicates the maximum batch size that Triton should use with the model.

For models that do not support batching, or do not support batching in the specific ways described above, *max_batch_size* must be set to zero.

[...]

### Inputs and Outputs#

#### Special Conventions for PyTorch Backend#

# Model Configuration#
## Minimal Model Configuration#
### Inputs and Outputs#
#### Special Conventions for PyTorch Backend#
The input names in the configuration in this case must not follow the above naming conventions `<name>__<index>`. Instead, the names of the inputs in this case must map to the string value ‘key’ for that specific tensor. For this case, the inputs would be “A” and “B”, where input “A” refers to value corresponding to tensor1 and “B” refers to the value corresponding to tensor2.

The datatypes allowed for input and output tensors varies based on the type of the model. Section Datatypes describes the allowed datatypes and how they map to the datatypes of each model type.

An input shape indicates the shape of an input tensor expected by the model and by Triton in inference requests. An output shape indicates the shape of an output tensor produced by the model and returned by Triton in response to an inference request. Both input and output shape must have rank greater-or-equal-to 1, that is, the empty shape **[ ]** is not allowed.

Input and output shapes are specified by a combination of *max_batch_size* and the dimensions specified by the input or output *dims* property. For models with *max_batch_size* greater-than 0, the full shape is formed as [ -1 ] + *dims*. For models with *max_batch_size* equal to 0, the full shape is formed as *dims*. For example, for the following configuration the shape of “input0” is [-1, 16 ] and the shape of “output0” is [ -1, 4 ].

```
  platform: "tensorrt_plan"
  max_batch_size: 8
  input [
    {
      name: "input0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 16 ]
    }
  ]
  output [
    {
      name: "output0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 4 ]
    }
  ]
```

# Model Configuration#
## Minimal Model Configuration#
### Inputs and Outputs#
#### Special Conventions for PyTorch Backend#
For a configuration that is identical except that *max_batch_size* equal to 0, the shape of “input0” is [ 16 ] and the shape of “output0” is [ 4 ].

```
  platform: "tensorrt_plan"
  max_batch_size: 0
  input [
    {
      name: "input0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 16 ]
    }
  ]
  output [
    {
      name: "output0"
      data_type: TYPE_FP32
      dims: [ 4 ]
    }
  ]
```

For models that support input and output tensors with variable-size dimensions, those dimensions can be listed as -1 in the input and output configuration. For example, if a model requires a 2-dimensional input tensor where the first dimension must be size 4 but the second dimension can be any size, the model configuration for that input would include *dims: [ 4, -1 ]*. Triton would then accept inference requests where that input tensor’s second dimension was any value greater-or-equal-to 0. The model configuration can be more restrictive than what is allowed by the underlying model. For example, even though the framework model itself allows the second dimension to be any size, the model configuration could be specified as *dims: [ 4, 4 ]*. In this case, Triton would only accept inference requests where the input tensor’s shape was exactly *[ 4, 4 ]*.

The *reshape* property must be used if there is a mismatch between the input shape that Triton receives in an inference request and the input shape expected by the model. Similarly, the *reshape* property must be used if there is a mismatch between the output shape produced by the model and the shape that Triton returns in a response to an inference request.

[...]

## Auto-Generated Model Configuration#

# Model Configuration#
## Auto-Generated Model Configuration#
The model configuration file containing the required settings must be available with each model to be deployed on Triton. In some cases the required portions of the model configuration can be generated automatically by Triton. The required portion of the model configuration are the settings shown in the Minimal Model Configuration. By default, Triton will try to complete these sections. However, by starting Triton with `--disable-auto-complete-config` option, Triton can be configured to not auto-complete model configuration on the backend side. However, even with this option Triton will fill in missing `instance_group` settings with default values.

# Model Configuration#
## Auto-Generated Model Configuration#
Triton can derive all the required settings automatically for most of the TensorRT saved-model, ONNX models, and OpenVINO models. For Python models, `auto_complete_config` function can be implemented in Python backend to provide `max_batch_size`, `input` and `output` properties using `set_max_batch_size`, `add_input`, and `add_output` functions. These properties will allow Triton to load the Python model with Minimal Model Configuration in absence of a configuration file. All other model types *must* provide a model configuration file.

# Model Configuration#
## Auto-Generated Model Configuration#
When developing a custom backend, you can populate required settings in the configuration and call `TRITONBACKEND_ModelSetConfig` API to update completed configuration with Triton core. You can take a look at Onnxruntime backends as examples of how to achieve this. Currently, only inputs, outputs, max_batch_size and dynamic batching settings can be populated by backend. For custom backends, your config.pbtxt file must include a `backend` field or your model name must be in the form `<model_name>.<backend_name>`.

You can also see the model configuration generated for a model by Triton using the model configuration endpoint. The easiest way to do this is to use a utility like *curl*:

```
$ curl localhost:8000/v2/models/<model name>/config
```

# Model Configuration#
## Auto-Generated Model Configuration#
This will return a JSON representation of the generated model configuration. From this you can take the max_batch_size, inputs, and outputs sections of the JSON and convert it to a config.pbtxt file. Triton only generates the minimal portion of the model configuration. You must still provide the optional portions of the model configuration by editing the config.pbtxt file.

[...]

## Custom Model Configuration#

### Default Max Batch Size and Dynamic Batcher#

When a model is using the auto-complete feature, a default maximum batch size may be set by using the `--backend-config=default-max-batch-size=<int>` command line argument. This allows all models which are capable of batching and which make use of Auto Generated Model Configuration to have a default maximum batch size. This value is set to 4 by default. Backend developers may make use of this default-max-batch-size by obtaining it from the TRITONBACKEND_BackendConfig api. Currently, the following backends which utilize these default batch values and turn on dynamic batching in their generated model configurations are:

1. Onnxruntime backend
2. TensorRT backend
   
   1. TensorRT models store the maximum batch size explicitly and do not make use of the default-max-batch-size parameter. However, if max_batch_size > 1 and no scheduler is provided, the dynamic batch scheduler will be enabled.

If a value greater than 1 for the maximum batch size is set for the model, the dynamic_batching config will be set if no scheduler is provided in the configuration file.

[...]

## Instance Groups#

Triton can provide multiple instances of a model so that multiple inference requests for that model can be handled simultaneously. The model configuration *ModelInstanceGroup* property is used to specify the number of execution instances that should be made available and what compute resource should be used for those instances.

[...]

### Rate Limiter Configuration#

#### Resources#

The set of resources required to execute a model instance. The “name” field identifies the resource and “count” field refers to the number of copies of the resource that the model instance in the group requires to run. The “global” field specifies whether the resource is per-device or shared globally across the system. Loaded models can not specify a resource with the same name both as global and non-global. If no resources are provided then triton assumes the execution of model instance does not require any resources and will start executing as soon as model instance is available.

[...]

### Ensemble Model Instance Groups#

Ensemble models are an abstraction Triton uses to execute a user-defined pipeline of models. Since there is no physical instance associated with an ensemble model, the `instance_group` field can not be specified for it.

However, each composing model that makes up an ensemble can specify `instance_group` in its config file and individually support parallel execution as described above when the ensemble receives multiple requests.

[...]

## Optimization Policy#

The model configuration *ModelOptimizationPolicy* property is used to specify optimization and prioritization settings for a model. These settings control if/how a model is optimized by the backend and how it is scheduled and executed by Triton. See the ModelConfig protobuf and optimization documentation for the currently available settings.

**标题**: Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution — NVIDIA Triton Inference Server

# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#

Navigate to

Part 1: Model Deployment

Part 3: Optimizing Triton Configuration

Part-1 of this series introduced the mechanisms to set up a Triton Inference Server. This iteration discusses the concept of dynamic batching and concurrent model execution. These are important features that can be used to reduce latency as well as increase throughput via higher resource utilization.

## What is Dynamic Batching?#

# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#
## What is Dynamic Batching?#
Dynamic batching, in reference to the Triton Inference Server, refers to the functionality which allows the combining of one or more inference requests into a single batch (which has to be created dynamically) to maximize throughput.

Dynamic batching can be enabled and configured on per model basis by specifying selections in the model’s `config.pbtxt`. Dynamic Batching can be enabled with its default settings by adding the following to the `config.pbtxt` file:

```
dynamic_batching { }
```

While Triton batches these incoming requests without any delay, users can choose to allocate a limited delay for the scheduler to collect more inference requests to be used by the dynamic batcher.

```
dynamic_batching {
    max_queue_delay_microseconds: 100
}
```

Let’s discuss a sample scenario(refer the diagram below). Say there are 5 inference requests, `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, and `E`, with batch sizes of `4`, `2`, `2`, `6`, and `2` respectively. Each batch requires time `X ms` to be processed by the model. The maximum batch size supported by the model is `8`. `A` and `C` arrive at time `T = 0`, `B` arrives at time `T = X/3`, and `D` and `E` arrive at time `T = 2*X/3`.

In the case where no dynamic batching is used, all requests are processed sequentially, which means that it takes `5X ms` to process all the requests. This process is quite wasteful as each batch processing could have processed more batches than it did in sequential execution.

Using Dynamic batching in this case leads to more efficient packing of requests into the GPU memory resulting in a considerably faster `3X ms`. It also reduces the latency of responses as more queries can be processed in fewer cycles. If the use of `delay` is considered, `A`, `B`, `C` and `D`, `E` can be batched together to get even better utilization of resources.

# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#
## What is Dynamic Batching?#
**Note:** The above is an extreme version of an ideal case scenario. In practice, not all elements of execution can be perfectly parallelized, resulting in longer execution time for larger batches.

As observed from the above, the use of Dynamic Batching can lead to improvements in both latency and throughput while serving models. This batching feature is mainly focused on providing a solution for stateless models(models which do not maintain a state between execution, like object detection models). Triton’s sequence batcher can be used to manage multiple inference requests for stateful models. For more information and configurations regarding dynamic batching, refer to the Triton Inference Server documentation.

[...]

## Concurrent model execution#

# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#
## Concurrent model execution#
The key takeaway from the above examples is that the Triton Inference Server provides flexibility with respect to policies related to creating more efficient batching, thus enabling better resource utilization, resulting in reduced latency and increased throughput.

## Demonstration#

This section showcases the use of dynamic batching and concurrent model execution using the example for Part 1 of this series.

### Getting access to the model#

Let’s use the `text recognition` used in part 1. We do need to make some minor changes in the model, namely making the 0th axes of the model have dynamic shape to enable batching. Step 1, download the Text Recognition model weights. Use the NGC PyTorch container as the environment for the following.

```
docker run -it --gpus all -v ${PWD}:/scratch nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:<yy.mm>-py3
cd /scratch
wget https://www.dropbox.com/sh/j3xmli4di1zuv3s/AABzCC1KGbIRe2wRwa3diWKwa/None-ResNet-None-CTC.pth
```

Export the models as `.onnx` using the file in the `utils` folder. This file is adapted from Baek et. al. 2019.

```
import torch
from utils.model import STRModel

# Create PyTorch Model Object
model = STRModel(input_channels=1, output_channels=512, num_classes=37)

# Load model weights from external file
state = torch.load("None-ResNet-None-CTC.pth")
state = {key.replace("module.", ""): value for key, value in state.items()}
model.load_state_dict(state)

# Create ONNX file by tracing model
trace_input = torch.randn(1, 1, 32, 100)
torch.onnx.export(model, trace_input, "str.onnx", verbose=True, dynamic_axes={'input.1':[0],'308':[0]})
```

### Launching the server#

As discussed in `Part 1`, a model repository is a filesystem based repository of models and configuration schema used by the Triton Inference Server (refer to `Part 1` for a more detailed explanation for model repositories). For this example, the model repository structure would need to be set up in the following manner:

```
model_repository
|
|-- text_recognition
    |
    |-- config.pbtxt
    |-- 1
        |
        |-- model.onnx
```

This repository is a subset from the previous example. The key difference in this set up is the use of `instance_group`(s) and `dynamic_batching` in the model configuration. The additions are as follows:

```
instance_group [
    {
      count: 2
      kind: KIND_GPU
    }
]
dynamic_batching { }
```

With `instance_group` users can primarily tweak two things. First, the number of instances of that model deployed on each GPU. The above example will deploy `2` instances of the model `per GPU`. Secondly, the target GPUs for this group can be specified with `gpus: [ <device number>, ... <device number> ]`.

Adding `dynamic_batching {}` will enable the use of dynamic batches. Users can also add `preferred_batch_size` and `max_queue_delay_microseconds` in the body of dynamic batching to manage more efficient batching per their use case. Explore the model configuration documentation for more information.

With the model repository set up, the Triton Inference Server can be launched.

```
docker run --gpus=all -it --shm-size=256m --rm -p8000:8000 -p8001:8001 -p8002:8002 -v ${PWD}:/workspace/ -v ${PWD}/model_repository:/models nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:yy.mm-py3 bash

tritonserver --model-repository=/models
```

### Measuring Performance#

# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#
## Demonstration#
### Measuring Performance#
Having made some improvements to the model’s serving capabilities by enabling `dynamic batching` and the use of `multiple model instances`, the next step is to measure the impact of these features. To that end, the Triton Inference Server comes packaged with the Performance Analyzer which is a tool specifically designed to measure performance for Triton Inference Servers. For ease of use, it is recommended that users run this inside the same container used to run client code in Part 1 of this series.

```
docker run -it --net=host -v ${PWD}:/workspace/ nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:yy.mm-py3-sdk bash
```

On a third terminal, it is advisable to monitor the GPU Utilization to see if the deployment is saturating GPU resources.

```
watch -n0.1 nvidia-smi
```

To measure the performance gain, let’s run performance analyzer on the following configurations:

- **No Dynamic Batching, single model instance**: This configuration will be the baseline measurement. To set up the Triton Server in this configuration, do not add `instance_group` or `dynamic_batching` in `config.pbtxt` and make sure to include `--gpus=1` in the `docker run` command to set up the server.

```
# perf_analyzer -m <model name> -b <batch size> --shape <input layer>:<input shape> --concurrency-range <lower number of request>:<higher number of request>:<step>

# Query
perf_analyzer -m text_recognition -b 2 --shape input.1:1,32,100 --concurrency-range 2:16:2 --percentile=95
# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#
## Demonstration#
### Measuring Performance#
# Summarized Inference Result
Inferences/Second vs. Client p95 Batch Latency

Concurrency: 4, throughput: 977.314 infer/sec, latency 8497 usec

```

- **Just Dynamic Batching**: To set up the Triton Server in this configuration, add `dynamic_batching` in `config.pbtxt`.

```
perf_analyzer -m text_recognition -b 2 --shape input.1:1,32,100 --concurrency-range 2:16:2 --percentile=95
# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#
## Demonstration#
### Measuring Performance#
# Inference Result
Inferences/Second vs. Client p95 Batch Latency
Concurrency: 2, throughput: 998.141 infer/sec, latency 4140 usec

As each of the requests had a batch size (of 2), while the maximum batch size of the model was 8, dynamically batching these requests resulted in considerably improved throughput. Another consequence is a reduction in the latency. This reduction can be primarily attributed to reduced wait time in queue wait time. As the requests are batched together, multiple requests can be processed in parallel.

# Dynamic Batching & Concurrent Model Execution#
## Demonstration#
### Measuring Performance#
- **Dynamic Batching with multiple model instances**: To set up the Triton Server in this configuration, add `instance_group` in `config.pbtxt` and make sure to include `--gpus=1` and make sure to include `--gpus=1` in the `docker run` command to set up the server. Include `dynamic_batching` per instructions of the previous section in the model configuration. A point to note is that peak GPU utilization on the GPU shot up to 74% (A100 in this case) while just using a single model instance with dynamic batching. Adding one more instance will definitely improve performance but linear perf scaling will not be achieved in this case.
