sources.text: ```` # PYTORCH\_NPU\_ALLOC\_CONF ## 功能描述 通过此环境变量可控制缓存分配器行为。配置此环境变量会改变内存占用量，可能造成性能波动。 > [!CAUTION] > > 从TorchNPU 26.2.0版本且PyTorch 2.10.0及以上版本开始，torch\_npu也支持通过[PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF](PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF.md)环境变量配置缓存分配器参数，配置方式、支持的参数和PYTORCH\_NPU\_ALLOC\_CONF相同，二者选其一配置即可，同时配置会报错并退出程序。建议优先使用PYTORCH\_ALLOC\_CONF环境变量配置缓存分配器行为。 缓存分配器会根据申请内存的大小使用不同内存池，小于1MB使用小块内存池，反之使用大块内存池；虚拟内存特性下，大块内存池申请的物理内存粒度（segment\_size\_mb）默认为20MB，小块内存池默认为2MB（不可配置）；大模型场景下小块内存池内存使用通常较少，因此部分环境配置项（page\_size、segment\_size\_mb）只作用于大块内存池。 > [!NOTICE] > > Ascend 950DT仅支持expandable\_segments、pinned\_use\_background\_threads、pin\_memory\_expandable\_segments和pinned\_mem\_register四个参数，其余参数均不支持。 可选参数： - max\_split\_size\_mb:，内存块允许切分上限。 大于设定值的内存块在使用过程中不会进行切分，这有助于减少内存碎片。此选项主要用于当模型由于OOM（Out of Memory，内存不足）而中断，并出现大量非活动的切分内存块场景时的优化。默认值为无限大，单位MB，即所有大小的内存块都可以切分，最小设置值大于20MB。 - garbage\_collection\_threshold:，垃圾回收阈值。 主动回收未使用的NPU内存块。在设置value阈值（例如0.8）后，如果NPU内存容量使用超过阈值（即分配给NPU应用程序的总内存的80%），缓存分配器将开始回收NPU内存块，优先释放最先申请和长时间未复用的内存块，避免释放积极复用的内存块。其中取值范围为\(0.0,1.0\)。默认不开启该功能。垃圾回收阈值需与内存因子配合使用，内存因子可参考《[自定义API](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/op-plugin/blob/master/docs/zh/custom_APIs/overview.md)》的“torch\_npu.npu.set\_per\_process\_memory\_fraction”。 - expandable\_segments:，开启内存池扩展段功能，即虚拟内存特性。 默认为False。如果设置为True，此设置将指示缓存分配器创建特定的内存块分配，这些内存块后续可以扩展，以便能更好地处理内存使用中频繁变更使用内存大小的情况。如果设置为False，关闭内存池扩展段功能，使用原有的内存申请方式。 - base\_addr\_aligned\_kb:，内存基地址对齐粒度。 取值范围为0\~16，设置值需为整数，单位KB，默认值为16。仅在expandable\_segments设置为True的时候生效。若此参数配置为16，在申请大块内存（大于等于2MB）的时候，会尽量保持申请内存的基地址16KB对齐；若配置为0时，申请内存的基地址512B对齐。 - page\_size:，设置申请大页内存的大小。 取值仅支持1GB，参考[配置示例](#配置示例)。内存申请粒度为1GB，不足1GB的向上对齐到1GB，始终为1GB的整数倍。在虚拟内存特性下，该配置项只作用于缓存分配器的大块内存池。 未配置该选项时，内存申请粒度为2MB，如需申请1GB的大页内存，会占用1024/2=512个页表；设置该选项后，内存申请粒度为1GB，1GB大页内存只占用1个页表，能有效降低页表数量，有效扩大TLB（Translation Lookaside Buffer）缓存的地址范围，从而提升离散访问的性能。 TLB是昇腾AI处理器中用于高速缓存的硬件模块，用于存储最近使用的虚拟地址到物理地址的映射。 - segment\_size\_mb:，虚拟内存特性下，设置物理内存的申请粒度。 取值范围20\~512，设置值需为整数，单位MB，不配置时默认为20。仅在expandable\_segments设置为True的时候生效，该配置项只作用于缓存分配器的大块内存池。与page\_size同时配置时，仅page\_size生效。与large\_segment\_size\_mb同时配置时，仅large\_segment\_size\_mb生效。 增大segment\_size\_mb可以减少内存申请及内存映射接口的调用次数，从而提升内存申请效率，但也可能带来更多的内存碎片。因此，在内存使用极限的场景下，请谨慎调大此值。 > [!NOTE] > > segment\_size\_mb已废弃，建议使用large\_segment\_size\_mb。large\_segment\_size\_mb同时支持虚拟内存特性和非虚拟内存特性场景，功能更全面。 - roundup\_power2\_divisions: 或 roundup\_power2\_divisions:\[:,:,...\]，将请求的分配大小向上舍入到最近的2的幂次分段，从而更高效地复用内存块。 不配置时分配大小会以512字节为单位向上对齐，这对较小的分配尺寸效果良好；对于较大的、尺寸相近的分配请求，这种策略可能效率低下。因为每个请求会被分配到不同大小的内存块中，导致这些内存块难以被复用，继而产生大量未被充分复用的内存块，浪费内存容量。 支持两种配置方式： - **单一值**：为每个内存块设置相同的分段数量，例如配置为“4”。 - **键值对数组**：为每个2的幂区间单独设置分段数量。例如配置为“\[256:1,512:2,1024:4,\>:8\]”时，表示为256MB以下的所有分配设置1个分段，256MB到512MB之间的分配设置2个分段，512MB到1GB之间的分配设置4个分段，以及更大的分配设置8个分段。 - multi\_stream\_lazy\_reclaim:，多流场景下，内存申请时延迟查询Events。 默认值为False，即每次内存申请时都执行Events查询。当设置为True时，每次内存申请优先使用空闲内存块，当Events数量超过阈值512或者找不到可用内存块时，才触发Events查询。通过减少Events查询次数，降低CPU资源占用，提升Host侧性能。该配置仅影响Events状态查询的频率，不改变内存释放的条件，也不改变内存峰值，内存块仍需等待所有相关Events完成后才会被释放。 - pinned\_use\_background\_threads:，是否启用后台线程来处理events。 默认值为False，不启用后台线程。当设置为True时，启用后台线程，在后台线程执行查询和处理events操作，减少主线程的阻塞时间。 - pin\_memory\_expandable\_segments:，开启pin_memory内存池扩展段功能，即虚拟内存特性。 默认为False。如果设置为True，此设置将指示pin_memory缓存分配器内存池物理内存申请粒度为20MB（不可配置），创建的内存块后续可以扩展，以便能更好地处理内存使用中频繁变更内存大小的情况，同时pin_memory内存块计数相关统计指标不参与统计（默认值：0）。如果设置为False，关闭pin_memory内存池扩展段功能，使用原有的内存申请方式。 - pinned\_mem\_register:，设置pin_memory内存是否启用host register功能。 默认为False。如果设置为True，此设置将指示pin_memory内存启用host register功能，将pin_memory内存映射注册为Device可访问的内存地址。如果设置为False，关闭host register功能。 - large\_segment\_size\_mb:，设置大块内存池的段分配粒度。 取值需大于10，设置值需为整数，单位MB，不配置时默认为20。该配置项同时作用于虚拟内存特性和非虚拟内存特性场景。在虚拟内存特性下，控制物理内存的申请粒度；在非虚拟内存特性下，控制1~10MB区间内存申请的段大小。 增大large\_segment\_size\_mb可以减少内存申请及内存映射接口的调用次数，从而提升内存申请效率，但也可能带来更多的内存碎片。因此，在内存使用极限的场景下，请谨慎调大此值。 与segment\_size\_mb同时配置时，仅large\_segment\_size\_mb生效。与page\_size同时配置时，仅page\_size生效。与max\_split\_size\_mb同时配置时，要求max\_split\_size\_mb >= large\_segment\_size\_mb。 - per\_process\_memory\_fraction:，限制当前进程可使用的NPU显存比例。 取值范围为\[0.0,1.0\]，表示可用的设备显存比例，默认值为1.0，即不限制进程显存使用。配置后，框架在初始化时会根据设备总显存和配置的比例计算当前进程可使用的最大显存，超出限制的内存申请将触发OOM（Out of Memory，内存不足）错误。 该配置项适用于多进程共享同一NPU设备的场景，通过限制进程的可用显存的比例，避免单个进程占用过多显存导致其他进程OOM。 - throw\_on\_npumalloc\_oom:，在发生内存OOM之前预防式拒绝内存申请，跳过内存分配重试流程。 取值为True或False，默认为False。默认或设置为False时，如果调用底层ACL接口分配内存失败则释放部分空闲内存并进行必要的Host-Device同步，然后尝试重新分配内存，该重试流程对性能有一定的影响。设置为True时，缓存分配器在调用底层ACL接口分配内存之前，先校验“当前进程已分配的内存大小+本次的申请大小”是否超出设备内存上限；超出则直接拒绝本次申请并抛出OutOfMemoryError异常，不再进入内存分配重试流程。 以下二种情况throw\_on\_npumalloc\_oom不生效： - 使用环境变量PYTORCH\_NPU\_ALLOC\_CONF或PYTORCH\_ALLOC\_CONF配置per\_process\_memory\_fraction小于1.0。 - 调用torch\_npu.npu.set\_per\_process\_memory\_fraction\(\)接口设置fraction小于1.0。 throw\_on\_npumalloc\_oom设置为True且拒绝内存申请时，内存申请的拒绝次数会累加到torch\_npu.npu.memory\_stats\(\)\[\'num\_oom\_rejections\'\]字段，可通过torch\_npu.npu.reset\_accumulated\_memory\_stats\(\)接口清零。这种情况下环境变量OOM\_SNAPSHOT\_ENABLE不生效。 - pinned\_max\_round\_threshold\_mb:，pinned memory分配大小是否向上取整到2的幂次的判别阈值。 取值为正整数，单位为MB。默认不开启，即对所有pinned memory分配都执行power-of-2向上取整。设置后，分配大小若小于等于此阈值，仍执行向上取整；若大于此阈值，则跳过取整并按精确请求大小分配，从而减少大块pinned memory因取整带来的内存浪费。例如阈值设为128MB时，129MB的分配请求将使用129MB而非向上取整到256MB。 向上取整是为了让内存块便于后续复用，不进入缓存的块无需对齐，所以无论本选项如何设置，超过pinned\_max\_cached\_size\_mb的分配始终不会执行向上取整。 - pinned\_max\_cached\_size\_mb:，pinned memory释放后是否缓存到free list复用的判别阈值。 取值为正整数，单位为MB。默认不开启，即所有释放的pinned memory块都进入free list缓存复用。设置后，块大小若大于此阈值，则在释放时立即归还给OS，不再进入free list缓存（也不再执行向上取整），从而降低大块pinned memory使用频率较低场景下的峰值内存占用。 - max\_non\_split\_rounding\_mb:，显存复用控制项，结合max\_split\_size\_mb控制显存块大小和复用。 取值为正整数，单位为MB，默认20M。显存块free后物理上不一定释放，假定保留给下次分配使用，该块保留的显存大小为A、max\_non\_split\_rounding\_mb为B、max\_split\_size\_mb为C，需要新分配一个内存D。 当D大于C，计算A-D： - 如果A-D小于等于B，则不需要重新分配，复用A； - 如果A-D大于B，则需要重新分配新的显存。 当D小于等于C，当前变量不生效。 - release\_lock\_on\_npumalloc:，显存分配锁控制项，决策是否在分配显存时释放部分锁，控制的项保持与原生社区一致。 取值为bool类型，True或False，默认为False。设置后，显存分配会释放部分锁，可缓解host计算开销压力，但是可能造成更多资源占用，自定义开发显存管理可能存在不兼容问题，需谨慎使用。 > [!NOTE] > > 用户使用TorchNPU 6.0.RC3及以上版本配套的驱动（Ascend HDK 24.1.RC3及以上），开启虚拟内存特性时，可以使用单进程多卡特性；用户使用TorchNPU 6.0.RC3以下版本配套的驱动（Ascend HDK 24.1.RC3以下版本），开启虚拟内存特性时，不能使用单进程多卡特性。 ## 配置示例 示例一： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6 ``` 示例二： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True,base_addr_aligned_kb:16 ``` 示例三： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=page_size:1g ``` 示例四： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True,segment_size_mb:40 ``` 示例五： - 单一值示例： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF="roundup_power2_divisions:4" ``` - 键值对数组示例： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF="roundup_power2_divisions:[256:1,512:2,1024:4,>:8]" ``` 示例六： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=multi_stream_lazy_reclaim:True ``` 示例七： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_use_background_threads:True ``` 示例八： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=pin_memory_expandable_segments:True ``` 示例九： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_mem_register:True ``` 示例十： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=large_segment_size_mb:50 ``` 示例十一： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=per_process_memory_fraction:0.5 ``` 示例十二： ```bash export PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6 ``` 示例十三： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=throw_on_npumalloc_oom:True ``` 示例十四： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=pinned_max_round_threshold_mb:128,pinned_max_cached_size_mb:256 ``` 示例十五： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:50,max_non_split_rounding_mb:30 ``` 示例十六： ```bash export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=release_lock_on_npumalloc:True ``` ## 使用约束 - expandable\_segments特性需在Ascend HDK 23.0.0及以上版本上使用。 - max\_split\_size\_mb和garbage\_collection\_threshold中任意一个为非默认值时，expandable\_segments必须设置为False。 - page\_size特性要求在Ascend HDK 25.0.RC1及以上版本、CANN商用8.1.RC1及以上版本使用，支持如下产品： - Atlas A2 训练系列产品 - Atlas A3 训练系列产品 - page\_size特性与其他特性同时配置时，仅page\_size配置生效，且申请内存注意事项如下： - 当申请内存大于1MB时： - 若配置page\_size，内存申请粒度为1GB。 - 若未配置page\_size，内存申请粒度为2MB。 - 当申请内存小于等于1MB时：配置page\_size也不生效，内存申请粒度为2MB。 - pin_memory_expandable_segments特性要求TorchNPU 7.3.0及以上版本、Ascend HDK 25.5.0及以上版本、CANN商用8.5.0及以上版本使用。 - pinned_use_background_threads特性要求在TorchNPU 26.0.0及以上版本且PyTorch 2.8.0及以上版本使用。 - pinned_mem_register使用注意事项如下： - 特性要求TorchNPU 26.0.0及以上版本、Ascend HDK 26.0.RC1及以上版本、CANN商用8.5.0及以上版本使用。 - 与pin_memory_expandable_segments特性不支持同时配置。 - multi_stream_lazy_reclaim使用注意事项： - 特性要求在TorchNPU 7.3.0以上版本上使用。 - 该特性主要解决多流场景下，Host侧存在下发性能瓶颈时的系统效率问题。单流、少流场景或者非Host性能瓶颈时，该功能收益不大。 - large\_segment\_size\_mb特性需在TorchNPU 26.1.0及以上版本、PyTorch 2.11.0及以上版本使用。 - per\_process\_memory\_fraction特性需在TorchNPU 26.1.0及以上版本、PyTorch 2.10.0 及以上版本使用。 - throw\_on\_npumalloc\_oom特性需在TorchNPU 26.2.0及以上版本、PyTorch 2.13.0及以上版本使用。 - pinned\_max\_round\_threshold\_mb和pinned\_max\_cached\_size\_mb特性需在TorchNPU 26.2.0及以上版本、PyTorch 2.13.0及以上版本使用。两者仅作用于默认（非expandable）pinned memory分配器路径。与pin\_memory\_expandable\_segments同时配置时，这两个阈值不生效，框架会输出一次告警提示，但进程仍可正常启动；如需启用这两个阈值，请将pin\_memory\_expandable\_segments设置为False。 - **标题**: NPU显存溢出：如何通过设置max_split_size_mb避免？_编程语言-CSDN问答

# NPU显存溢出：如何通过设置max_split_size_mb避免？

**问题：** 在昇腾（Ascend）NPU上训练大模型时，常因显存分配策略激进导致`OutOfMemoryError`，尤其在启用`torch.compile`或动态shape场景下。错误日志中频繁出现“Failed to allocate XXX MB from device memory”，但实际显存占用远未达卡上限。经查，这是由于PyTorch NPU后端默认将大张量一次性申请连续显存块，而碎片化或对齐开销引发溢出。`max_split_size_mb`作为关键调优参数，控制NPU内存分配器的最大单次切分粒度——值过大会加剧碎片风险，过小则增加分配开销甚至触发fallback失败。那么：**如何根据模型规模、batch size和NPU型号（如910B/910C），科学设置`max_split_size_mb`以平衡显存利用率与分配稳定性？是否需配合`ASCEND_ALLOC_CONF`环境变量协同生效？**

- ```html
  
  ## 一、现象层：OOM错误的表象与典型日志特征
  
  在昇腾910B/910C NPU上训练LLaMA-2-7B（batch_size=8, seq_len=2048）时，`torch.compile(mode="max-autotune")`触发后频繁报错：`OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate 1248 MB from device memory`。监控显示`npu-smi`显存占用仅68%，远低于910B单卡80GB上限。该现象在动态shape（如`torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention` with varying `attn_mask`）下复现率超92%。
  
  ## 二、机制层：NPU内存分配器的双阶段碎片成因
  
  - **第一阶段（预分配）**：PyTorch Ascend后端调用`aclrtMalloc`请求连续物理页，受Ascend CANN 7.0+中`GeMemoryPool`管理策略约束；
  - **第二阶段（对齐放大）**：为满足DMA传输边界（如2MB对齐）、Tensor Core访存粒度（128B/256B），实际申请量 = ceil(逻辑大小 / 对齐单位) × 对齐单位；
  - **关键矛盾**：`max_split_size_mb`控制*单次切分最大块*，但默认值（CANN 7.0为512MB）在大模型中间激活张量（如[8,32,2048,128] FP16 ≈ 4096MB）场景下，强制要求4GB连续空间，而碎片化后剩余最大连续块常＜2GB。
  
  ## 三、参数层：`max_split_size_mb`的科学取值模型
  
  经华为昇腾实验室实测验证（基于CANN 8.0.RC1 + PyTorch 2.3.0-ascend），推荐配置如下表：
  
  NPU型号典型模型规模batch_size推荐`max_split_size_mb`依据说明Ascend 910BLLaMA-7B4–16128–256兼顾`kv_cache`分片与梯度allreduce通信对齐Ascend 910CQwen2-14B2–864–128910C L2缓存更小（4MB vs 910B 8MB），需更细粒度切分Ascend 910BGPT-3-175B（ZeRO-3）132避免`optimizer.state`分配失败，实测32MB下碎片容忍度提升3.8×
  
  ## 四、协同层：`ASCEND_ALLOC_CONF`环境变量的必要性
  
  `max_split_size_mb`必须通过`ASCEND_ALLOC_CONF`注入才生效，直接传参（如`torch.npu.set_allocator_config`）在CANN 7.0+已被弃用。正确用法：
  
  ```
  export ASCEND_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128,enable_vmm:1
  # enable_vmm=1启用虚拟内存映射，缓解物理地址碎片影响
  # 若未设置ASCEND_ALLOC_CONF，max_split_size_mb将被忽略，回退至默认512MB
  ```
  
  ## 五、验证层：量化诊断与闭环调优流程
  
  graph TD A[启动训练脚本] --> B{监控npu-smi -d 0 -t 1} B -->|连续块<max_split_size_mb| C[降低max_split_size_mb] B -->|分配延迟＞200ms| D[增大max_split_size_mb] C --> E[记录OOM频次/epoch] D --> E E --> F{频次≤0.5/epoch & 吞吐下降＜8%} F -->|是| G[锁定当前值] F -->|否| H[网格搜索：64→128→256]
  
  ## 六、进阶层：与torch.compile及动态shape的深度适配
  
  当启用`torch.compile`时，需额外注意：
  
  - 编译后图中`view`/`permute`操作会生成临时buffer，其size由`max_split_size_mb`决定是否可切分；
  - 动态shape导致`Inductor`无法静态推导tensor生命周期，需配合`torch._dynamo.config.cache_size_limit = 64`限制图缓存数量，避免内存分配器被大量废弃图元污染；
  - 实测表明：910B上`max_split_size_mb=128` + `cache_size_limit=32`可使Qwen2-7B动态batch训练稳定性从57%提升至99.2%。
  
  ## 七、生产层：自动化调优脚本与SRE实践
  
  我们构建了`ascend_mem_tuner.py`工具，支持自动扫描最优值：
  
  ```
  python ascend_mem_tuner.py \
    --model llama2_7b \
    --npu 910B \
    --batch 8 \
    --seq_len 2048 \
    --metric "oom_rate,throughput,mem_fragment_ratio"
  # 输出：best_max_split_size_mb=192, fragment_ratio=0.31, oom_rate=0.0
  ```
  
  该脚本已集成至华为ModelArts Pipeline，在12个客户大模型训练任务中平均减少OOM中断3.7次/天。
  
  ```

# 昇腾NPU大模型训练调试调优全攻略 原创 [![vip_tag](https://csdnimg.cn/release/blogv2/dist/mobile/img/vip-article-tag.png)](https://mall.csdn.net/vip?spm=1003.2018.3001.6455)

### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)1. 项目概述

#### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)1.1 核心需求解析

先聊个现象，我这两年接触了不少团队从GPU栈往昇腾NPU上迁移 大模型 训练，聊天记录里出现频率最高的一句话就是："代码在GPU上能跑，怎么到了昇腾上要么loss不降，要么慢得离谱，再要么直接OOM都不知道死在哪一步？"

这其实就是大模型训练调试调优的核心痛点。昇腾作为国产AI算力平台，硬件 架构 跟CUDA生态有本质区别——GPU是SIMT架构，NPU是达芬奇架构，从算子到通信再到显存管理，每一条链路都需要重新适配。而大模型的训练，无论是7B还是70B的规模，又恰好是最考验系统全链路稳定性的场景：分布式并行、梯度同步、激活值显存、混合精度、Checkpoint策略，任何一个环节掉链子，整个训练都会前功尽弃。

这篇博文聚焦的是昇腾上大模型训练的完整生命周期，从环境准备、数据与模型迁移、训练启动与监控，到性能调优和问题排查，给你一套可以直接照着做的实操路线。适合正在做国产化算力迁移的算法工程师，也适合被安排搭昇腾训练环境的平台团队，哪怕你手头只有一两张昇腾卡，里面聊的很多排查思路和优化手段一样用得上。

#### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)1.2 为什么单独聊昇腾调试调优

说白了，昇腾调试调优这件事，跟你在网上搜到的通用PyTorch调参技巧不是一回事。PyTorch在CUDA上跑得好好的代码，放到NPU上，第一道坎就是算子适配——PyTorch封装的算子底层如果调用的是cuDNN或者cuBLAS，换到昇腾上就得走CANN自研的算子库。CANN这些年迭代得已经相当全了，常见的 `torch.add` 、 `torch.bmm` 、 `LayerNorm` 、 `Softmax` 都能找到对应实现，但问题是，一些非常规操作、自定义算子、或者新版PyTorch刚加的特性，适配就会滞后。

另一道坎是通信。大模型训练逃不开张量并行、流水并行、数据并行，这些并行的底层依赖集合通信原语。GPU生态走的是NCCL，昇腾走的是HCCL，两个库虽然接口语义类似，但在拓扑感知、通信调度策略上有差异，直接导致同样的并行策略在昇腾上收敛速度不同，甚至会卡死。

说这些不是为了劝退，而是把底层逻辑给你摆清楚。了解差异在哪，调试时就有方向感，不至于一报错就懵。

### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)2. 前置环境准备与踩坑避雷

#### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)2.1 昇腾NPU环境搭建要点

昇腾训练环境的核心依赖是CANN工具包，它的地位相当于CUDA+cuDNN在GPU生态里的组合。版本选择上我的建议很明确：不要追新，优先看你的PyTorch版本和模型代码依赖了哪些算子，倒推一个稳定组合。

以目前主流的组合为例，我习惯用 Python 3.9/3.10 + PyTorch 2.1/2.2 + CANN 8.0。装的时候留意三个东西是否配套：昇腾驱动固件（NPU Firmware）、CANN toolkit、以及 `torch_npu` 这个适配层。 `torch_npu` 就是让PyTorch算子能跑到NPU上的关键桥梁，它有独立的版本号，必须跟CANN版本与PyTorch版本匹配。怎么看是否匹配？官方文档的版本配套表就是依据，别自己想象着搭配，跨版本组合经常出现"安装时一切正常，一跑就崩"的诡异问题。

另外一个非常容易被忽略的点： 环境变量 。即便你正确安装了CANN，没有source环境变量，程序依然找不到NPU设备文件。我一般会在 `~/.bashrc` 里固定写入这样一段：

```bash
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3

1212
```

`ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` 相当于GPU场景的 `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` ，控制哪些物理NPU对当前进程可见。多卡用户务必确认设备编号，否则训练时跑到板上只有4张卡但系统实际插了8张卡的情况，你会被资源分配搞得晕头转向。

#### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)2.2 分布式并行训练环境检查清单

大模型训练默认就是分布式，跟单卡Debug是完全两码事。昇腾分布式依赖HCCL集合通信库，在正式起训练之前，我强烈建议先跑一个HCCL通信自检，也不复杂，几行Python代码就行：

```python
import torch
import torch_npu
import torch.distributed as dist

dist.init_process_group(backend='hccl', init_method='tcp://127.0.0.1:23456', rank=0, world_size=1)
x = torch.randn(1024).npu()
dist.all_reduce(x)
print(x.sum().item())

1234567812345678
```

这一步看起来简单，却能一次性验证NPU设备是否正常、HCCL是否可用、TCP通信是否畅通三层问题。很多人在全量训练跑到一半才发现通信异常，白白浪费几天时间，就是省略了这个冒烟测试。但凡起多卡训练，先跑通信自检，没有商量的余地。

还有一点要提醒的是，HCCL默认走的是PCIe或者RoCE，在跨机训练时要确保网卡类型、IP配置、权限都对得上，不然会报 `HCCL connect timeout` 。这类错误排查起来最费劲，因为网络问题跟模型问题往往是纠缠在一起的。

### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)3. 模型迁移全流程：从GPU代码到昇腾NPU

#### [](https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_30872577/article/details/164347537)3.1 PyTorch模型的NPU适配改造

昇腾对PyTorch的适配方式是提供 `torch_npu` 扩展库，你在GPU代码里写的 `.cuda()` 、 `torch.cuda.FloatTensor` 需要对应替换成 `.npu()` 和 `torch.npu.FloatTensor` 。听起来简单，但实际改起来工作量取决于你代码里硬编码了多少设备逻辑。

我见过最省事的改法是全局搜替换：

```python
device = 'npu' if torch_npu.npu.is_available() else 'cpu'
model = model.to(device)
data = data.to(device)

123123
```

稍微严谨一点是先用环境变量统一控制：

```python
import os
import torch
import torch_npu

device = os.environ.get('DEVICE', 'npu')

1234512345
```

在典型的大模型训练脚本里，除了设备名，还需要处理输出保存路径、日志落盘位置、混合 精度 API。混合精度这块，GPU生态常用 `torch.cuda.amp` ，昇腾这里通常用 `torch.npu.amp` ，或者直接使用 `torch.cuda.amp`

# 昇腾（CANN + torch_npu）训练 NPU out of memory 排查与显存优化

## 一、排查步骤

1. **确认 OOM 现场**：报错典型为 `OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate XXX MB from device memory`。用 `npu-smi info` 看物理占用；若显示占用远低于卡上限仍 OOM，多半是**显存碎片**（reserved 远大于 allocated，剩余最大连续块不够）。
2. **用内存管理 API 定位**：torch_npu 提供与 torch.cuda 对应的内存管理接口（官方 API 列表页见来源[4]，本轮抓取两次均返回了错误页面（标题为 hi_remap_lut），**具体接口清单未核实**；按 torch_npu 惯例可用 `torch_npu.npu.memory_allocated()`、`max_memory_allocated()`、`memory_summary()`、`memory_stats()`、`empty_cache()`、`set_per_process_memory_fraction()` 等，使用前请以你安装版本的官方 API 列表为准）。重点看 reserved vs allocated 差值判断碎片。
3. **定位占用大头**：参数/梯度/优化器状态（Adam 状态约 2×参数量）为静态占用；激活值随 batch size、序列长度增长。检查日志/保存中是否意外持有带计算图的张量（如未 `.item()` 的 loss 累积）。
4. 官方还支持 OOM snapshot 机制：环境变量 `OOM_SNAPSHOT_ENABLE`（在 `throw_on_npumalloc_oom:True` 拒绝申请的场景下不生效），可用于事后分析分配历史（来源[3]提及该字段，细节未进一步核实）。

## 二、PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF（官方环境变量）

控制缓存分配器行为。格式：`PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=<option1>:<value1>,<option2>:<value2>`（来源[1][2]）。分配器按大小分池：<1MB 用小块池，≥1MB 用大块池。

关键参数（默认值/约束均来自官方文档，来源[2]）：

| 参数 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `max_split_size_mb` | 内存块允许切分上限，默认无限大（所有块可切分），最小设置值 >20MB。大于设定值的块不再切分，**用于 OOM 且存在大量非活动切分块（碎片）场景的优化** |
| `garbage_collection_threshold` | 垃圾回收阈值，取值 (0.0,1.0)，默认 0.0（不开启）。占用超阈值时主动回收未使用内存块；需配合 `torch_npu.npu.set_per_process_memory_fraction` 使用 |
| `expandable_segments` | 虚拟内存特性，默认 False。能更好应对频繁变化的内存大小。要求 Ascend HDK 23.0.0+ |
| `base_addr_aligned_kb` | 基地址对齐，0~16，默认 16KB，仅 expandable_segments=True 时生效 |
| `roundup_power2_divisions` | 把分配大小向上舍入到 2 的幂次分段，提高内存块复用率，支持 `[256:1,512:2,1024:4,>:8]` 形式 |
| `large_segment_size_mb` | 大块池段分配粒度，默认 20MB（>10）。增大可提升申请效率但可能增加碎片 |
| `page_size:1g` | 1G 大页内存，减少页表数量。要求 Ascend HDK 25.0.RC1+、CANN 商用 8.1.RC1+，仅 Atlas A2/A3 训练系列；与其他特性不同时配置 |
| `per_process_memory_fraction` | 限制进程可用显存比例 [0.0,1.0]，默认 1.0，用于多进程共享卡（TorchNPU 26.1.0+/PyTorch 2.10.0+） |
| `throw_on_npumalloc_oom` | True 时超上限直接抛 OOM，跳过重试流程（TorchNPU 26.2.0+/PyTorch 2.13.0+） |

**重要互斥约束**：`max_split_size_mb` 和 `garbage_collection_threshold` 任一为非默认值时，`expandable_segments` 必须为 False（来源[1][2]）。

**版本说明**：从 TorchNPU 26.2.0 + PyTorch 2.10.0 起，也可用 `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`（参数相同），二选一，同时配置会报错退出（来源[2]）。

典型配置（治碎片）：
```bash
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6
# 或虚拟内存路线（与上面互斥）：
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True,base_addr_aligned_kb:16
```

## 三、梯度检查点（重计算）

torch_npu 兼容 PyTorch 原生 API，直接使用 `torch.utils.checkpoint`：

```python
from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint

# 训练中包裹前向段，反向时重计算，省去中间激活显存
output = checkpoint(self.block, x, use_reentrant=False)
```

要点：
- 以约 20–30% 额外计算换取激活显存大幅下降，激活不再随层数线性增长；
- 仅在 `self.training` 时启用，eval/推理不用包；
- 冻结不训练的部分不需要包；
- 推荐 `use_reentrant=False`（新版默认行为，与 AMP/分布式兼容性更好）。
- 大模型场景也可直接用 MindSpeed/各训练框架内置的 recompute 配置（本轮未核实具体参数名）。

## 四、显存碎片治理

1. 先判碎片：`memory_summary()` 中 reserved ≫ allocated、或 OOM 报错显示大量非活动切分块。
2. 设 `max_split_size_mb`（建议 32~256MB 网格试，官方未给固定推荐值；第三方给出 910B 上 128–256 的经验区间，来源[5]，可信度见下）。
3. 或改用 `expandable_segments:True`（注意互斥约束；HDK 23.0.0+）。
4. `roundup_power2_divisions` 提高尺寸相近分配的复用率。
5. 减少大小不一的临时张量；谨慎使用 `torch_npu.npu.empty_cache()`（影响性能，不能减少已分配显存）。
6. `garbage_collection_threshold:0.6~0.8` + memory fraction 配合主动回收。

## 五、其他常规手段

- 减小 batch size + 梯度累积；缩短序列长度；
- 混合精度 `torch_npu.npu.amp`（或 torch.cuda.amp 接口兼容）；
- 大模型用 ZeRO/FSDP 分片优化器状态；
- 多进程共享单卡时用 `per_process_memory_fraction` 隔离。

## 来源与可信度

- [1] https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/Pytorch/720/comref/Envvariables/Envir_012.html — TorchNPU 7.2.0 官方 PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF 文档（直接正文，含参数/默认值/约束/示例，末"支持的型号"一节可能截断）
- [2] https://github.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/master/docs/zh/api/environment_variable/memory_management/PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF.md — 官方仓库 master 版（最完整，含全部参数与逐参数版本约束）
- [3] https://gitcode.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/v2.7.1/docs/zh/environment_variable_reference/PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF.md — 官方镜像（仅搜索摘要）
- [4] https://www.hiascend.com/document/detail/zh/Pytorch/700/apiref/apilist/ptaoplist_000265.html — 官方 Memory management API 列表，**两次抓取均返回错误页面（hi_remap_lut），原因未确定**，接口清单未核实

仅凭已有知识，我可以给出如下回答（未核实处已标注）：

**排查 CUDA OOM 的思路：**
1. 用 `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` / `torch.cuda.memory_reserved()` 查看当前显存分配与保留；`torch.cuda.memory_summary()` 打印详细报告。
2. 用 `nvidia-smi` 查看进程占用，确认是否有其他进程或僵尸进程占显存。
3. PyTorch 2.x 提供显存快照：`torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()` 配合 `torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("snapshot.pickle")`，上传至 pytorch.org/memory_viz 可视化分析（具体 API 名称在不同版本可能有变化，未核实）。
4. 使用环境变量 `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` 配置分配器。

**max_split_size_mb：**
- 通过 `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128`（或其他值如 64/256/512）限制分配器将大块内存分割的阈值，缓解显存碎片化导致的 OOM（即 reserved 远大于 allocated 的情况）。
- 我记忆中相关配置项还有 `roundup_power2_divisions`、`garbage_collection_threshold`（较新版本，未核实）。

**梯度检查点（gradient checkpointing）：**
- `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(fn, *args)` 包装前向计算，反向时重算激活值，以计算换显存。
- PyTorch 2.x 推荐 `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(fn, *args, use_reentrant=False)`（use_reentrant 参数的确切推荐值我比较有把握是 False）。
- 对 HuggingFace Transformers 模型可用 `model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()`。
- 需注意 input 需要 `requires_grad=True`，否则可能报错或无法省显存。

**empty_cache：**
- `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` 释放 caching allocator 中未使用的缓存显存回给 CUDA；它**不会**释放仍被张量占用的显存，因此通常不能解决训练过程中的 OOM，只能缓解碎片化或供其他进程使用。
- 不建议在训练循环中频繁调用（有同步开销）。误用 `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` 期待减少 allocated 显存是常见误区。

**其他常见手段：** 减小 batch size、混合精度（`torch.cuda.amp` / `torch.amp.autocast`）、梯度累积、`torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction()` 限制单进程显存上限等。

**不确定处：**
- `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` 各配置项在不同 PyTorch 版本的可用性与默认值（如 `expandable_segments:True`、`garbage_collection_threshold` 的引入版本）。
- `use_reentrant` 的具体引入版本和当前推荐写法。
- 官方文档的确切 URL 与最新措辞。
- `max_split_size_mb` 的具体语义细节（它是"超过该大小的块不再分割"还是其他定义），需查官方文档核实。

现在执行检索核实以上不确定点。

# Memory Management Section — Full Extraction

**Summary:** The complete "Memory management" section was present in the provided content with **no apparent truncation**. It covers the caching allocator, `empty_cache()` behavior, memory monitoring APIs, and the full `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF` option list (note: the docs now use `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF` as the primary name — `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` is a backward-compatibility alias). Below is the verbatim text, organized by subsection.

---

## Memory management (intro text — verbatim)

> PyTorch uses a caching memory allocator to speed up memory allocations. This allows fast memory deallocation without device synchronizations. However, the unused memory managed by the allocator will still show as if used in `nvidia-smi`. You can use `memory_allocated()` and `max_memory_allocated()` to monitor memory occupied by tensors, and use `memory_reserved()` and `max_memory_reserved()` to monitor the total amount of memory managed by the caching allocator. Calling `empty_cache()` releases all **unused** cached memory from PyTorch so that those can be used by other GPU applications. However, the occupied GPU memory by tensors will not be freed so it can not increase the amount of GPU memory available for PyTorch.

> To better understand how CUDA memory is being used over time, [Understanding CUDA Memory Usage](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/torch_cuda_memory.html#torch-cuda-memory) describes tools for capturing and visualizing traces of memory use.

> For more advanced users, we offer more comprehensive memory benchmarking via `memory_stats()`. We also offer the capability to capture a complete snapshot of the memory allocator state via `memory_snapshot()`, which can help you understand the underlying allocation patterns produced by your code.

### Key points: `empty_cache()` behavior and caveats
- Releases **only unused** cached memory (making it available to *other* GPU applications).
- Does **not** free memory occupied by tensors — it **cannot increase** memory available to PyTorch itself.
- Cached (unused) memory still appears as used in `nvidia-smi` — a common source of confusion.

---

## Optimizing memory usage with `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`

> Use of a caching allocator can interfere with memory checking tools such as `cuda-memcheck`. To debug memory errors using `cuda-memcheck`, set `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` in your environment to disable caching.

> The behavior of the caching allocator can be controlled via the environment variable `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` is its alias and is provided only for backward compatibility. The format is `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=<option>:<value>,<option2>:<value2>...` Available options:

### Requested options (verbatim)

**`backend`**
> `backend` allows selecting the underlying allocator implementation. Currently, valid options are `native`, which uses PyTorch's native implementation, and `cudaMallocAsync`, which uses [CUDA's built-in asynchronous allocator](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/using-cuda-stream-ordered-memory-allocator-part-1/). `cudaMallocAsync` requires CUDA 11.4 or newer. The default is `native`. `backend` applies to all devices used by the process, and can't be specified on a per-device basis.

**`max_split_size_mb`**
> `max_split_size_mb` prevents the native allocator from splitting blocks larger than this size (in MB). This can reduce fragmentation and may allow some borderline workloads to complete without running out of memory. Performance cost can range from 'zero' to 'substantial' depending on allocation patterns. Default value is unlimited, i.e. all blocks can be split. The `memory_stats()` and `memory_summary()` methods are useful for tuning. This option should be used as a last resort for a workload that is aborting due to 'out of memory' and showing a large amount of inactive split blocks. `max_split_size_mb` is only meaningful with `backend:native`. With `backend:cudaMallocAsync`, `max_split_size_mb` is ignored.

**`roundup_power2_divisions`**
> `roundup_power2_divisions` helps with rounding the requested allocation size to nearest power-2 division and making better use of the blocks. In the native CUDACachingAllocator, the sizes are rounded up in multiple of blocks size of 512, so this works fine for smaller sizes. However, this can be inefficient for large near-by allocations as each will go to different size of blocks and reuse of those blocks are minimized. This might create lots of unused blocks and will waste GPU memory capacity. This option enables the rounding of allocation size to nearest power-2 division. For example, if we need to round-up size of 1200 and if number of divisions is 4, the size 1200 lies between 1024 and 2048 and if we do 4 divisions between them, the values are 1024, 1280, 1536, and 1792. So, allocation size of 1200 will be rounded to 1280 as the nearest ceiling of power-2 division. Specify a single value to apply for all allocation sizes or specify an array of key value pairs to set power-2 division individually for each power of two interval. For example to set 1 division for all allocations under 256MB, 2 division for allocations between 256MB and 512MB, 4 divisions for allocations between 512MB and 1GB and 8 divisions for any larger allocations, set the knob value to: [256:1,512:2,1024:4,>:8]. `roundup_power2_divisions` is only meaningful with `backend:native`. With `backend:cudaMallocAsync`, `roundup_power2_divisions` is ignored.

**`garbage_collection_threshold`**
> `garbage_collection_threshold` helps actively reclaiming unused GPU memory to avoid triggering expensive sync-and-reclaim-all operation (release_cached_blocks), which can be unfavorable to latency-critical GPU applications (e.g., servers). Upon setting this threshold (e.g., 0.8), the allocator will start reclaiming GPU memory blocks if the GPU memory capacity usage exceeds the threshold (i.e., 80% of the total memory allocated to the GPU application). The algorithm prefers to free old & unused blocks first to avoid freeing blocks that are actively being reused. The threshold value should be between greater than 0.0 and less than 1.0. The default value is set at 1.0.
>
> `garbage_collection_threshold` is only meaningful with `backend:native`. With `backend:cudaMallocAsync`, `garbage_collection_threshold` is ignored.

**`expandable_segments`** (full text — long paragraph, complete in source)
> `expandable_segments` (experimental, default: `False`) If set to `True`, this setting instructs the allocator to create CUDA allocations that can later be expanded to better handle cases where a job changing allocation sizes frequently, such as having a changing batch size. Normally for large (>2MB) allocations, the allocator calls cudaMalloc to get allocations that are the same size as what the user requests. In the future, parts of these allocations can be reused for other requests if they are free. This works well when the program makes many requests of exactly the same size or of sizes that even multiples of that size. Many deep learning models follow this behavior. However, one common exception is when the batch size changes slightly from one iteration to the next, e.g. in batched inference. When the program runs initially with batch size `N`, it will make allocations appropriate for that size. If in the future, it runs at size `N - 1`, the existing allocations will still be big enough. However, if it runs at size `N + 1`, then it will have to make new allocations that are slightly larger. Not all the tensors are the same size. Some might be `(N + 1)*A` and others `(N + 1)*A*B` where `A` and `B` are some non-batch dimensions in the model. Because the allocator reuses existing allocations when they are big enough, some number of `(N + 1)*A` allocations will actually fit in the already existing `N*B*A` segments, though not perfectly. As the model runs it will partially fill up all of these segments leaving unusable free slices of memory at the end of these segments. The allocator at some point will need to `cudaMalloc` a new `(N + 1)*A*B` segment. If there is not enough memory, there is now no way to recover the slices of memory that are free at the end of existing segments. With models 50+ layers deep, this pattern might repeat 50+ times creating many slivers.
>
> `expandable_segments` allows the allocator to create a segment initially and then expand its size later when more memory is needed. Instead of making one segment per allocation, it tries to make one segment (per stream) that grows as necessary. Now when the `N + 1` case runs, the allocations will tile nicely into the one large segment until it fills up. Then more memory is requested and appended to the end of the segment. This process does not create as many slivers of unusable memory, so it is more likely to succeed at finding this memory.

### Remaining options in the section (for completeness)

- **`large_segment_size_mb`** — "the native allocator uses small and large blocks to manage allocated memory. This setting is used to configure the size of the large block. The default value is 20 MB."
- **`max_non_split_rounding_mb`** — allows non-split blocks for better reuse (e.g., a 1024MB cached block reused for a 512MB request). Default allows only up to 20MB of rounding; setting it to 1024 permits 512–1536 MB blocks to serve a 512MB request, reducing stalls from expensive `cudaMalloc` calls.
- **`pinned_use_cuda_host_register`** — boolean; use `cudaHostRegister` (with pre-mapped pages via regular malloc) instead of `cudaHostAlloc` for pinned memory, reducing lock time.
- **`pinned_num_register_threads`** — only valid when `pinned_use_cuda_host_register=True`; parallelizes page mapping. "A good value for this option is 8 based on benchmarking results."
- **`pinned_use_background_threads`** — boolean (disabled by default); enables a background thread for processing events, avoiding slow-path event queries in the fast allocation path.
- **`pinned_reserve_segment_size_mb`** — reserves a large pinned-memory segment upfront to serve small requests, reducing expensive device library calls.
- **`pinned_max_round_threshold_mb`** — max allocation size (MB) rounded up to nearest power-of-2; larger allocations use exact size (e.g., threshold 128 → a 129MB request uses 129MB, not 256MB). Disabled by default.
- **`pinned_max_cached_size_mb`** — max block size (MB) cached in the free list; larger blocks are not rounded and are freed immediately rather than cached. Disabled by default.
- **`graph_capture_record_stream_reuse`** (experimental, default `False`) — during CUDA Graph capture, reclaims device memory using graph topology instead of CUDA events to determine when a freed block is safe to reuse.
- **`per_process_memory_fraction`** — limits allocatable memory across all CUDA devices to a fraction (0–1) of available memory; exceeding it raises OOM.
- **`throw_on_cudamalloc_oom`** (default `False`) — when `True`, the allocator preemptively throws `OutOfMemoryError` instead of attempting driver allocation that could cause a fatal GPU abort. Example given:
  ```
  PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=per_process_memory_fraction:0.95,throw_on_cudamalloc_oom:True
  ```
  Described as "particularly useful for inference serving," letting a server catch the exception and reject individual requests without crashing.

### Closing note (verbatim)

> **Note:** Some stats reported by the `CUDA memory management API` are specific to `backend:native`, and are not meaningful with `backend:cudaMallocAsync`. See each function's docstring for details.

---

## Memory Statistics / Monitoring APIs Mentioned

| API | Purpose (per doc text) |
|---|---|
| `memory_allocated()` / `max_memory_allocated()` | Monitor memory occupied by tensors |
| `memory_reserved()` / `max_memory_reserved()` | Monitor total memory managed by the caching allocator |
| `empty_cache()` | Releases all **unused** cached memory (usable by other GPU apps; doesn't free tensor-occupied memory) |
| `memory_stats()` | "More comprehensive memory benchmarking" for advanced users; also cited for tuning `max_split_size_mb` |
| `memory_snapshot()` | Captures "a complete snapshot of the memory allocator state" to understand allocation patterns |
| `memory_summary()` | Mentioned (under `max_split_size_mb`) as useful for tuning |

---

## Completeness / Truncation Notes

1. **No truncation detected.** The section runs uninterrupted from the intro paragraph through the final "Note" about `backend:native`-specific stats, and the next top-level heading ("Using custom memory allocators for CUDA") begins cleanly afterward.
2. **Naming caveat:** Your request referenced `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`; the current docs treat **`PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`** as canonical and `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` as a backward-compatibility alias only.
3. **All five options you named** (`max_split_size_mb`, `expandable_segments`, `garbage_collection_threshold`, `roundup_power2_divisions`, `backend`) are present in full, including the lengthy `expandable_segments` explanation and the per-option `backend:native`-only caveats.
4. The section contains **9 additional options** beyond the ones you listed (mostly `pinned_*` options, plus `graph_capture_record_stream_reuse`, `per_process_memory_fraction`, and `throw_on_cudamalloc_oom`) — summarized above for completeness.

# torch.utils.checkpoint — Full Documentation Extraction

**Source:** PyTorch main documentation (v2.15.0 unstable) · Created On: Jun 16, 2025 | Last Updated On: Jul 27, 2026

**Summary:** The page documents activation checkpointing in PyTorch. The main API is `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint()` with two overloads (direct call and decorator form), plus `checkpoint_sequential()` for sequential models, and several supporting utilities for selective checkpointing, RNG state, and debugging. The `use_reentrant` parameter defaults to `None` in the signature but **must be passed explicitly** (an exception is planned); `use_reentrant=False` is explicitly recommended.

---

## 1. Page-Level Usage Note (RNG Handling)

> "Checkpointing is implemented by rerunning a forward-pass segment for each checkpointed segment during backward propagation. This can cause persistent states like the RNG state to be more advanced than they would without checkpointing. By default, checkpointing includes logic to juggle the RNG state such that checkpointed passes making use of RNG (through dropout for example) have deterministic output as compared to non-checkpointed passes. The logic to stash and restore RNG states can incur a moderate performance hit depending on the runtime of checkpointed operations. If deterministic output compared to non-checkpointed passes is not required, supply `preserve_rng_state=False` to `checkpoint` or `checkpoint_sequential` to omit stashing and restoring the RNG state during each checkpoint."

> "The stashing logic saves and restores the RNG state for CPU and another device type (infer the device type from Tensor arguments excluding CPU tensors by `_infer_device_type`) to the `run_fn`. If there are multiple devices, device state will only be saved for devices of a single device type, and the remaining devices will be ignored. Consequently, if any checkpointed functions involve randomness, this may result in incorrect gradients. (Note that if CUDA devices are among the devices detected, it will be prioritized; otherwise, the first device encountered will be selected.) If there are no CPU-tensors, the default device type state (default value is `cuda`, and it could be set to other device by `DefaultDeviceType`) will be saved and restored. However, the logic has no way to anticipate if the user will move Tensors to a new device within the `run_fn` itself. Therefore, if you move Tensors to a new device ("new" meaning not belonging to the set of [current device + devices of Tensor arguments]) within `run_fn`, deterministic output compared to non-checkpointed passes is never guaranteed."

### Decorator Form
> "`checkpoint` may also be called without a function to produce a decorator. This keeps checkpoint configuration separate from the keyword arguments passed to the checkpointed function:"

```python
checkpointed_fn = checkpoint(use_reentrant=False, preserve_rng_state=False)(fn)
out = checkpointed_fn(*args, **kwargs)
```

---

## 2. `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint`

### Signatures (two overloads, as documented)

```python
torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
    function: Callable[[...], _T],
    *args: Any,
    use_reentrant: bool | None = None,
    preserve_rng_state: bool = True,
    context_fn: Callable[[], Tuple[ContextManager, ContextManager]] = noop_context_fn,
    determinism_check: str = _DEFAULT_DETERMINISM_MODE,
    debug: bool = False,
    early_stop: bool = True,
    respect_saved_tensors_hooks: bool | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any
) → _T
```

```python
torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
    function: None = None,
    *,
    use_reentrant: bool | None = None,
    preserve_rng_state: bool = True,
    context_fn=noop_context_fn,
    determinism_check=_DEFAULT_DETERMINISM_MODE,
    debug=False,
    early_stop=True,
    respect_saved_tensors_hooks=None
) → Callable[[Callable[[_P], _T]], Callable[[_P], _T]]
```

*(Type annotations above were flattened from hyperlinked HTML; defaults and structure are verbatim.)*

### Description (verbatim)

> "Checkpoint a model or part of the model.
>
> Activation checkpointing is a technique that trades compute for memory. By default, tensors computed during the forward pass are kept alive until they are used in gradient computations in the backward pass. To reduce this memory usage, tensors produced in the passed `function` are not kept alive until the backward pass. Instead, any passed tensors in `args` are kept alive, and the unsaved tensors are recomputed by re-invoking `function` in the backward pass as needed for gradient computation. Activation checkpointing can be applied to any part of a model – this is sometimes described as "checkpointing" that part of the model.
>
> There are currently two checkpointing implementations available, determined by the `use_reentrant` parameter. **It is recommended that you use `use_reentrant=False`.** Please refer the note below for a discussion of their differences."

### Warnings (verbatim)

> ⚠️ "If the `function` invocation during the backward pass differs from the forward pass, e.g., due to a global variable, the checkpointed version may not be equivalent, potentially causing an error being raised or leading to silently incorrect gradients."

> ⚠️ "The `use_reentrant` parameter should be passed explicitly. In a future release, we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed. If you are using the `use_reentrant=True` variant, please refer to the note below for important considerations and potential limitations."

### Reentrant vs. Non-Reentrant Differences (verbatim bullets)

> "The reentrant variant of checkpoint (`use_reentrant=True`) and the non-reentrant variant of checkpoint (`use_reentrant=False`) differ in the following ways:
>
> - Non-reentrant checkpoint stops recomputation as soon as all needed intermediate activations have been recomputed. This feature is enabled by default, but can be disabled with `set_checkpoint_early_stop()`. Reentrant checkpoint always recomputes `function` in its entirety during the backward pass.
> - The reentrant variant does not record the autograd graph during the forward pass, as it runs with the forward pass under `torch.no_grad()`. The non-reentrant version does record the autograd graph, allowing one to perform backward on the graph within checkpointed regions.
> - The reentrant checkpoint only supports the `torch.autograd.backward()` API for the backward pass without its inputs argument, while the non-reentrant version supports all ways of performing the backward pass.
> - **At least one input and output must have `requires_grad=True` for the reentrant variant.** If this condition is unmet, the checkpointed part of the model will not have gradients. The non-reentrant version does not have this requirement.
> - The reentrant version does not consider tensors in nested structures (e.g., custom objects, lists, dicts, etc) as participating in autograd, while the non-reentrant version does.
> - The reentrant checkpoint does not support checkpointed regions with detached tensors from the computational graph, whereas the non-reentrant version does. For the reentrant variant, if the checkpointed segment contains tensors detached using `detach()` or with `torch.no_grad()`, the backward pass will raise an error. This is because `checkpoint` makes all the outputs require gradients and this causes issues when a tensor is defined to have no gradient in the model. To avoid this, detach the tensors outside of the `checkpoint` function."

### Parameters (verbatim)

- **function** – "describes what to run in the forward pass of the model or part of the model. It should also know how to handle the inputs passed as the tuple. For example, in LSTM, if user passes `(activation, hidden)`, `function` should correctly use the first input as `activation` and the second input as `hidden`. If omitted, `checkpoint` returns a decorator that can be used to wrap a function before passing user arguments."
- **args** – "tuple containing inputs to the `function`"

### Keyword Arguments (verbatim)

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **preserve_rng_state** (bool, optional) | `True` | "Omit stashing and restoring the RNG state during each checkpoint. Note that under torch.compile, this flag doesn't take effect and we always preserve RNG state." |
| **use_reentrant** (bool) | `None` (signature) | "specify whether to use the activation checkpoint variant that requires reentrant autograd. This parameter should be passed explicitly. In a future release, we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed. If `use_reentrant=False`, `checkpoint` will use an implementation that does not require reentrant autograd. This allows `checkpoint` to support additional functionality, such as working as expected with `torch.autograd.grad` and support for keyword arguments input into the checkpointed function." |
| **context_fn** (Callable, optional) | `noop_context_fn` | "A callable returning a tuple of two context managers. The function and its recomputation will be run under the first and second context managers respectively. This argument is only supported if `use_reentrant=False`." |
| **determinism_check** (str, optional) | `"default"` | "A string specifying the determinism check to perform. By default it is set to `"default"` which compares the shapes, dtypes, and devices of the recomputed tensors against those the saved tensors. To turn off this check, specify `"none"`. Currently these are the only two supported values. Please open an issue if you would like to see more determinism checks. This argument is only supported if `use_reentrant=False`, if `use_reentrant=True`, the determinism check is always disabled." |
| **debug** (bool, optional) | `False` | "If `True`, error messages will also include a trace of the operators ran during the original forward computation as well as the recomputation. This argument is only supported if `use_reentrant=False`." |
| **early_stop** (bool, optional) | `True` | "If `True`, non-reentrant checkpoint stops recomputation as soon as it has computed all needed Tensors. This argument is ignored if `use_reentrant=True`. Can be overridden globally using `set_checkpoint_early_stop()` context manager." |
| **respect_saved_tensors_hooks** (bool, optional) | `None` | "Whether tensors that selective activation checkpointing (SAC) saves are routed through the surrounding user `torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks()` (e.g. `torch.autograd.graph.save_on_cpu()`). Such tensors are held outside the autograd graph, so historically these hooks did not see them; a future release will make checkpoint honor the hooks by default. Until then the default (`None`) keeps the legacy behavior and emits a `FutureWarning` when a user hook is in scope; pass `True` to opt in or `False` to keep the legacy behavior without the warning. Has no effect without SAC (plain checkpoint recomputes rather than saves) or when `use_reentrant=True`. This argument is only supported if `use_reentrant=False`." |

### Returns

> "Output of running `function` on `*args`, or a decorator when `function` is omitted."

### Examples (verbatim code)

```python
>>> # Direct call: checkpoint the function immediately.
>>> out = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
...     fn, *args, use_reentrant=False, **kwargs
... )
>>> # Decorator/curried form: configure once, then call.
>>> checkpointed_fn = torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(
...     use_reentrant=False,
...     preserve_rng_state=False,
... )(fn)
>>> out = checkpointed_fn(*args, **kwargs)
>>> # The same decorator can be applied directly to a function or method.
>>> @torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)
... def fn(*args, **kwargs):
...     ...
>>> out = fn(*args, **kwargs)
```

---

## 3. `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint_sequential`

### Signature

```python
torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint_sequential(functions, segments, input, use_reentrant=None, **kwargs)
```

### Description (verbatim)

> "Checkpoint a sequential model to save memory.
>
> Sequential models execute a list of modules/functions in order (sequentially). Therefore, we can divide such a model in various segments and checkpoint each segment. All segments except the last will not store the intermediate activations. The inputs of each checkpointed segment will be saved for re-running the segment in the backward pass."

### Warning (verbatim)

> ⚠️ "The `use_reentrant` parameter should be passed explicitly. In a future release, we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed. If you are using the `use_reentrant=True` variant, please see `torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint` for the important considerations and limitations of this variant. It is recommended that you use `use_reentrant=False`."

### Parameters (verbatim)

- **functions** – "A `torch.nn.Sequential` or the list of modules or functions (comprising the model) to run sequentially."
- **segments** – "Number of chunks to create in the model"
- **input** – "A Tensor that is input to `functions`"
- **preserve_rng_state** (bool, optional) – "Omit stashing and restoring the RNG state during each checkpoint. Default: `True`"
- **use_reentrant** (bool) – "specify whether to use the activation checkpoint variant that requires reentrant autograd. This parameter should be passed explicitly. **In version 2.5 we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed.** If `use_reentrant=False`, `checkpoint` will use an implementation that does not require reentrant autograd. This allows `checkpoint` to support additional functionality, such as working as expected with `torch.autograd.grad` and support for keyword arguments input into the checkpointed function."

> ⚠️ **Editorial note:** This parameter text says "In version 2.5" while the warning banner above it says "In a future release" — this appears to be stale leftover wording in the v2.15.0 (unstable) docs.

### Returns

> "Output of running `functions` sequentially on `*inputs`"

### Example (verbatim)

```python
>>> model = nn.Sequential(...)
>>> input_var = checkpoint_sequential(model, chunks, input_var)
```

---

## 4. Supporting APIs on the Same Page (verbatim summaries)

| API | Key Details |
|---|---|
| `set_checkpoint_debug_enabled(enabled)` | Context manager; "sets whether checkpoint should print additional debug information when running... when set, this context manager overrides the value of `debug` passed to checkpoint. To defer to the local setting, pass `None` to this context." |
| `class CheckpointPolicy(value)` | Enum for SAC policies: `{MUST,PREFER}_SAVE`, `{MUST,PREFER}_RECOMPUTE`, `{MUST,PREFER}_CPU_OFFLOAD` (save → offload to CPU → reload to GPU in backward). "Use `MUST_*` over `PREFER_*` to indicate that the policy should not be overridden by other subsystems like torch.compile." Notes: "A policy function that always returns `PREFER_RECOMPUTE` is equivalent to vanilla checkpointing. A policy function that returns `PREFER_SAVE` every op is NOT equivalent to not using checkpointing." |
| `class SelectiveCheckpointContext(*, is_recompute, op_output=None)` | "Context passed to policy function during selective checkpointing... The policy function is only called during the forward pass. During recomputation, cached values are retrieved by index, so `is_recompute` is deprecated and always `False`." |
| `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts(policy_fn_or_list, allow_cache_entry_mutation=False)` | "Helper to avoid recomputing certain ops during activation checkpointing." Accepts a policy fn `(ctx, op, *args, **kwargs) → CheckpointPolicy` or a list of ops (equivalent to `MUST_SAVE` for listed ops, `PREFER_RECOMPUTE` otherwise). `allow_cache_entry_mutation`: "By default, an error is raised if any tensors cached by selective activation checkpoint are mutated in order to ensure correctness. If set to True, this check is disabled." Returns "A tuple of two context managers." Also recommends the separate **torch_remat** package for region-based policies. |
| `class GraphExecGroup` | "Any checkpointed regions encountered by backward under the same instance of this context manager will trigger recompute at most once, even if there are multiple calls to backward." Backward calls "must execute over non-overlapping regions of the backward graph even if retain_graph=True." "This context manager only affects checkpoint with use_reentrant=False, and is a no-op otherwise." |
| `set_checkpoint_early_stop(enable)` | "Controls whether checkpoint should stop recomputation early. By default, non-reentrant checkpoint stops recomputation as soon as it has computed all needed Tensors... This context manager only needs to be active when forward is run. It does not need to be active during backward." |
| `set_device_states(devices, states, *, device_type=None)` | "Sets random number generator states for the specified devices." `device_type` default: "the device returned by a call to `DefaultDeviceType.get_device_type()`, which is `cuda` if not changed by calling `DefaultDeviceType::set_device_type()`." |

---

## 5. Key Findings — `use_reentrant` Default & Recommendations

1. **Signature default:** `use_reentrant: bool | None = None` — but `None` is *not* a sanctioned default; the docs warn twice that "In a future release, we will raise an exception if `use_reentrant` is not passed."
2. **Official recommendation:** "It is recommended that you use `use_reentrant=False`."
3. **Requirements (reentrant variant only):** at least one input AND one output must have `requires_grad=True`, otherwise "the checkpointed part of the model will not have gradients." Non-reentrant has no such requirement.
4. **RNG handling:** enabled by default (`preserve_rng_state=True`); saves/restores CPU + one device type's RNG state (CUDA prioritized); multi-device-type randomness "may result in incorrect gradients"; moving tensors to a new device inside `run_fn` means "deterministic output... is never guaranteed"; under `torch.compile` RNG state is always preserved regardless of the flag.
5. **Feature gating:** `context_fn`, `determinism_check`, `debug`, `respect_saved_tensors_hooks`, and `GraphExecGroup` are **only supported with `use_reentrant=False`**; `early_stop` is ignored when `use_reentrant=True`.

---

## 6. Truncation / Fidelity Notes

- **No content truncation detected.** The provided capture spans the full page — from the page-level Note through `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_sequential`, all six supporting APIs (`set_checkpoint_debug_enabled`, `CheckpointPolicy`, `SelectiveCheckpointContext`, `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts`, `GraphExecGroup`, `set_checkpoint_early_stop`, `set_device_states`) — plus the page footer.
- Minor rendering artifacts normalized: hyperlinked type annotations in signatures were flattened to plain text; the `>>> deffn(...)` and `>>> importfunctools` examples were re-spaced (HTML stripped a space in the original capture).
- Source links point to `torch/utils/checkpoint.py` at commit `e1994aea` (e.g., `checkpoint` at L422, `checkpoint_sequential` at L701).
- The one inconsistency worth flagging: `checkpoint_sequential`'s parameter text still references "In version 2.5" for the `use_reentrant` exception, despite this being the v2.15.0 (unstable) page — the banner text ("In a future release") should be treated as authoritative.

# Understanding CUDA Memory Usage — Full Content Extraction

**Source**: PyTorch main documentation (v2.15.0 unstable) | Created On: Aug 23, 2023 | Last Updated On: Jul 07, 2026

This page documents PyTorch's CUDA memory snapshot tooling: recording allocation history with `_record_memory_history()`, saving snapshots with `_dump_snapshot()`, and visualizing them at `pytorch.org/memory_viz`. Below is the extracted content organized by your requested topics, with original wording preserved.

---

## 1. Overview & Visibility Limitations

> To debug CUDA memory use, PyTorch provides a way to generate memory snapshots that record the state of allocated CUDA memory at any point in time, and optionally record the history of allocation events that led up to that snapshot.
>
> The generated snapshots can then be drag and dropped onto the interactiver viewer hosted at [pytorch.org/memory_viz](https://pytorch.org/memory_viz) which can be used to explore the snapshot.

**Note (visibility scope, quoted from the page):**

> By default, the memory profiler only has visibility into CUDA device memory allocated and managed through the PyTorch allocator (e.g., `torch.empty(..., device='cuda')`, `torch.cuda.memory.CUDAPluggableAllocator`). CPU pinned memory (host memory) can optionally be included by passing `record_pinned_host_memory=True` to `_record_memory_history`.
>
> Any memory allocated directly from CUDA APIs in C++ (e.g., `cudaMalloc`, `cuMemCreate`) or via third-party Python bindings such as cuda-python will not be visible in the PyTorch memory profiler. NCCL (used for distributed communication on CUDA devices) is a common example of a library that allocates GPU memory outside of PyTorch's allocator.

---

## 2. Capturing Traces: Generating a Snapshot

> The common pattern for recording a snapshot is to enable memory history, run the code to be observed, and then save a file with a pickled snapshot:

```python
# enable memory history, which will
# add tracebacks and event history to snapshots
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()

run_your_code()
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("my_snapshot.pickle")
```

### Including Pinned (Host) Memory

> By default, memory snapshots only include CUDA device memory. To also capture CPU pinned memory allocations (e.g., tensors created with `pin_memory=True`), pass `record_pinned_host_memory=True`:

```python
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(record_pinned_host_memory=True)

run_your_code()
snapshot = torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()
# Host allocator data is in snapshot["host_segments"] and snapshot["host_traces"]
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("my_snapshot.pickle")
```

> To record only host pinned memory and skip the CUDA device allocator entirely, pair `record_pinned_host_memory=True` with `record_cuda=False`:

```python
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(record_pinned_host_memory=True, record_cuda=False)
```

**Note (visualizer limitation for host memory):**

> The pytorch.org/memory_viz visualizer does not yet support displaying host memory data. You can inspect `host_segments` and `host_traces` programmatically from the snapshot dict.

---

## 3. Using the Visualizer (pytorch.org/memory_viz)

> Open https://pytorch.org/memory_viz and drag/drop the pickled snapshot file into the visualizer. The visualizer is a javascript application that runs locally on your computer. It does not upload any snapshot data.

---

## 4. Interpreting the Active Memory Timeline

> The Active Memory Timeline shows all the live tensors over time in the snapshot on a particular GPU. Pan/Zoom over the plot to look at smaller allocations. Mouse over allocated blocks to see a stack trace for when that block was allocated, and details like its address. The detail slider can be adjusted to render fewer allocations and improve performance when there is a lot of data.

*(The page embeds an image: `_images/active_memory_timeline.png`)*

---

## 5. Interpreting Allocator State History & OOM Stack Traces

> The Allocator State History shows individual allocator events in a timeline on the left. Select an event in the timeline to see a visual summary of the allocator state at that event. This summary shows each individual segment returned from cudaMalloc and how it is split up into blocks of individual allocations or free space. Mouse over segments and blocks to see the stack trace when the memory was allocated. Mouse over events to see the stack trace when the event occurred, such as when a tensor was freed. **Out of memory errors are reported as OOM events. Looking at the state of memory during an OOM may provide insight into why an allocation failed even though reserved memory still exists.**

*(The page embeds an image: `_images/allocator_state_history.png`)*

### Address annotation format (for correlating traces)

> The stack trace information also reports the address at which an allocation occurred. The address `b7f064c000000_0` refers to the (b)lock at address 7f064c000000 which is the "_0"th time this address was allocated. This unique string can be looked up in the Active Memory Timeline and searched in the Active State History to examine the memory state when a tensor was allocated or freed.

---

## 6. Identifying Non-PyTorch Allocations

> If you suspect CUDA memory is being allocated outside of PyTorch, you can collect the raw CUDA allocation info using the pynvml package, and compare that to the allocation reported by pytorch.
>
> To collect raw memory usage outside pytorch, use `device_memory_used()`

```python
importtorch
device_idx = ...
print(torch.cuda.device_memory_used(device_idx))
```

*(⚠️ Formatting note: `importtorch` appears without a space in the source HTML extraction; the intended code is `import torch`.)*

---

## 7. Snapshot API Reference

### `torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history`

**Full signature:**

```python
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(
    enabled='all', context='all', stacks='all',
    max_entries=9223372036854775807, device=None,
    clear_history=False, compile_context=False,
    global_record_annotations=False, skip_actions=None,
    record_pinned_host_memory=False, record_cuda=True
)
```

> Enable recording of stack traces associated with memory allocations, so you can tell what allocated any piece of memory in `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()`.
>
> In addition to keeping stack traces with each current allocation and free, this will also enable recording of a history of all alloc/free events.

#### Buffer behavior (ring buffer)

> This will store up to max_entries instances of TraceEntry when enabled. Python trace collection defaults to sys.maxsize, meaning long-running or indefinitely running jobs should set a reasonable limit to avoid excessive memory use. Expect each entry to be several KB.
>
> Longer running workflows or those with smaller max_entries values will only store the last accumulated max_entries entries, meaning new entries overwrite older entries.

C++ implementation for reference to ring buffer implementation:

```cpp
if(record_history){
if(alloc_trace->size()<alloc_trace_max_entries_){
alloc_trace->emplace_back(te);
}else{
(*alloc_trace)[alloc_trace_next++]=te;
if(alloc_trace_next==alloc_trace_max_entries_){
alloc_trace_next=0;
}
}
}
```

#### Latency impact

> The Python trace collection is fast (2us per trace), so you may consider enabling this on production jobs if you anticipate ever having to debug memory issues.
>
> C++ trace collection is also fast (~50ns/frame), which for many typical programs works out to ~2us per trace, but can vary depending on stack depth.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | Literal[None, "state", "all"], optional | None, disable recording memory history. "state", keep information for currently allocated memory. "all", additionally keep a history of all alloc/free calls. Defaults to "all". |
| `context` | Literal[None, "state", "alloc", "all"], optional | None, Do not record any tracebacks. "state", Record tracebacks for currently allocated memory. "alloc", additionally keep tracebacks for alloc calls. "all", additionally keep tracebacks for free calls. Defaults to "all". |
| `stacks` | Literal["python", "all"], optional | "python", include Python, TorchScript, and inductor frames in tracebacks. "all", additionally include C++ frames. Defaults to "all". |
| `max_entries` | int, optional | Keep a maximum of max_entries alloc/free events in the recorded history recorded. |
| `clear_history` | bool, optional | Clear history when enabling, defaults to False. |
| `skip_actions` | list[str], optional | List of action types to skip when recording memory history (see below). Defaults to None (record all actions). |
| `record_pinned_host_memory` | bool, optional | If True, also record memory history for the CPU pinned memory (host) allocator. Host allocator traces will appear in the `host_segments` and `host_traces` keys of the snapshot. Defaults to False. |
| `record_cuda` | bool, optional | If True, record memory history for the CUDA device allocator. Set to False (together with `record_pinned_host_memory=True`) to record only host pinned memory. Defaults to True. |

**Valid `skip_actions` action types** (used "to reduce memory overhead by excluding certain types of events from being recorded"):

- `"alloc"`: Memory allocation events
- `"free_requested"`: Free requests (memory marked for freeing)
- `"free_completed"`: Completed free operations (memory actually freed)
- `"segment_alloc"`: Segment allocation from cudaMalloc
- `"segment_free"`: Segment freed back to CUDA via cudaFree
- `"oom"`: Out-of-memory exceptions
- `"snapshot"`: Memory snapshot generation events

> For example, to skip recording free_requested events: `skip_actions=["free_requested"]`

### `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot`

```python
torch.cuda.memory._snapshot(device=None, augment_with_fx_traces=False)
```

> Save a snapshot of CUDA memory state at the time it was called.

**Parameters:**
- **device** (*Device*) – Device to capture snapshot for. If None, captures for current device.
- **augment_with_fx_traces** – If True, augment stack trace frames with FX debug information that maps generated FX code back to original model source code. This adds fx_node_op, fx_node_name, fx_original_trace, and fx_node_info fields to Frame objects. Default: False.

**Returns:** The Snapshot dictionary object, with the following structure:

```python
class Snapshot(TypedDict):
    segments: List[Segment]
    device_traces: List[List[TraceEntry]]


class Segment(TypedDict):
    # Segments are memory returned from a cudaMalloc call.
    # The size of reserved memory is the sum of all Segments.
    # Segments are cached and reused for future allocations.
    # If the reuse is smaller than the segment, the segment
    # is split into more than one Block.
    # empty_cache() frees Segments that are entirely inactive.
    address: int
    total_size: int  #  cudaMalloc'd size of segment
    stream: int
    segment_type: Literal["small", "large"]  # 'large' (>1MB)
    segment_pool_id: Tuple[
        int, int
    ]  # id of the memory pool owning this segment
    allocated_size: int  # size of memory in use
    active_size: int  # size of memory in use or in active_awaiting_free state
    blocks: List[Block]


class Block(TypedDict):
    # A piece of memory returned from the allocator, or
    # current cached but inactive.
    size: int
    requested_size: int  # size requested during malloc, may be smaller than
    # size due to rounding
    address: int
    state: Literal[
        "active_allocated",  # used by a tensor
        "active_awaiting_free",  # waiting for another stream to finish using
        # this, then it will become free
        "inactive",
    ]  # free for reuse
    frames: List[Frame]  # stack trace from where the allocation occurred


class Frame(TypedDict):
    filename: str
    line: int
    name: str
    # Optional FX debug fields (present when augment_with_fx_traces=True
    # and the frame corresponds to FX-generated code)
    fx_node_op: str  # FX node operation type (e.g., 'call_function', 'output')
    fx_node_name: str  # FX node name (e.g., 'linear', 'relu_1')
    fx_original_trace: str  # Original model source code stack trace


class TraceEntry(TypedDict):
    # When `torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()` is enabled,
    # the snapshot will contain TraceEntry objects that record each
    # action the allocator took.
    action: Literal[
        "alloc"  # memory allocated
        "free_requested",  # the allocated received a call to free memory
        "free_completed",  # the memory that was requested to be freed is now
        # able to be used in future allocation calls
        "segment_alloc",  # the caching allocator ask cudaMalloc for more memory
        # and added it as a segment in its cache
        "segment_free",  # the caching allocator called cudaFree to return memory
        # to cuda possibly trying free up memory to
        # allocate more segments or because empty_caches was called
        "oom",  # the allocator threw an OOM exception. 'size' is
        # the requested number of bytes that did not succeed
        "snapshot",  # the allocator generated a memory snapshot
        # useful to correlate a previously taken
        # snapshot with this trace
        "annotate",  # metadata was attached to a live allocation
        # via _annotate_tensor. 'addr' is the allocation's base
        # address and 'user_metadata' holds the annotation
    ]
    addr: int  # not present for OOM
    frames: List[Frame]
    size: int
    stream: int
    user_metadata: str  # the calling thread's metadata at the time of
    # the event, as set via _set_memory_metadata (dicts appear as
    # their JSON serialization)
    internal_metadata: str  # only present when allocator internals
    # tagged the event (e.g. "mallocWithAddress" on the synthetic
    # prefix-block malloc/free pair)
    device_free: int  # only present for OOM, the amount of
    # memory cuda still reports to be free
    pool_id: Tuple[int, int]  # id of the memory pool for this entry
```

### `torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot`

```python
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot(filename='dump_snapshot.pickle', augment_with_fx_traces=False)
```

> Save a pickled version of the torch.memory._snapshot() dictionary to a file.
>
> This file can be opened by the interactive snapshot viewer at pytorch.org/memory_viz
>
> **Snapshot file sizes scale with max_entries and stack trace depth per entry, with several KB per entry. These can easily be in the GB range for longer running workflows with large max_entries.**

**Parameters:**
- **filename** (*str, optional*) – Name of the file to create. Defaults to "dump_snapshot.pickle".
- **augment_with_fx_traces** (*bool, optional*) – If True, augment the snapshot with FX debug information before dumping. This maps generated FX code stack traces back to original model source code. Defaults to False.

---

## Key Takeaways

1. **Minimal workflow**: `_record_memory_history()` → run code → `_dump_snapshot("file.pickle")` → drag/drop onto `pytorch.org/memory_viz` (runs locally, no data upload).
2. **OOM debugging**: OOM failures appear as distinct "oom" events in the Allocator State History; inspecting memory state at the OOM point can reveal why allocation failed despite existing reserved memory. TraceEntry's `device_free` field (OOM-only) records how much memory CUDA still reported free.
3. **Correlation mechanism**: Address strings like `b7f064c000000_0` uniquely identify a block allocation instance and can be searched across both visualizer views.
4. **Production viability**: Python tracing costs ~2µs/trace; C++ ~50ns/frame — cheap enough to leave enabled for future debugging.
5. **Blind spots**: Non-PyTorch allocations (raw `cudaMalloc`, NCCL, cuda-python) are invisible to the profiler; use `torch.cuda.device_memory_used()` (pynvml-based) to measure total device usage for comparison.

# PyTorch 训练 CUDA out of memory：排查与显存优化

## 一、排查步骤

### 1. 先分清"真不够"还是"碎片化"
PyTorch 使用 caching allocator：已释放但缓存的显存在 `nvidia-smi` 中仍显示占用。关键指标（[官方 CUDA semantics 文档](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/cuda.html)）：

```python
import torch
print(torch.cuda.memory_allocated() / 2**30)   # 张量实际占用
print(torch.cuda.memory_reserved() / 2**30)    # 分配器持有的总量
print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())             # 详细报告，含 inactive split blocks
```

若 `reserved` 远大于 `allocated`，且 `memory_summary()` 中有大量 **inactive split blocks**，说明是碎片化问题 → 用 `max_split_size_mb`（见下）。若 `allocated` 本身就接近卡容量 → 需要真正减少占用（梯度检查点、减 batch、AMP 等）。

### 2. 显存快照定位 OOM 现场
（[Understanding CUDA Memory Usage](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/torch_cuda_memory.html)）

```python
torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()
run_your_code()  # 跑训练，直到 OOM 附近
torch.cuda.memory._dump_snapshot("my_snapshot.pickle")
```

把 pickle 文件拖进 https://pytorch.org/memory_viz （纯本地运行，不上传数据）。OOM 会在 Allocator State History 中显示为独立 "oom" 事件，可查看 OOM 时刻的显存状态及每个块的分配堆栈。注意：NCCL、裸 `cudaMalloc` 等非 PyTorch 分配不可见，可用 `torch.cuda.device_memory_used(idx)`（基于 pynvml）对比总占用。长时间任务要设 `max_entries` 防止快照文件过大（可上 GB）。

### 3. 排除其他进程
`nvidia-smi` 确认无僵尸/其他进程占卡。

## 二、`max_split_size_mb`（治碎片化）

通过环境变量配置（官方现以 `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF` 为正名，`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` 是向后兼容别名，两者均可）：

```bash
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
```

官方语义原文：*"prevents the native allocator from splitting blocks larger than this size (in MB). This can reduce fragmentation... Default value is unlimited"*。要点：

- 仅对 `backend:native` 有意义；`backend:cudaMallocAsync` 下被忽略。
- 官方定位是 **last resort**："should be used as a last resort for a workload that is aborting due to 'out of memory' and showing a large amount of inactive split blocks"。
- 性能开销从零到显著不等，用 `memory_stats()` / `memory_summary()` 辅助调值（常见尝试 64/128/256/512）。
- 相关可选项：`expandable_segments:True`（实验性，默认 False；适合 batch size 频繁变化场景，创建可增长的 segment 减少碎片）、`garbage_collection_threshold:0.8`（默认 1.0，占用超阈值时主动回收未用块）、`roundup_power2_divisions`（大分配按 2 的幂区间取整以提高块复用）。

## 三、梯度检查点（activation checkpointing，治真不够）

以计算换显存：前向不保存中间激活，反向时重算。（[torch.utils.checkpoint 官方文档](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/checkpoint.html)）

```python
from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint

out = checkpoint(my_forward_fn, x, use_reentrant=False)
# 或装饰器形式
@checkpoint(use_reentrant=False)
def my_forward_fn(x): ...
```

要点（均为官方文档明确内容）：

- **官方推荐 `use_reentrant=False`**；该参数必须显式传入，未来版本不传将抛异常。
- `use_reentrant=True` 变体要求**至少一个输入和输出 `requires_grad=True`**，否则该部分无梯度；不支持区域内 `detach()`；嵌套结构不参与 autograd。非 reentrant 版本无这些限制，且支持 `torch.autograd.grad`、关键字参数、`context_fn`、`debug=True` 等。
- RNG：默认 `preserve_rng_state=True` 保证 dropout 等结果与不开检查点一致；不需要可设 `False` 省一点开销。多设备类型下随机性可能导致梯度不正确。
- 对 `nn.Sequential` 可用 `checkpoint_sequential(model, segments, input, use_reentrant=False)`。
- HuggingFace 模型：`model.gradient_checkpointing_enable()`（第三方常见用法，本轮未抓 HF 官方页核实）。
- 代价：反向多一次前向重算，训练变慢约 20–30%（量级为社区经验，官方文档未给出数字）。

## 四、`empty_cache`（正确使用姿势）

```python
torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```

官方原文：*"releases all **unused** cached memory from PyTorch so that those can be used by other GPU applications. However, the occupied GPU memory by tensors will not be freed so it can not increase the amount of GPU memory available for PyTorch."*

- 它**只释放未被张量占用的缓存块**，不会让你的训练能分配更多显存——**不能解决训练中的 OOM**。
- 适用场景：训练结束后/推理与训练交替时归还显存给其他进程；缓解跨进程的碎片。
- 不要放在训练循环每步调用（有同步与重新 cudaMalloc 的开销，通常反而更慢）。这是常见误区。

## 五、其他常备手段（简要）

减 batch size + 梯度累积、混合精度 `torch.amp.autocast('cuda')`、`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`、限制单进程上限 `per_process_memory_fraction:0.95,throw_on_cudamalloc_oom:True`（推理服务场景）、大模型用 ZeRO/FSDP 分片。

## 来源

- PyTorch CUDA semantics — Memory management: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/cuda.html （完整取得，含 `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF` 全部选项原文）
- Understanding CUDA Memory Usage: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/torch_cuda_memory.html （完整取得）
- torch.utils.checkpoint: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/checkpoint.html （完整取得；页内 `checkpoint_sequential` 参数说明残留 "In version 2.5" 字样与页首 "future release" 警告不一致，以页首警告为准）
- 第三方旁证（max_split_size_mb 与梯度检查点用法一致）：知乎 https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/652560340 、CSDN https://blog.csdn.net/weixin_42701915/article/details/160458699 等

## 无法核实 / 注意事项

- 所抓官方页为 main 分支（v2.15.0 unstable）文档；各配置项引入的**具体最低稳定版本号**未逐项核实（`cudaMallocAsync` 后端官方明确要求 CUDA ≥ 11.4）。`/en/stable/` 路径下 `notes/cuda.html` 与 `checkpoint.html` 返回 404，原因未确定。
- HF `gradient_checkpointing_enable()` 未查 HF 官方文档核实。
- 训练变慢 20–30% 为经验值，非官方数据。
- 所有代码未实际运行（未运行）。

仅凭已有知识，我可以这样回答：

CANN / torch_npu / 固件驱动 / PyTorch 的配套关系查询方法：

1. **官方版本配套表**：昇腾（Ascend）官方文档（hiascend.com）有「版本配套表」，通常在 CANN 软件安装指南或「版本说明」中，给出 CANN 版本 ↔ 固件/驱动（firmware/driver）版本 ↔ 支持的 PyTorch 版本的对应关系。torch_npu 的版本与 CANN 严格绑定。

2. **torch_npu 的版本规则**：torch_npu 的版本号通常形如 `x.y.z.postN` 或带 cann 后缀（如 `2.1.0.post3` 对应 PyTorch 2.1.0 和某个 CANN 版本）。其发布页（gitee.com/ascend/pytorch 或 pypi 的 torch-npu）的 release notes / README 会写明每个 torch_npu 版本要求的 CANN 版本和 PyTorch 版本。

3. **检查本地版本**：
   - 驱动：`npu-smi info` 查看驱动版本和固件版本
   - CANN：`cat /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/*/ascend_toolkit_install.info` 或 `cat /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest/version.cfg`（路径因版本而异）
   - torch：`python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__)"`
   - torch_npu：`python -c "import torch_npu; print(torch_npu.__version__)"` 或 `pip show torch_npu`
   - 报错时常见如 "CANN version mismatch"、"torch_npu xx requires torch yy" 之类，可对照配套表降级/升级相应组件。

4. **安装时用官方安装命令**：昇腾官方安装指引会让你按 CANN 版本选择 torch 与 torch_npu 的 wheel（pypi 源或 mirrors），比如 `pip install torch==2.1.0 torch-npu==2.1.0.postX`。

- 当前最新 CANN（如 8.x）与 torch_npu、PyTorch 的具体对应版本号我不确定，需要查官方配套表。

# 版本配套

TorchNPU需与特定版本的PyTorch、CANN、Python及固件与驱动配合使用。各版本间的匹配关系由昇腾社区统一维护，建议优先使用推荐版本组合以确保最佳兼容性和性能。固件与驱动的版本配套与所使用的昇腾硬件及CANN版本相关，具体选择请参考 [固件与驱动安装页面](https://www.hiascend.com/hardware/firmware-drivers/commercial)。

## 推荐版本组合

|    组件    |               推荐版本               |
|:--------:|:--------------------------------:|
| TorchNPU |              2.12.0（安装包版本）             |
| PyTorch  |              2.12.0              |
|   CANN   |              9.1.0               |
|  Python  | 3.10 / 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13 / 3.14 |

## TorchNPU 版本配套表

下表中的TorchNPU版本与`torch_npu`安装包版本采用不同的命名规则：

- **TorchNPU版本**：标识产品的发布版本，采用独立于PyTorch的版本编号，如`26.1.0`、`26.1.1`。正式版本通常使用三段数字，历史预发布版本包含`RC`标识，如`6.0.RC3`。同一个TorchNPU产品版本可以配套多个PyTorch版本，因此会发布多个不同版本号的安装包。
- **TorchNPU安装包版本**：以配套的PyTorch版本号为基础，通常采用`{PyTorch版本}`或`{PyTorch版本}.postN`的形式。`.postN`用于区分同一PyTorch版本下安装包的后续发布，`N`为发布序号，不能直接换算为TorchNPU产品版本。历史预发布安装包还可能包含`rc`标识。使用`pip`安装或查询`torch_npu`时，应使用安装包版本号。

例如，TorchNPU `26.1.0`配套PyTorch `2.7.1`时，安装包版本为`2.7.1.post8`；配套PyTorch `2.12.0`时，安装包版本为`2.12.0`。TorchNPU产品版本、安装包版本及依赖版本的对应关系以下表为准。
